styles.prompt_fragment: as black-and-white 35mm film push-processed two stops: coarse gritty grain, hard contrast with blocked shadows and blown highlights, available-light reportage, slight motion blur, tilted handheld framing, documentary immediacy of the 1960s-70s, uncropped full frame
styles.avoid: Avoid clean, smooth digital monochrome and dramatic studio lighting; the light must be available and imperfect.
styles.feasibility_note: Grain and contrast render convincingly.
styles.sensitivity_note: 'Tri-X' is a Kodak trademark. Reportage styling of real conflicts or protests can mislead, so avoid fabricating news events.
styles.short_de: Schwarzweißer Kleinbildfilm, knapp belichtet und länger entwickelt, mit grobem Korn und harter Gradation; der Available-Light-Look des Fotojournalismus der 1960er bis 1980er.
styles.short_en: Black-and-white 35mm film underexposed and over-developed, giving coarse grain and hard contrast; the available-light look of photojournalism from the 1960s to the 1980s.
markers_de: harte Gradation, zugelaufene Schatten, ausgefressene Lichter
schräger Ausschnitt aus der Hand, leichte Unschärfe
markers_en: hard contrast, blocked shadows, blown highlights
tilted handheld framing with slight blur
styles.sensitivity_de: „Tri-X“ ist eine Marke von Kodak; Reportage-Optik kann wie echte Pressefotos wirken, daher keine realen Konflikte oder Proteste nachstellen.
styles.sensitivity_en: 'Tri-X' is a Kodak trademark; reportage styling can pass for real news photos, so do not fabricate real conflicts or protests.

styles.era_origin: Graphic-arts lith films of the mid-20th century; a staple of 1960s-70s poster and record-sleeve design.
visual_markers: only pure black and pure white, no greys
styles.prompt_fragment: as a high-contrast lith-film conversion: every tone collapsed into pure black and pure white with no greys, graphic silhouettes, crisp edges with slight film grain at the transitions, posterised poster-like look, printed on white paper or shown as a black film positive
styles.avoid: Avoid vector-smooth edges and perfect digital thresholding; keep slight photographic grain at the edges.
styles.feasibility_note: Two-tone rendering is reliable.
styles.sensitivity_note: 'Kodalith' is a Kodak trademark and appears only as an alias.
styles.short_de: Reprofilm, der jeden Tonwert auf reines Schwarz oder Weiß reduziert, ganz ohne Grautöne; in den 1960ern und 1970ern viel für Plakate und Plattencover verwendet.
styles.short_en: Graphic-arts film that reduces every tone to pure black or white with no greys; widely used for posters and record sleeves in the 1960s and 1970s.
markers_de: nur Schwarz und Weiß, keine Grautöne
markers_en: pure black and white, no greys
styles.sensitivity_de: „Kodalith“ ist eine Marke von Kodak und taucht nur als Alternativname auf.
styles.sensitivity_en: 'Kodalith' is a Kodak trademark and appears only as an alias.

styles.era_origin: Developed by Kodak in the early 1940s for camouflage detection; Aerochrome III 1443 was discontinued in 2009.
visual_markers: living vegetation hot pink, magenta and crimson
styles.prompt_fragment: as a colour-infrared photograph on false-colour reversal film: all living vegetation rendered hot pink, magenta and crimson, skies deep saturated blue, water dark, skin pale and waxy, other colours shifted along the spectrum, fine grain, surreal high-contrast daylight
styles.avoid: Avoid general pink colour grading; only chlorophyll-rich elements turn pink while skies stay blue.
styles.feasibility_note: The pink-foliage logic is well learned.
styles.sensitivity_note: 'Aerochrome' is a Kodak trademark. The look is strongly associated with a living photographer's war-zone series, so do not reference or imitate it. It also has military reconnaissance origins.
styles.short_de: Falschfarben-Umkehrfilm, der lebende Pflanzen pink bis karminrot unter tiefblauem Himmel zeigt; Anfang der 1940er von Kodak zur Tarnungserkennung entwickelt, 2009 eingestellt.
styles.short_en: False-colour reversal film that renders living plants hot pink to crimson under deep blue skies; developed by Kodak in the early 1940s for camouflage detection, discontinued in 2009.
markers_de: Vegetation in Pink, Magenta und Karminrot
markers_en: vegetation hot pink, magenta and crimson
styles.sensitivity_de: „Aerochrome“ ist eine Kodak-Marke militärischen Ursprungs, und der Look ist eng mit der Kriegsserie eines lebenden Fotografen verbunden, die weder zitiert noch nachgeahmt werden soll.
styles.sensitivity_en: 'Aerochrome' is a Kodak trademark of military origin, and the look is tied to a living photographer's war-zone series, which should not be referenced or imitated.

styles.era_origin: Spread in the 2000s with digital cameras converted to infrared, using roughly 590-720 nm filters.
visual_markers: foliage white to pale gold or candy-floss pink
styles.prompt_fragment: as a converted digital infrared photograph with channel swap: foliage glowing white to pale gold or candy-floss pink, skies turned deep blue to turquoise, clouds bright and crisp, faint hotspot in the centre, smooth noiseless tones, dreamlike surreal clarity
styles.avoid: Avoid Aerochrome's magenta-red foliage; here foliage turns white-gold against blue.
styles.feasibility_note: It can drift towards Aerochrome pink; name the white-gold foliage explicitly.
styles.short_de: Aufnahme mit einer auf Infrarot umgebauten Digitalkamera, bei der Rot- und Blaukanal getauscht werden: Laub wird weiß oder golden, der Himmel türkis; verbreitet seit den 2000ern.
styles.short_en: Photograph from a digital camera converted to infrared, with red and blue channels swapped so foliage turns white or gold and skies turquoise; widespread since the 2000s.
markers_de: Laub weiß bis blassgolden oder rosa
markers_en: foliage white to pale gold or pink

styles.era_origin: The SX-70 system was launched by Polaroid in 1972; integral film has been continued by The Impossible Project (now Polaroid) since 2010.
visual_markers: square image in a thick white frame with a wider bottom strip
soft dreamy focus and muted colour
creamy highlights with greenish or bluish shadows
chemical spread marks at an edge
styles.prompt_fragment: as a 1970s-style integral instant photo: square image inside a thick white frame with a wider bottom strip, soft dreamy focus, warm creamy highlights, slightly greenish or bluish shadows, low contrast and muted colour, chemical spread marks at one edge, faint glossy surface glare
styles.avoid: Avoid crisp, saturated imagery placed inside a frame; the colour must be soft and slightly off.
styles.feasibility_note: The frame and palette are well learned.
styles.sensitivity_note: 'Polaroid' and 'SX-70' are trademarks, used as format descriptors.
styles.short_de: Quadratisches Sofortbild im weißen Rahmen mit breitem unterem Rand, weich, kontrastarm und in gedeckten Farben; das 1972 von Polaroid eingeführte Integralfilm-System.
styles.short_en: Square instant photo in a white frame with a wide bottom strip, soft and low in contrast with muted colours; the integral film system Polaroid launched in 1972.
markers_de: quadratisches Bild im breiten weißen Rahmen, unten breiter
cremige Lichter, grünliche oder bläuliche Schatten
markers_en: square image in a thick white frame, wider at the bottom
creamy highlights, greenish or bluish shadows
chemical spread marks at one edge
styles.sensitivity_de: „Polaroid“ und „SX-70“ sind Marken und dienen nur als Formatbezeichnung.
styles.sensitivity_en: 'Polaroid' and 'SX-70' are trademarks and are used only as format names.

styles.era_origin: Introduced by Fujifilm in 1998; mainstream again since the 2010s.
styles.prompt_fragment: as a small credit-card-sized instant print: vertical format with an even narrow white border, direct on-camera flash, bright punchy colour, slight cool cast, flash falloff into a darker background, glossy surface, mildly soft focus, casual party snapshot
styles.avoid: Avoid the square Polaroid frame with its wide bottom strip and pastel softness.
styles.feasibility_note: The format renders reliably.
styles.sensitivity_note: 'Instax' is a Fujifilm trademark, used as a format descriptor.
styles.short_de: Kleines Sofortbild im Hochformat, etwa kreditkartengroß, mit schmalem weißem Rand und hellen, leicht kühlen Blitzfarben; 1998 von Fujifilm eingeführt, seit den 2010ern wieder sehr beliebt.
styles.short_en: Credit-card-sized vertical instant print with a narrow white border and bright, slightly cool flash colour; introduced by Fujifilm in 1998 and popular again since the 2010s.
styles.sensitivity_de: „Instax“ ist eine Marke von Fujifilm und dient nur als Bezeichnung des Looks.
styles.sensitivity_en: 'Instax' is a Fujifilm trademark and is used only as the name of the look.

styles.name_en: Peel-apart instant print with raw border
styles.era_origin: Polaroid Type 55 positive/negative film (1961-2008); its border became a 1990s fashion and album-cover signature.
visual_markers: irregular dark chemical border with streaks and drips
notched marks from the reagent pod
styles.prompt_fragment: as a peel-apart positive/negative instant print with its raw border: sharp fine-grained black-and-white image framed by an irregular dark chemical edge with streaks, drips and notch marks from the reagent pod, slight fogging along one side, satin gelatin surface, studio test-print feel
styles.avoid: Avoid neat white instant frames; the border is messy chemistry, not plastic.
styles.feasibility_note: The border renders convincingly.
styles.sensitivity_note: 'Polaroid' and 'Type 55' are trademarks, used as format descriptors.
styles.short_de: Schwarzweißes Peel-Apart-Sofortbild mit ausgefranstem, dunklem Chemierand; entstanden auf Polaroid Type 55 (1961–2008), dessen Rand in den 1990ern zum Gestaltungsmerkmal wurde.
styles.short_en: Black-and-white peel-apart instant print framed by its ragged dark chemical border; made on Polaroid Type 55 (1961–2008), whose edge became a 1990s design signature.
markers_de: unregelmäßiger dunkler Rand mit Schlieren und Tropfen
markers_en: irregular dark border with streaks and drips
styles.sensitivity_de: „Polaroid“ und „Type 55“ sind Marken und dienen nur als Formatbezeichnung.
styles.sensitivity_en: 'Polaroid' and 'Type 55' are trademarks and are used only as format names.

styles.era_origin: A popular fine-art technique of the 1980s-90s using Polaroid peel-apart films such as Type 669.
visual_markers: mottled patchy dye pressed into rough watercolour paper
missing areas where dye did not transfer
soft fuzzy edges and muted palette
wrinkled floating emulsion with folds and tears
styles.prompt_fragment: as an instant-film image transfer onto rough watercolour paper: dye pressed from a peeled-apart negative into the fibres, mottled patchy colour, missing areas where dye did not transfer, soft fuzzy edges and faded muted palette, or a floating wrinkled emulsion lift with folds and tears, handmade art-print feel
styles.avoid: Avoid crisp instant-film borders; this is a dissolved, painterly, irregular image on paper.
styles.feasibility_note: Paper mottling works; emulsion folds are inconsistent.
styles.sensitivity_note: 'Polaroid' is a trademark, used as a process descriptor.
styles.short_de: Sofortbild, dessen Farbstoffe auf Aquarellpapier übertragen werden oder dessen Emulsion als runzelige Haut abgelöst wird; eine Kunsttechnik der 1980er und 1990er mit Polaroid-Peel-Apart-Film.
styles.short_en: Instant-film image whose dyes are pressed onto watercolour paper, or whose emulsion is floated off as a wrinkled skin; fine-art technique of the 1980s–90s using Polaroid peel-apart film.
markers_de: runzelige, abgelöste Emulsion mit Falten und Rissen
markers_en: mottled patchy dye in rough watercolour paper
missing areas where dye did not transfer
wrinkled floating emulsion with folds and tears
styles.sensitivity_de: „Polaroid“ ist eine Marke von Polaroid und dient nur als Bezeichnung des Looks.
styles.sensitivity_en: 'Polaroid' is a Polaroid trademark and is used only as the name of the look.

styles.era_origin: Box cameras like the Kodak Brownie made snapshots a mass practice; deckle-edged prints were common c. 1930s-1960s.
visual_markers: soft box-camera lens with gentle vignetting
black photo corners on an album page
styles.prompt_fragment: as a small black-and-white family snapshot from a 1940s-1950s box camera: deckle-cut wavy white border, slightly soft lens with gentle vignetting, neutral to warm grey tones, square or 6x9 format, off-centre amateur framing, mild overexposure in sunlight, mounted with black photo corners on a dark album page
styles.avoid: Avoid professional composition and studio lighting; it must look like an amateur's casual family snap.
styles.feasibility_note: The deckle border and album context render well.
styles.short_de: Kleiner Schwarzweißabzug aus der Boxkamera mit gewelltem Büttenrand, mit Fotoecken ins Album geklebt; das typische Familienfoto der 1930er bis 1960er.
styles.short_en: Small black-and-white box-camera print with a wavy deckle-cut border, fixed into an album with photo corners; the typical family snapshot of the 1930s to the 1960s.
markers_en: black photo corners on an album page

styles.era_origin: Single-use cameras were launched by Fujifilm (1986) and Kodak (1987); date-back compacts peaked in the 1990s-2000s.
styles.prompt_fragment: as a cheap 35mm disposable or point-and-shoot camera snapshot with built-in flash: harsh direct frontal flash, bright overexposed foreground, background falling into darkness, red-eye and shiny skin, hard shadow behind subjects, saturated slightly green-tinted colour negative, visible grain, orange LED date stamp in the lower right corner
styles.avoid: Avoid flattering soft light and perfect composition; the flash must be harsh and amateurish.
styles.feasibility_note: A strongly learned look; the date stamp digits are mostly legible.
styles.short_de: Schnappschuss mit hartem Frontalblitz, überstrahltem Vordergrund und dunklem Hintergrund auf körnigem Farbnegativ, typisch für Einweg- und Kompaktkameras der späten 1980er bis 2000er.
styles.short_en: Amateur snapshot with harsh built-in flash, blown-out foreground, dark background and grainy colour negative, typical of single-use and compact 35mm cameras from the late 1980s to 2000s.
markers_de: harter Frontalblitz mit Schlagschatten hinter der Person
markers_en: harsh frontal flash with hard shadow behind subjects
overexposed foreground, background falling into darkness

styles.era_origin: Diana (1960s Hong Kong) and Holga (1982 Hong Kong); celebrated by the Lomographic Society, founded in Vienna in 1992.
visual_markers: soft blurry corners with a sharper centre
square 120 frame with rough black border
styles.prompt_fragment: as a plastic toy-camera photograph on 120 film: heavy dark vignetting, soft blurry corners around a sharper centre, red-orange light leaks streaking in from the edges, oversaturated colour, square frame with a rough black border, occasional overlapping frames, lo-fi dreamy imperfection
styles.avoid: Avoid Instagram vignette presets on sharp digital images; the corners must be optically soft and the light leaks real.
styles.feasibility_note: Renders reliably.
styles.sensitivity_note: Holga, Diana, LC-A and Lomography are brand names, used here only as look descriptors in the aliases.
styles.short_de: Lo-Fi-Fotos aus billigen Plastikkameras mit starker Vignette, weichen Ecken, Light Leaks und übersättigten Farben; Kameras aus Hongkong (1960er–80er), ab 1992 von der Wiener Lomographischen Gesellschaft wiederbelebt.
styles.short_en: Lo-fi photos from cheap plastic cameras: heavy vignetting, soft corners, light leaks, oversaturated colour; Hong Kong cameras of the 1960s–80s, revived by Vienna's Lomographic Society from 1992.
markers_de: weiche, unscharfe Ecken um eine schärfere Mitte
quadratisches Format mit unregelmäßigem schwarzem Rand
markers_en: soft blurry corners around a sharper centre
square frame with rough black border
styles.sensitivity_de: Holga, Diana, LC-A und Lomography sind Markennamen; sie dienen nur als Stilbezeichnung und stehen nicht im Prompt.
styles.sensitivity_en: Holga, Diana, LC-A and Lomography are brand names; they serve only as look descriptors and are not used in the prompt.

styles.era_origin: The camera obscura principle has been known since antiquity; pinhole photography dates from the 1850s and has been revived as an art practice since the 1960s-70s.
visual_markers: uniform softness without any sharp plane
ghosting where things moved during long exposure
styles.prompt_fragment: as a pinhole camera photograph: lensless image with infinite but uniformly soft focus, no sharp edges anywhere, strong natural vignetting, wide stretched perspective, long-exposure ghosting where things moved, slightly muted tones, curved or rough frame edges
styles.avoid: Avoid selective focus with bokeh; everything is equally soft.
styles.feasibility_note: The model tends to make it either sharp or bokeh-blurred instead of uniformly soft.
styles.short_de: Linsenlose Aufnahme durch ein winziges Loch: gleichmäßig weich, stark vignettiert, bei langer Belichtung mit Geisterbildern; seit den 1850er-Jahren bekannt, ab den 1960ern künstlerisch wiederentdeckt.
styles.short_en: Lensless photographs through a tiny hole: evenly soft throughout, strongly vignetted and often ghosted by long exposures; practised since the 1850s and revived as art from the 1960s.
styles.era_en: since the 1850s; art revival from the 1960s–70s
markers_en: uniform softness with no sharp plane

styles.era_origin: A Flickr-era trend of the mid-2000s, typically photographing through the viewfinder of an old Kodak Duaflex.
visual_markers: square frame with dark rounded vignette edges
dust, hairs and scratches on the ground glass
styles.prompt_fragment: as a through-the-viewfinder photograph: image captured through the dusty ground-glass viewfinder of an old box camera, square frame with dark rounded vignette edges, specks of dust, hairs and scratches on the glass, faint Fresnel-ring texture, soft dim brightness, nostalgic haze
styles.avoid: Avoid a clean square crop; the viewfinder frame, dust and dimness must be visible.
styles.feasibility_note: The framing and dust render well.
styles.short_de: Aufnahmen durch den verstaubten Sucher einer alten Box- oder zweiäugigen Kamera, quadratisch mit dunklem Rand und Staub auf der Mattscheibe; ein Flickr-Trend der mittleren 2000er-Jahre.
styles.short_en: Photographs taken through the dusty viewfinder of an old box or twin-lens camera, with square dark-edged frame and specks on the glass; a Flickr trend of the mid-2000s.
markers_de: quadratisches Bild mit dunklen, abgerundeten Rändern
Staub, Haare und Kratzer auf dem Sucherglas
markers_en: square frame with dark rounded vignette edges
dust, hairs and scratches on the viewfinder glass

styles.era_origin: Consumer digital compacts c. 2002-2010, revived as a Gen-Z 'digicam' trend in the 2020s.
visual_markers: blown white highlights and punchy colour
JPEG artefacts with deep depth of field
orange date stamp in a 4:3 frame
styles.prompt_fragment: as a mid-2000s CCD digital compact camera photo: crisp but slightly harsh 3-5 megapixel rendering, punchy colour, blown white highlights, purple fringing on contrast edges, built-in flash glare, JPEG compression artefacts, deep depth of field, slight wide-angle distortion, 4:3 frame with an orange date stamp
styles.avoid: Avoid modern smartphone HDR and portrait-mode blur.
styles.feasibility_note: Well learned from the digicam trend.
styles.short_de: Schnappschüsse aus digitalen Kompaktkameras der 2000er: kräftige Farben, ausgefressene Lichter, violette Farbsäume, Direktblitz und JPEG-Artefakte; in den 2020ern von der Gen Z als Digicam-Look wiederentdeckt.
styles.short_en: Snapshots from early-2000s digital compacts: punchy colour, blown highlights, purple fringing, direct flash and JPEG artefacts, revived by Gen Z as the 'digicam' look in the 2020s.
markers_en: blown white highlights and punchy colour
JPEG artefacts and deep depth of field

styles.era_origin: The first camera phones appeared in Japan in 2000 (J-Phone J-SH04) and were mainstream in Europe c. 2003-2007.
visual_markers: blocky JPEG compression and smeared detail
styles.prompt_fragment: as an early-2000s camera-phone photo: VGA 640x480 resolution, blocky JPEG compression, smeared detail, colour noise in the shadows, washed-out highlights, slight greenish or magenta cast, rolling-shutter skew on movement, no depth-of-field control, awkward close framing
styles.avoid: Avoid pixel-art aesthetics; it should look like a degraded photograph, not a drawing.
styles.feasibility_note: The low resolution has to be simulated at high output resolution, and the blockiness sometimes looks too stylised.
styles.short_de: Grob aufgelöste VGA-Fotos früher Handys mit blockiger Kompression, verschmierten Details, Farbrauschen und Farbstichen; zuerst 2000 in Japan, in Europa verbreitet etwa 2003–2007.
styles.short_en: Low-resolution VGA photos from early mobile phones, with blocky compression, smeared detail, colour noise and odd casts; first sold in Japan in 2000, common in Europe 2003–2007.
markers_en: blocky JPEG compression and smeared detail

styles.era_origin: Gelatin dry plates (Richard Leach Maddox, 1871) were standard from c. 1880 to the 1920s; today they are known mostly through museum and library scans.
visual_markers: cracked glass with a break line and chipped corners
emulsion lifting and silvering-out in the shadows
handwritten catalogue number scratched into the corner
styles.prompt_fragment: as a positive scan of a damaged gelatin dry-plate glass negative, c. 1880-1920: crisp neutral black-and-white detail, cracked glass with a diagonal break line, chipped corners, emulsion lifting at the edges, bluish silver-mirroring sheen creeping in from the plate edges, handwritten catalogue number scratched into a corner, remnants of paper binding tape, archival lightbox scan
styles.avoid: Avoid a generic grain overlay and vignette; the damage must be physical glass and emulsion damage, not a scratch filter.
styles.feasibility_note: Cracks and plate edges render well.
styles.short_de: Schwarzweißer Archivscan eines Glasplattennegativs (Gelatine-Trockenplatte) mit Sprüngen, abgeplatzten Ecken und sich lösender Schicht; Trockenplatten waren von etwa 1880 bis in die 1920er Standard.
styles.short_en: Black-and-white archival scan of a gelatin dry-plate glass negative with cracks, chipped corners and lifting emulsion; dry plates were standard from c. 1880 to the 1920s.
markers_de: abhebende Schicht und Silberspiegel an den Rändern
markers_en: lifting emulsion and silver mirroring at the edges
catalogue number scratched into a corner

styles.era_origin: Colour negative films with an integral orange mask, from late-1940s Kodacolor to today's C-41 stocks.
visual_markers: film rebate with frame numbers, backlit
styles.prompt_fragment: as an unconverted colour negative: all tones and colours inverted, the image sitting on a dense orange-amber film-base mask, dark areas pale orange, bright areas deep blue-black, skin cyan-blue, film rebate with frame numbers along the edge, backlit on a light table
styles.avoid: Avoid a plain colour-inversion filter without the orange base; it must look like physical film.
styles.feasibility_note: The orange base renders well, but the inversion logic is often inconsistent.
styles.short_de: Nicht invertiertes Farbnegativ: umgekehrte Tonwerte und Komplementärfarben auf dichter Orangemaske, Filmrand mit Bildnummern, von hinten beleuchtet; Standard der maskierten Negativfilme seit den späten 1940ern.
styles.short_en: Uninverted colour negative: reversed tones and complementary colours on a dense orange mask, film edge with frame numbers, backlit; the masked negative standard since the late 1940s.
markers_en: backlit film edge with frame numbers

styles.era_origin: The standard editing tool of 20th-century photographers, iconic in 1950s-90s photojournalism and fashion.
visual_markers: rows of six small sequential frames on film strips
film edge markings and frame numbers
frames circled or crossed out in red grease pencil
styles.prompt_fragment: as a black-and-white 35mm contact sheet: strips of six small negatives printed as positives in rows, sequential near-identical frames, film edge markings and frame numbers, a few frames circled or crossed out in red grease pencil, crop marks, darker strip borders, photographic paper with slight curl
styles.avoid: Avoid neat digital grid layouts; frames must sit on film strips with edge printing.
styles.feasibility_note: Frames often vary too much or repeat exactly, and the edge text may come out garbled.
styles.short_de: Bogen mit kleinen Bildfolgen, direkt von den Negativstreifen kopiert, mit Randbeschriftung und Fettstift-Markierungen; das Auswahlwerkzeug der Fotografen im ganzen 20. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Sheet of small sequential frames printed directly from film strips, with edge markings and grease-pencil selections; the photographer's editing tool throughout the 20th century.
markers_de: Reihen mit je sechs kleinen, aufeinanderfolgenden Bildern
Bilder mit rotem Fettstift eingekreist oder durchgestrichen
markers_en: rows of six small sequential frames
film edge markings and frame numbers
frames circled or crossed out in red grease pencil

styles.era_origin: Popular with film scanning and sprocket-exposing cameras since the 2000s; the black filed-out negative-carrier border goes back to 1970s darkroom printing.
visual_markers: visible sprocket holes above and below the image
edge printing, frame numbers and arrows
styles.prompt_fragment: as a full 35mm negative scan including the film rebate: image extending across the frame with visible sprocket holes along the top and bottom, edge printing, frame numbers and small arrows in orange, slightly uneven black borders, dust specks, grain, colour negative tones
styles.avoid: Avoid a fake film-strip graphic pasted around a modern digital image.
styles.feasibility_note: The rebate renders well; brand-like edge text may come out garbled.
styles.short_de: Kleinbild-Scan samt Filmrand mit Perforationslöchern, Randbeschriftung und Bildnummern; seit den 2000ern beliebt, mit Vorläufern im schwarz gerandeten Dunkelkammerabzug.
styles.short_en: 35mm film scan including the film edge, with sprocket holes, edge printing and frame numbers; popular since the 2000s, rooted in black-bordered darkroom prints.
styles.era_de: seit den 2000ern; schwarzer Bildrand ab den 1970ern
styles.era_en: since the 2000s; black carrier border from the 1970s
markers_de: Perforationslöcher über und unter dem Bild
markers_en: sprocket holes above and below the image
edge printing, frame numbers and arrows

styles.era_origin: Mounted slides were the family and travel medium of the 1950s-1990s.
visual_markers: glowing transparency inside a white plastic or cardboard mount
handwritten date label on the mount
dust, hairs, scratches and Newton rings
styles.prompt_fragment: as a mounted 35mm colour slide photographed on a lightbox: transparency glowing inside a white plastic or cardboard mount with a handwritten date label, dust specks, hairs and fine scratches, slight Newton-ring patterns, saturated reversal colours, a faint fingerprint, top-down view with soft light-table glow around the mount
styles.avoid: Avoid a print look; the image must glow as a transparency inside its mount.
styles.feasibility_note: The mount and glow render reliably.
styles.short_de: Gerahmtes Farbdia, das auf dem Leuchttisch leuchtet, im Kunststoff- oder Papprähmchen mit handschriftlicher Beschriftung, Staub und Kratzern; Familien- und Reisemedium der 1950er bis 1990er.
styles.short_en: Colour slide glowing on a light table in a plastic or card mount with handwritten label, dust and scratches; the family and travel medium of the 1950s–1990s.
markers_de: leuchtendes Dia im weißen Kunststoff- oder Papprähmchen
markers_en: glowing transparency in a white plastic or card mount
handwritten date label on the mount
dust, hairs, scratches and Newton rings

styles.era_origin: Nitrate and acetate film decay has been documented since the early 20th century; deliberate 'film soup' experiments became popular in the 2010s.
visual_markers: bubbled and crazed emulsion with reticulation cracks
mould blooms and colour blotches spreading from edges
styles.prompt_fragment: as a damaged, decaying film negative: emulsion bubbled and crazed into reticulation cracks, channelled ripples from vinegar syndrome, mould blooms and colour blotches spreading from the edges, partially missing image areas, layered chemical stains, archival rescue scan
styles.avoid: Avoid generic grunge overlays; the damage should follow film chemistry, with blooms and cracks.
styles.feasibility_note: Damage textures render convincingly.
styles.short_de: Negativ mit blasiger, rissiger oder verschimmelter Emulsion, Farbflecken und Fehlstellen durch chemischen Zerfall; bekannt seit dem Nitratfilm, als „Film Soup“ seit den 2010ern gezielt herbeigeführt.
styles.short_en: Negative with bubbled, cracked, mouldy or channelled emulsion, colour blotches and missing areas from chemical decay; known since early nitrate film, provoked as 'film soup' since the 2010s.
styles.era_de: seit dem frühen 20. Jh.; „Film Soup“ seit den 2010ern
styles.era_en: since the early 20th century; 'film soup' since the 2010s
markers_de: Schimmelblüten und Farbflecken vom Rand her
markers_en: bubbled, crazed emulsion with reticulation cracks
mould blooms and colour blotches from the edges

styles.era_origin: Robin Hill's sky camera (1923); commercial fisheye lenses from the 1960s; a signature of 1990s skate and music videos.
visual_markers: full-frame or circular image on black
styles.prompt_fragment: as a fisheye lens photograph: extreme 180-degree barrel distortion bending straight lines into curves, edges stretched and bulging, subjects close to the lens appearing enlarged, full-frame or circular image on black, deep focus, 1990s skate and hip-hop video energy
styles.avoid: Avoid mild wide-angle; the distortion must be extreme and curvilinear.
styles.feasibility_note: Renders well; the circular variant is sometimes cropped.
styles.short_de: Extremes Weitwinkelbild, das Geraden zu Bögen krümmt, formatfüllend oder kreisrund; in den 1920ern für Himmelsaufnahmen entwickelt, typisch für Skate- und Musikvideos der 1990er.
styles.short_en: Extreme wide-angle view bending straight lines into arcs, full-frame or circular; built for sky photography in the 1920s, a staple of 1990s skate and music videos.
styles.era_de: seit den 1920ern (Wolkenkameras); im Handel ab den 1960ern
styles.era_en: since the 1920s (sky cameras); commercial from the 1960s
markers_de: formatfüllendes oder kreisrundes Bild auf Schwarz
markers_en: full-frame or circular image on black

styles.era_origin: Designed by Joseph Petzval in Vienna in 1840; reissued for modern cameras in the 2010s.
visual_markers: swirling bokeh rotating around the subject
strong field curvature and soft edges
styles.prompt_fragment: as a photograph taken with an antique Petzval portrait lens: sharp centre, swirling circular bokeh rotating around the subject, strong field curvature and soft edges, vignetting, gentle glow on highlights, intimate central composition
styles.avoid: Avoid clean round bokeh balls; the background should spiral around the centre.
styles.feasibility_note: The swirl is often rendered as generic bokeh.
styles.short_de: Porträts mit scharfer Bildmitte, wirbelndem Hintergrund-Bokeh, weichen Rändern und Vignette, aufgenommen mit dem 1840 in Wien von Joseph Petzval berechneten Porträtobjektiv; seit den 2010ern neu aufgelegt.
styles.short_en: Portraits with a sharp centre and swirling background bokeh, soft edges and vignetting, from the portrait lens Joseph Petzval designed in Vienna in 1840; reissued in the 2010s.
markers_de: Vignette und sanftes Leuchten der Lichter
markers_en: strong field curvature and soft edges

styles.era_origin: Fast portrait primes since the 1970s; smartphone portrait mode made the look ubiquitous after 2016, and it now defines the default AI photo aesthetic.
visual_markers: creamy blurred background with round bokeh balls
styles.prompt_fragment: shot on a modern full-frame camera with an 85mm f/1.2 lens wide open: razor-thin focal plane on the eyes, creamy smooth background blur with round bokeh balls, glossy clean colour, flattering soft key light, high resolution, polished commercial finish
styles.avoid: Use only as a deliberate contrast example; this is the default look to steer away from everywhere else.
styles.feasibility_note: This is the model's default.
styles.short_de: Porträtobjektiv bei Offenblende mit hauchdünner Schärfeebene und weich verschwommenem Hintergrund; seit den 1970ern verbreitet, durch den Handy-Porträtmodus allgegenwärtig und heute der Standardlook von KI-Fotos.
styles.short_en: Wide-open portrait lens with a razor-thin focal plane and smooth background blur; common since the 1970s, ubiquitous via phone portrait mode, and the default AI photo look.
markers_en: smooth background blur with round bokeh balls

styles.era_origin: The Cirkut camera was patented in 1904 for group and city panoramas; swing-lens cameras like the Widelux followed from 1959.
visual_markers: very long horizontal format of 3:1 or wider
people arranged in a long curved row
styles.prompt_fragment: as an ultra-wide panoramic photograph from a swing-lens or rotating panoramic camera: very long horizontal format around 3:1 or wider, straight lines bowing into curves at top and bottom, horizon bending, even sharpness across, people arranged in a long curved row, vintage silver-print or colour-film tones
styles.avoid: Avoid stitched digital panoramas with perfectly straight lines.
styles.feasibility_note: The elongated format works, but the characteristic curvature is inconsistent.
styles.short_de: Extrem breites Bild aus einer Kamera mit schwenkendem Objektiv oder rotierendem Gehäuse, mit gekrümmten Geraden; seit den 1840ern gebräuchlich, typisch für lange Gruppenfotos um 1900–1930.
styles.short_en: Very wide photograph from a swing-lens or rotating camera, with straight lines bowing into curves; used since the 1840s, typical of long group portraits around 1900–1930.
markers_en: very long horizontal format, 3:1 or wider
people arranged in a long curved row

styles.era_origin: Stereographic projection of spherical panoramas, popular from the mid-2000s with 360-degree photography.
visual_markers: ground wrapped into a small central sphere
horizon bent into a full circle
buildings and trees radiating like spokes
styles.prompt_fragment: as a stereographic 'little planet' projection from a 360-degree panorama: the ground wrapped into a small sphere in the centre, horizon bent into a circle, sky surrounding it as a ring, buildings and trees radiating outward like spokes, deep focus, playful distorted geometry
styles.avoid: Avoid an ordinary fisheye; the whole horizon must close into a circle.
styles.feasibility_note: The overall form works, but geometric consistency varies.
styles.short_de: Stereografisch projiziertes 360-Grad-Panorama, bei dem sich der Boden zu einer kleinen Kugel krümmt und der Himmel sie als Ring umgibt; seit Mitte der 2000er verbreitet.
styles.short_en: 360-degree panorama projected stereographically so the ground curls into a small sphere and the sky rings it; popular with spherical panorama photography since the mid-2000s.
markers_de: Boden zu kleiner Kugel in der Mitte gewölbt
Gebäude und Bäume strahlen wie Speichen aus
markers_en: ground wrapped into a small central sphere
horizon bent into a full circle
buildings and trees radiating like spokes

styles.era_origin: An optical principle described since antiquity; room-sized camera obscura photography became an art practice in the late 20th century.
visual_markers: upside-down outdoor scene projected across room surfaces
projection wrapping over walls, bed and furniture
quiet blend of interior and exterior
styles.prompt_fragment: as a camera obscura room projection: an upside-down image of the outside world projected through a small aperture onto the walls, ceiling and furniture of a darkened room, soft dim colours, projected light wrapping over objects, long-exposure stillness, quiet surreal blend of interior and exterior
styles.avoid: Avoid a plain double exposure; the outside scene must be projected upside down onto interior surfaces.
styles.feasibility_note: Inversion and projection onto surfaces are often wrong.
styles.sensitivity_note: Strongly associated with a living photographer's room projections, so do not reference or imitate specific works.
styles.short_de: Die Außenwelt fällt kopfüber durch ein kleines Loch auf Wände und Möbel eines abgedunkelten Raums; ein antikes Prinzip, seit dem späten 20. Jahrhundert als Kunstfotografie genutzt.
styles.short_en: Outside view projected upside down through a hole onto the walls and furniture of a darkened room; an ancient principle, photographed as art since the late 20th century.
styles.era_de: Prinzip seit der Antike; Kunstfotografie seit dem späten 20. Jh.
styles.era_en: principle since antiquity; art photography since the late 20th century
markers_de: Projektion legt sich über Wände, Bett und Möbel
stilles Ineinander von Innen und Außen
markers_en: upside-down outdoor scene across room surfaces
projection wrapping over walls, bed and furniture
quiet blend of interior and exterior
styles.sensitivity_de: Eng verbunden mit den Raumprojektionen eines lebenden Fotografen; keine konkreten Werke zitieren oder nachahmen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Closely linked to one living photographer's room projections, so do not reference or imitate specific works.

styles.era_origin: Cross-screen and diffusion filters were popular in late-1970s and 1980s glamour, portrait-studio and advertising photography.
visual_markers: four- or eight-point starbursts on every highlight
lifted blacks and warm pastel colour
styles.prompt_fragment: as a late-1970s to 1980s glamour photograph with a cross-screen star filter and diffusion: four- or eight-point starbursts on every highlight and light source, soft hazy glow, slightly lifted blacks, warm pastel colour, smeared soft edges, glossy magazine nostalgia
styles.avoid: Avoid modern lens flares and digital sparkles; the stars should be thin, symmetric optical spikes.
styles.feasibility_note: Renders reliably.
styles.short_de: Weiche, dunstige Aufnahmen mit vier- oder achtstrahligen Sternen auf jedem Spitzlicht, erzeugt durch Stern- und Weichzeichnerfilter in Glamour- und Werbefotos der späten 1970er und 1980er.
styles.short_en: Soft, hazy photographs with four- or eight-point starbursts on every highlight, from cross-screen and diffusion filters used in glamour and advertising of the late 1970s and 1980s.
markers_de: vier- oder achtstrahlige Sterne auf den Lichtern
markers_en: four- or eight-point starbursts on highlights
lifted blacks and warm pastel colour

styles.era_origin: Inherent to early photography; the minimalist neutral-density seascape became popular in the 2000s.
visual_markers: moving water smoothed to mist or glass
car lights as trails, people as ghosts
styles.prompt_fragment: as a long-exposure photograph on a tripod: moving elements smoothed into blur, water turned to mist or glass, clouds streaked across the sky, car lights and passers-by dissolved into trails and ghosts, static elements perfectly sharp, calm minimalist composition, twilight or neutral-density daylight
styles.avoid: Avoid HDR glow and oversaturated sunsets; keep the blur limited to moving parts.
styles.feasibility_note: Renders reliably.
styles.short_de: Belichtung über Sekunden bis Minuten vom Stativ: Wasser, Wolken und Lichter verwischen zu Nebel, Schlieren und Spuren, Unbewegtes bleibt scharf; so alt wie die Fotografie selbst.
styles.short_en: Exposure of seconds to minutes from a tripod: water, clouds and lights blur into mist, streaks and trails while static things stay sharp; as old as photography itself.
styles.era_de: seit den 1830ern; ND-Filter-Look seit den 2000ern verbreitet
styles.era_en: since the 1830s; ND-filter look popular since the 2000s
markers_de: bewegtes Wasser wird zu Nebel oder Glas
Autolichter als Spuren, Passanten als Geister
markers_en: moving water smoothed to mist or glass
car lights as trails, people as ghosts

styles.era_origin: Possible since zoom lenses spread in the 1960s; popular in 1970s-80s magazine photography.
visual_markers: radial streaks exploding from the centre
styles.prompt_fragment: as a zoom-burst photograph: the lens zoomed during a slow exposure, radial streaks exploding outward from the centre, fairly sharp core, lights becoming spokes, slightly uneven blur, dynamic tunnel effect, 1970s-80s experimental energy
styles.avoid: Avoid perfectly symmetrical digital radial blur.
styles.feasibility_note: Renders reliably.
styles.short_de: Während einer längeren Belichtung wird am Zoomring gedreht, sodass radiale Streifen aus einer recht scharfen Mitte schießen; seit den 1960ern möglich, beliebt in Magazinen der 1970er/80er.
styles.short_en: Photograph made by zooming the lens during a slow exposure, so radial streaks burst from a fairly sharp centre; possible with 1960s zoom lenses, popular in 1970s–80s magazines.
markers_en: radial streaks bursting from the centre

styles.era_origin: Photo-finish strip cameras from the late 1930s; strip and slit-scan photography as art from the 1960s; rolling-shutter distortion in phones today.
visual_markers: moving subjects stretched, compressed or warped
static background turned into uniform streaks
styles.prompt_fragment: as a slit-scan or photo-finish strip photograph: time recorded along one axis, moving subjects stretched, compressed and warped, static background turned into uniform horizontal or vertical streaks, elastic distorted bodies, sharp detail along the scan line
styles.avoid: Avoid pixel-sorting glitch effects; the distortion follows time and motion.
styles.feasibility_note: True time-axis logic is rarely reproduced; results are usually a generic stretch or glitch.
styles.short_de: Bild, das zeilenweise durch einen schmalen Spalt entsteht: Bewegtes wird gedehnt oder verzerrt, Statisches zu Streifen; Zielfotokameras seit 1937, künstlerisch genutzt seit den 1960ern.
styles.short_en: Image recorded through a narrow slit over time, so moving subjects stretch or warp and static backgrounds become streaks; photo-finish cameras since 1937, art practice since the 1960s.
styles.era_en: since 1937 (photo finish, USA); art since the 1960s
markers_de: statischer Hintergrund wird zu gleichmäßigen Streifen
markers_en: moving subjects stretched, compressed or warped
static background turned into uniform streaks

styles.era_origin: Introduced in November 2000 by Sławomir Decyk, Paweł Kula and Diego López Calvín (Solaris project); spread as a DIY pinhole practice.
visual_markers: dozens of bright arcing sun trails across the sky
warm orange-brown and teal tones from unprocessed paper
styles.prompt_fragment: as a solargraph: months-long pinhole exposure on unprocessed photo paper, dozens of bright arcing sun trails stacked across the sky, the scene below ghostly, static and soft, warm orange-brown, ochre and teal tones from scanned unprocessed paper, slight paper texture and blotches
styles.avoid: Avoid star-trail circles and sharp lens rendering; these are parallel sun arcs in pinhole softness.
styles.feasibility_note: The sun arcs render, but the palette tends to normalise.
styles.short_de: Wochen- bis monatelange Lochkamera-Belichtung auf unentwickeltem Fotopapier, die gestapelte Sonnenbögen in Orange und Petrol festhält; 2000 vom polnisch-spanischen Solaris-Projekt begründet.
styles.short_en: Pinhole exposure of weeks or months on unprocessed photo paper, recording stacked sun arcs in orange and teal; begun in 2000 by the Polish-Spanish Solaris project.
styles.era_de: seit 2000, Polen und Spanien, dann weltweit
styles.era_en: since 2000, Poland and Spain, then worldwide
markers_de: warme Orangebraun- und Petroltöne des unentwickelten Papiers
markers_en: dozens of bright arcing sun trails
warm orange-brown and teal tones of unprocessed paper

styles.era_origin: Popularised by tone-mapping software and Flickr photo groups c. 2005-2012.
styles.prompt_fragment: as a late-2000s HDR tone-mapped photograph: bracketed exposures merged with extreme local contrast, glowing halos around edges, every shadow opened up, gritty over-detailed textures, oversaturated colour, dramatic clouds, slightly grey-washed midtones
styles.avoid: Use only as a deliberate period look; do not confuse it with the subtle HDR of modern phones.
styles.feasibility_note: Renders reliably.
styles.short_de: Belichtungsreihen, mit extremem lokalem Kontrast verrechnet: Lichthöfe an Kanten, aufgehellte Schatten, überzeichnete Details und übersättigte Farben; der Flickr-Look von etwa 2005 bis 2012.
styles.short_en: Bracketed exposures merged with extreme local contrast, giving glowing edge halos, opened shadows, gritty detail and oversaturated colour; the Flickr look of about 2005–2012.

styles.era_origin: Wheatstone's stereoscope (1838) and Brewster's lens viewer (1849); mass-produced stereoviews were a parlour staple c. 1855-1930.
visual_markers: two nearly identical side-by-side photographs with slight parallax
arched tops on a curved buff or orange card
sepia tones and printed caption strip
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Victorian stereograph card: two nearly identical side-by-side photographs from slightly different viewpoints, arched tops, mounted on a curved buff or orange card, sepia albumen tones, faded edges, printed publisher caption strip along the bottom, foxing and corner wear, deep perspective with layered foreground and background
styles.avoid: Avoid two unrelated images or a modern split screen; both halves must show the same scene with only a slight offset.
styles.feasibility_note: The side-by-side layout works, but the parallax between the halves is often missing or the two halves differ too much.
styles.short_de: Zwei fast gleiche Fotos nebeneinander auf gewölbtem Karton, gedacht für das Stereoskop; massenhaft verbreitete Wohnzimmerunterhaltung von etwa 1855 bis 1930.
styles.short_en: Two nearly identical photographs side by side on a curved card, made for a stereoscope; mass-produced household entertainment c. 1855–1930.
markers_de: zwei fast gleiche Fotos nebeneinander mit leichter Parallaxe
oben abgerundete Bilder auf gewölbtem beigem oder orangem Karton
markers_en: two near-identical side-by-side photos with slight parallax
arched tops on a curved buff or orange card
sepia tones and printed caption strip

styles.era_origin: Principle by Wilhelm Rollmann (1853), patented for printing by Louis Ducos du Hauron (1891); boomed with 1950s 3D comics and films.
visual_markers: red channel offset one way, cyan the other
fringing vanishing at the depth plane
styles.prompt_fragment: as a red-cyan anaglyph 3D image: the scene doubled with a red channel offset left and a cyan channel offset right, colour fringes strongest on foreground edges and vanishing at the depth plane, slightly desaturated overall, 1950s 3D-comic and stereo-photo feel, made for red-blue glasses
styles.avoid: Avoid a uniform RGB-split glitch; the offset must follow depth, not be a flat chromatic-aberration filter.
styles.feasibility_note: The fringing appears, but depth-consistent offsets are only approximate.
styles.short_de: Stereobild aus versetzten roten und cyanfarbenen Auszügen, deren Farbsäume mit der Tiefe zunehmen, betrachtet mit Rot-Cyan-Brille; Prinzip von 1853, Boom mit 3D-Comics und -Filmen der 1950er.
styles.short_en: Stereo image printed as offset red and cyan layers whose fringes grow with depth, viewed through red-blue glasses; principle from 1853, popular in 1950s 3D comics and films.
styles.era_de: seit 1853, Deutschland und Frankreich; Boom in den 1950ern, USA
styles.era_en: since 1853, Germany and France; boom in the 1950s, USA
markers_de: roter und cyanfarbener Kanal gegeneinander versetzt
markers_en: red and cyan channels offset in opposite directions
fringing vanishing at the depth plane

styles.era_origin: Photographic lantern slides from 1850 (Langenheim brothers); hand-coloured slides were standard for lectures and entertainment until the 1930s.
visual_markers: transparent photographic positive on square glass
translucent watercolour tints bleeding over edges
round or arched black paper mask
black binding tape and handwritten label
styles.prompt_fragment: as a hand-coloured glass magic lantern slide: transparent photographic positive on a square glass plate, translucent watercolour tints in soft rose, ochre and turquoise bleeding slightly over the edges, round or arched black paper mask, black binding tape around the glass, handwritten paper label, backlit glow, fine dust and hairline cracks
styles.avoid: Avoid modern saturated colour and a paper-print look; it must be backlit glass with mask and tape.
styles.feasibility_note: The mask and tape render reliably.
styles.sensitivity_note: Many historic lantern slides carried racist or colonial caricatures, so avoid reproducing such content.
styles.short_de: Handkoloriertes Fotopositiv auf quadratischem Glas mit schwarzer Papiermaske und Klebeband, gedacht zur Projektion; ab 1850 für Vorträge und Vorführungen bis in die 1930er hergestellt.
styles.short_en: Hand-tinted photographic positive on square glass with black paper mask and binding tape, made for projection; produced from 1850 for lectures and shows until the 1930s.
markers_de: lasierende Aquarelltöne, leicht über die Konturen verlaufend
markers_en: transparent photo positive on square glass
translucent watercolour tints bleeding over edges
round or arched black paper mask
black binding tape and handwritten label
styles.sensitivity_de: Viele historische Glasdias zeigten rassistische oder koloniale Karikaturen; solche Inhalte nicht nachbilden.
styles.sensitivity_en: Many historic lantern slides carried racist or colonial caricatures; do not reproduce such content.

styles.era_origin: Developed from Fox Talbot's 1850s experiments and perfected by Karl Klíč in Vienna in 1879; the medium of fine photographic journals around 1900-1917.
visual_markers: image printed in ink on soft deckle-edged rag paper
fine aquatint grain instead of halftone dots
embossed plate mark with wide margin
styles.prompt_fragment: as a photogravure: photograph printed in ink from an etched copper plate onto soft deckle-edged rag paper, fine aquatint grain instead of halftone dots, rich warm-black or brown-black ink, velvety shadows, embossed plate mark around the image within a wide margin, faint plate tone, slight ink sheen

styles.sensitivity_en: Classic subjects were celebrities, so do not depict real people; treat the Mexican souvenir-art connotation with respect.

styles.era_origin: Developed in the English watercolour school of the 18th-19th century and central to modern loose watercolor.
styles.prompt_fragment: wet-in-wet watercolor on cold-press cotton paper, pigments bleeding into damp paper with soft feathered edges, cauliflower blooms and backruns, granulating blues and earth tones settling into the paper tooth, untouched white paper as highlights, dried tide-line edges, a few accidental drips and splashes
styles.avoid: Avoid the clean digital watercolor brush with uniform gradients and black outlines; it should feel uncontrolled and physical.
styles.feasibility_note: Blooms render well; the model sometimes adds ink outlines nobody asked for.
styles.short_de: Aquarellfarbe auf feuchtem Papier, die weich und ausfransend verläuft, mit Blumenkohl-Effekten und ausgespartem Papierweiß; entwickelt in der englischen Aquarellmalerei des 18. und 19. Jahrhunderts.
styles.short_en: Watercolour laid into damp paper, pigments bleeding into soft feathered edges, blooms and backruns, white paper left for light; developed in 18th–19th-century England.
styles.era_de: seit dem 18./19. Jh., England; prägend für das moderne freie Aquarell
styles.era_en: since the 18th–19th century, England; central to modern loose watercolour

styles.era_origin: Classical British topographical and architectural watercolour of the 18th-19th century.
visual_markers: crisp hard edges of dried washes
styles.prompt_fragment: transparent watercolor built in successive wet-on-dry glazes, each dried wash leaving a crisp hard edge, overlapping translucent layers deepening color where they cross, faint graphite underdrawing still visible, precisely reserved whites, hot-press paper with subtle tooth, calm restrained palette
styles.avoid: Avoid soft blooms (that is wet-in-wet) and opaque gouache-like coverage.
styles.feasibility_note: Hard-edged layering holds; can drift into wet-in-wet softness.
styles.short_de: Transparentes Aquarell aus nacheinander auf trockenes Papier gelegten Lasuren, jede mit scharfer Kante, über sichtbarer Bleistiftvorzeichnung; britische Topografie- und Architekturaquarelle des 18. und 19. Jahrhunderts.
styles.short_en: Transparent watercolour built in successive washes on dry paper, each leaving a crisp edge, over visible pencil underdrawing; British topographical and architectural watercolour, 18th–19th century.
markers_en: crisp hard edges of dried washes

styles.era_origin: Refined in mid-20th-century American realist watercolor and tempera; related to the 'flying white' of East Asian ink painting.
visual_markers: scratchy broken strokes over paper tooth
styles.prompt_fragment: dry-brush technique, a nearly dry brush dragged across rough paper so pigment catches only on the tooth, scratchy broken strokes with sparkling white gaps, split-hair striations rendering fur, wood grain and grass, muted palette of umber, ochre and gray-green, sparse quiet composition
styles.avoid: Avoid smooth washes and saturated color; avoid drifting into generic watercolor.
styles.feasibility_note: Broken-stroke texture holds at large scale but gets smoothed in small details.
styles.sensitivity_note: Do not name specific 20th-century realist painters known for this technique.
styles.short_de: Fast trockener Pinsel, über raues Papier gezogen, sodass die Farbe nur auf den Erhebungen haftet: kratzige, gebrochene Striche mit hellen Lücken; verfeinert im amerikanischen Realismus um 1950.
styles.short_en: Nearly dry brush dragged over rough paper so pigment catches only on the tooth, leaving scratchy broken strokes and sparkling white gaps; refined in mid-20th-century American realism.
styles.era_de: Mitte 20. Jh., USA; verwandt mit dem ostasiatischen „fliegenden Weiß“
styles.era_en: mid-20th century, USA; related to East Asian 'flying white'
markers_de: kratzige, gebrochene Striche auf der Papierstruktur
markers_en: scratchy broken strokes over the paper tooth
styles.sensitivity_de: Keine bestimmten Realisten des 20. Jahrhunderts nennen, die für diese Technik bekannt sind.
styles.sensitivity_en: Do not name specific 20th-century realist painters known for the technique.

styles.era_origin: Used since medieval manuscript painting; the dominant medium of mid-20th-century commercial and editorial illustration.
styles.prompt_fragment: opaque gouache painting on heavy paper, flat velvety matte color shapes with a slightly chalky finish, light colors laid confidently over dark, visible brush-edge ridges and occasional streaks where paint thinned, limited harmonious palette, crisp overlapping shapes, small paper-white gaps between areas
styles.avoid: Avoid vector flatness and digital gradients; the paint must show streaks, chalkiness and hand-cut edges.
styles.feasibility_note: Renders convincingly; risk of sliding into clean vector flats.
styles.short_de: Deckende Wasserfarbe in flachen, samtig matten Formen mit leicht kreidigem Auftrag, hell über dunkel gemalt; seit der Buchmalerei des Mittelalters, prägend für die Illustration der 1940er bis 1960er.
styles.short_en: Opaque watercolour in flat, velvety matte shapes with a slightly chalky finish, light painted over dark; used since medieval manuscripts, dominant in mid-20th-century illustration.
styles.era_de: seit dem Mittelalter; Blüte in der Gebrauchsillustration Mitte des 20. Jh.
styles.era_en: since the Middle Ages; peak in mid-20th-century commercial illustration

styles.name_en: Pen and wash (ink and wash drawing)
styles.era_origin: Old Master preparatory drawings of the 16th-18th century in iron-gall, bistre or sepia ink with brushed washes.
visual_markers: monochrome brushed washes of the same ink
styles.prompt_fragment: pen and brown ink drawing with brushed wash, quick nervous quill lines in iron-gall and bistre ink, transparent monochrome washes of diluted ink describing light and shadow, warm laid paper with visible chain lines, foxing spots and faded ink haloes, loose old-master study character
styles.avoid: Avoid modern clean fineliner lines and added color; keep it monochrome brown and aged.
styles.feasibility_note: Aged paper and wash render reliably.
styles.short_de: Rasche Federzeichnung in brauner Eisengallus- oder Bistertinte, mit dem Pinsel in derselben Tinte laviert, auf geripptem Papier; altmeisterliche Studienblätter des 16. bis 18. Jahrhunderts.
styles.short_en: Quick brown quill drawing in iron-gall or bistre ink with brushed washes of the same ink on laid paper; Old Master study drawings of the 16th–18th century.
markers_en: monochrome washes of the same ink

styles.era_origin: Long tradition of travel sketching, named as a global movement with the Urban Sketchers community founded in 2007-2008.
visual_markers: fineliner lines over loose watercolor washes
styles.prompt_fragment: urban sketching sketchbook spread drawn on location, wobbly confident fineliner ink lines with loose perspective, quick transparent watercolor washes splashed partly outside the lines, the book's center gutter visible, short handwritten date and place note in a corner, paper left white in the sky, a faint coffee-ring stain
styles.avoid: Avoid perfect architectural accuracy and full-bleed coloring; it should feel drawn in half an hour standing on the street.
styles.feasibility_note: Looks convincing; handwritten notes can become gibberish, so keep them short.
styles.short_de: Vor Ort gezeichnete Skizzenbuchseite: Fineliner-Linien, locker darübergelegte Aquarellflächen, die über die Konturen hinauslaufen, Bundsteg und handschriftliche Notizen; als weltweite Bewegung seit 2007.
styles.short_en: On-location sketchbook drawing in fineliner with loose watercolour washes spilling past the lines, visible gutter and handwritten notes; named as a global movement in 2007.
styles.era_en: since 2007, worldwide; rooted in older travel sketching
markers_de: Farbe läuft über die Linien hinaus
markers_en: fineliner lines over loose watercolour washes

styles.era_origin: Hobby and fine-art medium popularised from the 2000s on non-porous synthetic paper.
styles.prompt_fragment: alcohol ink painting on non-porous synthetic paper, vivid translucent dyes flowing into organic veils, dark ring-shaped dried edges and petal-like blooms, colors pushed by air into feathered lacy edges, occasional metallic gold, glossy surface with tiny bubbles, forms simplified and emerging from the flow
styles.avoid: Avoid watercolor paper texture and opaque paint; alcohol ink is transparent, ringed and glassy.
styles.feasibility_note: Figurative forms dissolve; works best with simple subjects.
styles.short_de: Leuchtende, durchscheinende Farbstoffe, die auf nicht saugendem Kunststoffpapier zu Schleiern mit dunklen Ringrändern, blütenartigen Formen und Goldakzenten verlaufen; Hobby- und Kunsttechnik seit den 2000ern.
styles.short_en: Vivid translucent dyes flowing on non-porous synthetic paper into veils with dark ring-shaped edges, petal-like blooms and gold accents; hobby and art medium since the 2000s.

styles.era_origin: Main panel-painting medium of medieval and early Renaissance Europe (13th-15th century), revived by 20th-century realists.
visual_markers: burnished gold-leaf ground with punched tooling
styles.prompt_fragment: egg tempera on gessoed wooden panel, forms built from thousands of fine parallel hatched brushstrokes, matte satin finish, clear bright unblended colors, greenish underpainting showing in the shadows of flesh, burnished gold-leaf background with punched tooling, small age cracks and worn panel edges
styles.avoid: Avoid oil-paint softness and glossy blends; tempera is crisp, hatched and matte.
styles.feasibility_note: Gold ground works well; fine hatching is often smoothed into blends.
styles.sensitivity_note: Gold-ground panels evoke Christian and Orthodox icons; avoid sacred conventions (halos, saints' attributes) on trivial or commercial motifs.
styles.short_de: Tafelmalerei mit eigebundenen Pigmenten aus feinen parallelen Schraffurstrichen, matt und klar, oft vor poliertem Goldgrund; wichtigste Maltechnik Europas im 13. bis 15. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Panel painting in egg-bound pigment built from fine parallel hatched strokes, matte and clear, often on burnished gold ground; Europe's main panel medium in the 13th–15th century.
styles.era_en: 13th–15th century, Europe; revived in the 20th century
markers_en: burnished gold ground with punched tooling
styles.sensitivity_de: Goldgrundtafeln erinnern an christliche und orthodoxe Ikonen; Heiligenscheine und Heiligenattribute nicht auf banale oder kommerzielle Motive übertragen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Gold-ground panels evoke Christian and Orthodox icons; avoid sacred conventions such as halos or saints' attributes on trivial or commercial motifs.

styles.era_origin: From Minoan and Roman wall painting through the Italian Renaissance; revived in 1920s-30s Mexican muralism.
styles.prompt_fragment: true fresco painted into wet lime plaster, chalky matte pigments in earth ochres, terre verte and faded azure, slightly uneven wall surface with visible day-work seams, flaked and lost patches revealing bare plaster, salt bloom, painted decorative border, soft diffused interior light on the wall
styles.avoid: Avoid glossy canvas surfaces and saturated digital color.
styles.feasibility_note: Plaster texture and fading render reliably.
styles.sensitivity_note: Many fresco cycles are devotional; avoid parodying sacred imagery.
styles.short_de: In den feuchten Kalkputz gemalte Pigmente: kreidig matte Erdfarben, sichtbare Tagwerke, abgeplatzte Stellen; von minoischen und römischen Wänden über die italienische Renaissance bis zum mexikanischen Muralismus.
styles.short_en: Pigments painted into wet lime plaster: chalky matte earth colours, day-work seams, flaked losses; from Minoan and Roman walls to the Italian Renaissance and Mexican muralism.
styles.era_de: seit der Bronzezeit (minoisch); Blüte in der italienischen Renaissance; Wiederbelebung in Mexiko 1920er–30er
styles.era_en: since the Bronze Age (Minoan); peak in the Italian Renaissance; revived in 1920s–30s Mexico
styles.sensitivity_de: Viele Freskenzyklen sind religiös; sakrale Bildmotive nicht parodieren.
styles.sensitivity_en: Many fresco cycles are devotional; do not parody sacred imagery.

styles.era_origin: Ancient Greek and Roman-Egyptian practice (Fayum funerary portraits), revived in 20th-century American and contemporary art.
styles.prompt_fragment: encaustic painting in pigmented hot beeswax on wooden panel, translucent milky layers with color suspended in depth, heat-fused ridges and soft melted edges, incised and scraped lines revealing underlayers, waxy satin sheen, embedded paper fragments, uneven drips at the panel edge
styles.avoid: Avoid flat matte surfaces and oil-like strokes; the wax depth and translucency are essential.
styles.feasibility_note: Waxy surface works; translucency in depth is approximate.
styles.sensitivity_note: Fayum-type mummy portraits are funerary artifacts; reference them respectfully, if at all.
styles.short_de: Pigmentiertes heißes Bienenwachs in milchig durchscheinenden Schichten, mit geschmolzenen Graten und eingeritzten Linien; antike griechische und römisch-ägyptische Technik, im 20. Jahrhundert in den USA wiederbelebt.
styles.short_en: Pigmented hot beeswax fused in translucent, milky layers with melted ridges and incised lines; ancient Greek and Roman-Egyptian practice, revived in 20th-century American art.
styles.era_de: Antike (Griechenland, römisches Ägypten); Wiederbelebung im 20. Jh., USA
styles.era_en: antiquity (Greece, Roman Egypt); revived in the 20th century, USA
markers_de: Farbe, die in der Tiefe schwebt
styles.sensitivity_de: Fayum-Mumienporträts sind Grabbeigaben; wenn überhaupt, nur mit Respekt darauf Bezug nehmen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Fayum mummy portraits are funerary objects; reference them respectfully, if at all.

styles.era_origin: Medieval origins; a major Central European folk art in the 18th-19th century (Bavaria, Bohemia, Silesia), later taken up by early-20th-century German avant-garde painters.
styles.prompt_fragment: reverse glass painting, image painted on the back of a glass pane and viewed through it: bold black contour lines, flat brilliant enamel colors filled in behind, glossy reflections and slight glare across the surface, patches of metallic foil shimmering behind the glass, naive folk simplification, simple painted wooden frame
styles.avoid: Avoid realistic shading and depth; the image is flat, outlined and seen through glass.
styles.feasibility_note: Glass glare and outlines work; foil and the painted-from-behind logic are approximate.
styles.sensitivity_note: Traditional Hinterglas images are often devotional; keep motifs secular unless that is intended.
styles.short_de: Auf die Rückseite einer Glasscheibe gemalt, erst die Konturen, dann flächige leuchtende Farben und Metallfolie, durch das glänzende Glas betrachtet; mitteleuropäische Volkskunst des 18. und 19. Jahrhunderts.
styles.short_en: Painted on the back of glass, contours first, then flat bright colour and foil, seen through the glossy pane; Central European folk art, 18th–19th century.
styles.era_de: Ursprünge im Mittelalter; Blüte im 18.–19. Jh., Mitteleuropa (Bayern, Böhmen, Schlesien)
styles.era_en: medieval origins; peak in the 18th–19th century, Central Europe (Bavaria, Bohemia, Silesia)
styles.sensitivity_de: Traditionelle Hinterglasbilder sind oft Andachtsbilder; Motive weltlich halten, sofern nichts anderes gewollt ist.
styles.sensitivity_en: Traditional reverse-glass images are often devotional; keep motifs secular unless that is intended.

styles.era_origin: Italian Renaissance façade decoration, widespread in 16th-century Central European architecture and revived in 1950s public art.
styles.prompt_fragment: sgraffito wall decoration, image scratched through a thin light lime-plaster layer to reveal a dark gray or terracotta layer beneath, two-tone graphic linework with slightly crumbly raised edges, hatching made of scratched grooves, coarse plaster grain, weathered façade with hairline cracks and patina
styles.avoid: Avoid painted shading and gradients; it is strictly two-level scratched relief, not a woodcut.
styles.feasibility_note: The two-tone scratch reads well but can be confused with engraving or woodcut.
styles.short_de: Fassadenschmuck, bei dem eine helle Putzschicht bis auf eine dunkle Unterschicht weggekratzt wird, zweifarbig und grafisch; italienische Renaissance, Mitteleuropa im 16. Jahrhundert, Kunst am Bau der 1950er.
styles.short_en: Wall decoration scratched through light top plaster to a dark layer beneath, in two-tone lines; Italian Renaissance façades, 16th-century Central Europe, revived in 1950s public art.
styles.era_de: 15.–16. Jh., Italien und Mitteleuropa; Wiederbelebung in den 1950ern
styles.era_en: 15th–16th century, Italy and Central Europe; revived in the 1950s

styles.era_origin: Pen drawing modeled on engraving from the 15th century, peaking in Victorian and early-20th-century book and newspaper illustration.
visual_markers: tone built only from layered hatching
styles.prompt_fragment: dip-pen and India ink drawing, all tone built from layered crosshatching in two to four directions, flexible steel nib giving swelling and tapering line weight, dense black cores in the shadows, white paper as light, tiny ink spatters and blots, slightly bleeding lines on bright Bristol board
styles.avoid: Avoid gray washes, uniform digital line weight and added color.
styles.feasibility_note: Hatching renders well at medium density; very dense areas can turn into gray noise.
styles.short_de: Zeichnung mit Spitzfeder und Tusche, bei der alle Tonwerte aus übereinandergelegten Schraffuren entstehen, mit an- und abschwellenden Linien; Blüte in der Buchillustration des 19. und frühen 20. Jahrhunderts.
styles.short_en: Dip-pen and India ink drawing where all tone comes from layered hatching in several directions, with swelling nib lines; peaking in 19th- and early-20th-century book and newspaper illustration.
styles.era_de: seit dem 15. Jh.; Blüte im 19. und frühen 20. Jh., Europa und USA
styles.era_en: since the 15th century; peak in the 19th and early 20th century, Europe and USA
markers_en: tone built only from layered hatching

styles.era_origin: Stipple engraving of the 18th century and scientific illustration of the 19th-20th century; still standard in natural-history drawing.
visual_markers: density gradients from dense to sparse
styles.prompt_fragment: stippling in black technical-pen ink, every tone made solely from thousands of tiny hand-placed dots, dense clusters in shadows thinning to sparse scatter in highlights, no contour lines or hatching, irregular dot spacing, crisp scientific-illustration clarity on smooth white paper
styles.avoid: Avoid regular halftone dot grids (that is printing) and any hatching lines.
styles.feasibility_note: The model often mixes in lines or regular halftone patterns; dot-only discipline breaks down over large areas.
styles.short_de: Zeichnung, deren Tonwerte allein aus winzigen, von Hand gesetzten Tuschepunkten entstehen, dicht im Schatten, locker im Licht; seit dem 19. Jahrhundert Standard der wissenschaftlichen Illustration.
styles.short_en: Drawing in which every tone is made only from tiny hand-placed ink dots, dense in shadow and sparse in light; standard in scientific illustration since the 19th century.
styles.era_de: seit dem 18. Jh. (Punktierstich); Standard der wissenschaftlichen Illustration seit dem 19. Jh.
styles.era_en: since the 18th century (stipple engraving); standard in scientific illustration since the 19th century
markers_en: density gradients from dense to sparse

styles.era_origin: Technical pens from the 1950s and fibre-tip fineliners from the 1970s became standard in design, architecture and illustration.
styles.prompt_fragment: fineliner pen drawing with uniform 0.3 mm black lines, clean confident contours and sparse parallel hatching only where needed, no fills, generous white space, slight human wobble and occasional overshoot at line ends, plain cartridge paper
styles.avoid: Avoid vector-perfect lines and coloring-book outlines; keep the human wobble and overshoots.
styles.feasibility_note: Clean linework holds well; it can become too vector-perfect.
styles.short_de: Zeichnung aus dünnen, gleichmäßig starken schwarzen Linien mit Tuschefüller oder Fineliner, seit Mitte des 20. Jahrhunderts verbreitet in Design, Architektur und Illustration.
styles.short_en: Drawing in thin, even black lines made with a technical pen or fineliner, typical of design, architecture and illustration since the mid-20th century.
markers_en: no fills, lots of white space

styles.era_origin: Ballpoint pens were mass-marketed from the late 1940s; ballpoint drawing grew into a recognised fine-art medium from the 1960s.
visual_markers: blue ink tones from layered scribble
styles.prompt_fragment: blue ballpoint pen drawing, tones built from layered scribbled hatching and tiny loops, the darkest areas glossy with a slight ink sheen, occasional ink blobs at stroke ends, faint grooves pressed into the paper, uneven pressure, plain office paper
styles.avoid: Avoid a grayscale pencil look; the blue ink sheen and blobs are essential.
styles.feasibility_note: Blue ink texture renders convincingly.
styles.short_de: Zeichnung mit blauem Kugelschreiber, Tonwerte aus übereinandergelegten Kritzelschraffuren, glänzende Tiefen und Tintenkleckse; von Künstlern seit den 1950er-Jahren genutzt.
styles.short_en: Drawing in blue ballpoint ink with tones built from layered scribbled hatching, glossy darks and ink blobs; used by artists since the 1950s.
markers_en: blue ink tones from layered scribbles
glossy ink sheen in the darks

styles.era_origin: Timeless school and office habit, recognised as a visual genre throughout 20th-century notebook culture.
visual_markers: lined school paper with red margin
styles.prompt_fragment: absent-minded doodles on a page of lined school notebook paper, blue ballpoint and pencil mixed, red margin line and spiral binding holes visible, wobbly naive forms filled with repetitive patterns, shading by over-scribbling, eraser smudges, crossed-out marks, slightly creased paper
styles.avoid: Avoid polished illustration skill; keep it amateur and spontaneous.
styles.feasibility_note: Paper context renders well; scribbled words become gibberish.
styles.short_de: Gedankenverlorene Kritzeleien mit Kugelschreiber und Bleistift auf liniertem Schulheftpapier, mit Musterfüllungen, Radierspuren und rotem Rand – eine Alltagsgewohnheit des 20. Jahrhunderts.
styles.short_en: Absent-minded doodles in ballpoint and pencil on lined school-notebook paper, with pattern fills, smudges and a red margin line; an everyday 20th-century habit.
markers_en: lined paper with red margin line

styles.era_origin: Western brush inking of 19th-20th-century illustration and newspaper strips; modern brush pens since the 1990s.
visual_markers: lines swelling and tapering with pressure
styles.prompt_fragment: black ink brush drawing, round sable brush lines swelling and tapering with pressure, bold solid black shapes, feathered dry-brush strokes at the edges, calligraphic contours, no gray tones, occasional white-out corrections, smooth bright bristol paper
styles.avoid: Avoid uniform vector line weight and the gray washes of East Asian ink painting.
styles.feasibility_note: Thick-thin brush lines hold well.
styles.short_de: Mit dem Rundpinsel gezogene schwarze Tuschlinien, die mit dem Druck an- und abschwellen, dazu satte Schwarzflächen und Trockenpinselränder; typisch für Zeitungs- und Comicillustration des 19. und 20. Jahrhunderts.
styles.short_en: Black ink drawn with a round brush, lines swelling and tapering with pressure, solid blacks and dry-brush edges; typical of 19th–20th-century illustration and comics inking.
styles.era_de: seit dem 19. Jh., Europa und USA
styles.era_en: since the 19th century, Europe and USA
markers_de: mit dem Druck an- und abschwellende Linien
markers_en: lines swelling and tapering with pressure

styles.era_origin: Ancient writing tool, used by 17th-century Dutch draughtsmen and in vigorous late-19th-century Post-Impressionist landscape drawings.
styles.prompt_fragment: reed pen drawing in brown-black ink, blunt broad strokes with abrupt ends, textures built from vigorous dashes, dots and short marks in rhythmic fields, ink running dry into broken scratchy lines, toned laid paper, no washes or hatching hairlines
styles.avoid: Avoid fine flexible-nib hairlines and smooth even hatching.
styles.feasibility_note: Can drift into generic pen hatching; insist on dashes and blunt marks.
styles.short_de: Federzeichnung mit zugeschnittener Rohr- oder Bambusfeder: breite, stumpfe Züge, Strichel und Punkte in rhythmischen Feldern; geschätzt im Holland des 17. Jahrhunderts und im Postimpressionismus.
styles.short_en: Pen drawing with a cut reed or bamboo nib: blunt broad strokes, dashes and dots in rhythmic fields; prized by 17th-century Dutch draughtsmen and the Post-Impressionists.
styles.era_de: seit der Antike; Niederlande 17. Jh., Frankreich 1880er

styles.era_origin: Modernist drawing practice of the early 20th century; a popular minimalist décor trend since the 2010s.
styles.prompt_fragment: continuous single-line drawing, the entire image made from one unbroken black line that never lifts from the paper, looping overlaps where it doubles back, simplified abstracted contours, no shading or fills, generous white space, slightly uneven pen pressure
styles.avoid: Avoid several disconnected strokes and sterile vector minimalism.
styles.feasibility_note: A truly continuous line is rarely achieved, but it reads as one line at a glance.
styles.short_de: Motiv aus einer einzigen, nie abgesetzten Linie; wurzelt in der Zeichenpraxis der frühen Moderne und ist seit den 2010er-Jahren als minimalistische Wanddeko beliebt.
styles.short_en: Motif drawn as one unbroken line that never leaves the paper; rooted in early-modernist drawing, a minimalist décor trend since the 2010s.
styles.era_de: frühes 20. Jh., Europa; seit den 2010ern international
styles.era_en: early 20th century, Europe; since the 2010s, international

styles.era_origin: Drawing exercise popularised by mid-20th-century American art education (codified in a 1941 drawing manual).
styles.prompt_fragment: blind contour drawing made without looking at the paper, one slow searching pen line tracing edges, comically distorted proportions, features drifting out of alignment, overlapping misplaced contours, wobbly hesitations and doubled-back lines, no shading, plain white paper
styles.avoid: Avoid correct proportions and stylised-but-competent line art; the charm is the misalignment.
styles.feasibility_note: The model resists real distortion and tends to produce stylised but correct drawings.
styles.short_de: Konturzeichnung, bei der der Blick nur auf dem Motiv und nie auf dem Blatt liegt, mit zittrigen Linien und verrutschten Proportionen; Übung aus dem US-Kunstunterricht ab 1941.
styles.short_en: Contour drawing made without looking at the paper, giving wobbly lines and drifting, distorted features; a classroom exercise popularised in US art teaching from 1941.

styles.era_origin: Contemporary sketchbook practice with opaque gel pens and white ink, widespread in 2010s hobby and illustration culture.
visual_markers: white lines on matte black paper
styles.prompt_fragment: drawing in opaque white gel pen and white ink on matte black paper, form described only through highlights and rim light, fine white hatching and stippling, thin strokes turning translucent gray where ink ran thin, slightly raised ink texture, black paper fibers visible
styles.avoid: Avoid an inverted photo or neon glow; it must stay hand-drawn.
styles.feasibility_note: Highlight-only logic renders well.
styles.short_de: Zeichnung mit weißem Gelstift und weißer Tusche auf mattschwarzem Papier, die Form entsteht nur aus Lichtern und weißer Schraffur; seit den 2010er-Jahren verbreitete Skizzenbuchpraxis.
styles.short_en: Drawing in white gel pen and ink on matte black paper, where form appears only through highlights and white hatching; a popular sketchbook practice since the 2010s.
markers_en: white lines on matte black paper

styles.era_origin: Developed in 19th-century Britain and France as a cheaper alternative to wood engraving for reproduction; popular in 1930s-50s advertising.
styles.prompt_fragment: scratchboard illustration, white lines scraped out of a black India-ink surface with a fine blade, tone built from tight parallel and contour-following white hatching, stark high contrast, crisp sharp-edged highlights, faint stray scratches and chalky white clay showing through
styles.avoid: Avoid gray tones and soft shading, and avoid the chunky gouges of a woodcut.
