fine crackle veins from broken wax
layered sogan brown, indigo and cream
styles.sensitivity_de: Einige Muster wie Parang waren historisch den javanischen Fürstenhöfen vorbehalten.
styles.sensitivity_en: Some motifs such as parang were historically reserved for the Javanese royal courts.

styles.era_origin: Java and Bali, Indonesia, mentioned in inscriptions from c. 10th c.; UNESCO Intangible Heritage.
visual_markers: rigid profile figures with very long thin arms
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Javanese wayang kulit shadow puppet: figures in rigid profile with exaggerated long thin arms, slender necks and stylized faces, intricately chiselled perforated buffalo-hide filigree, gilded and painted surfaces in gold, red, black and blue, articulated shoulders and elbows on slender horn rods, against a plain backdrop or lit by an oil lamp
styles.avoid: Avoid Western silhouette cut-outs and Chinese translucent colours; proportions are highly elongated and filigree dense.
styles.feasibility_note: Perforation and distorted anatomy partly succeed; arm articulation is often wrong.
styles.sensitivity_note: Figures represent characters from Hindu epics in ritual performance; use respectfully.
styles.short_de: Flache, fein durchbrochene Figuren aus Büffelleder im starren Profil mit überlangen, dünnen Armen, bemalt und vergoldet, an Hornstäben geführt; Java und Bali, belegt seit etwa dem 10. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Flat perforated buffalo-hide puppets in rigid profile with very long thin arms, painted and gilded, moved on horn rods; Java and Bali, attested since about the 10th century.
styles.era_de: seit ca. 10. Jh., Java und Bali (Indonesien)
styles.era_en: since c. 10th c., Java and Bali, Indonesia
markers_de: starre Profilfiguren mit überlangen, dünnen Armen
markers_en: rigid profile figures with very long thin arms
styles.sensitivity_de: Die Figuren verkörpern Gestalten hinduistischer Epen in rituellen Aufführungen; respektvoll verwenden.
styles.sensitivity_en: Figures embody characters from Hindu epics in ritual performances; use them respectfully.

styles.era_origin: Siam, Ayutthaya to Rattanakosin periods, 17th-19th c.
visual_markers: dark red or deep green grounds
jagged zigzag sinthao lines dividing scenes
graceful figures with backward-curving fingers and tapering crowns
lively everyday vignettes, no single perspective
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Thai Buddhist temple mural: flat tempera on plaster, dark red and deep green grounds, multiple scenes separated by jagged zigzag sinthao lines, graceful elongated figures with backward-curving fingers and tapering crowns picked out in gold leaf, lively small vignettes of everyday life alongside, no single perspective, softly worn and faded paint
styles.avoid: Avoid souvenir golden-Buddha art and glossy modern Thai painting; keep the flat multi-scene mural structure.
styles.feasibility_note: Ornamental figures render; sinthao scene dividers are omitted unless described.
styles.sensitivity_note: Sacred Jataka narratives; Thailand restricts disrespectful use of Buddha images.
styles.short_de: Buddhistische Wandmalerei in Tempera auf dunkelrotem oder grünem Grund, Szenen durch Zickzacklinien (Sinthao) getrennt, vergoldete, grazile Figuren und Alltagsszenen; Siam, 17. bis 19. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Buddhist wall paintings in tempera on dark red or green grounds, scenes divided by zigzag sinthao lines, gilded graceful figures and everyday vignettes; Siam, 17th–19th century.
markers_de: grazile Figuren mit zurückgebogenen Fingern und spitzen Kronen
markers_en: dark red or deep green grounds
graceful figures with back-curving fingers and tapering crowns
lively everyday vignettes, no single perspective
styles.sensitivity_de: Zeigt heilige Jataka-Erzählungen; in Thailand ist respektloser Umgang mit Buddha-Bildern eingeschränkt.
styles.sensitivity_en: Depicts sacred Jataka stories, and Thailand restricts disrespectful use of Buddha images.

styles.era_origin: Batuan village, Bali, from the 1930s.
visual_markers: crowded all-over composition of tiny figures
layered dark ink washes in greens, greys, sepia
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Balinese Batuan-style painting: a crowded all-over composition packed with hundreds of tiny figures, foliage and fantastical creatures, built up from countless layers of ink wash in dark greens, greys and sepia with occasional muted colour, meticulous fine detail, no horizon and no empty space, eerie dreamlike density
styles.avoid: Avoid bright tourist 'Bali' painting; keep the dark, dense layered-ink look.
styles.feasibility_note: Density is plausible; tiny figures dissolve into noisy texture.
styles.sensitivity_note: Contains Hindu-Balinese ritual and demonic imagery; respect sacred content.
styles.short_de: Dicht gefüllte balinesische Tuschbilder mit Hunderten winziger Figuren und Fabelwesen in geschichteten dunklen Lavierungen, ohne Horizont und Leerflächen; Dorf Batuan auf Bali, ab den 1930er-Jahren.
styles.short_en: Densely packed Balinese ink paintings with hundreds of tiny figures and creatures in layered dark washes, no horizon or empty space; Batuan village, Bali, from the 1930s.
markers_de: dicht gefüllte Gesamtfläche mit winzigen Figuren
geschichtete dunkle Lavierungen in Grün, Grau, Sepia
markers_en: crowded all-over composition of tiny figures
layered dark ink washes in green, grey, sepia
styles.sensitivity_de: Enthält hindu-balinesische Ritual- und Dämonenbilder; die sakralen Inhalte respektieren.
styles.sensitivity_en: Contains Hindu-Balinese ritual and demonic imagery; respect the sacred content.

styles.era_origin: Đông Hồ village, Bắc Ninh province, Vietnam, from c. 16th-17th c.; Tết folk prints.
visual_markers: dó paper coated with powdered seashell (điệp) with pearly shimmer
muted natural brick red, sophora yellow, leaf green, charcoal
one woodblock per colour, slight misregistration
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Vietnamese Đông Hồ folk woodblock print: printed on handmade dó paper coated with powdered seashell that glints with a soft pearly shimmer, flat earthy natural colours of brick red, sophora yellow, leaf green and charcoal black, one block per colour with slight misregistration, sturdy rounded forms, naive symmetry, a short block-printed caption at the top
styles.avoid: Avoid Chinese nianhua saturation and glossy reds; colours are muted and matte on a sparkling shell-white ground.
styles.feasibility_note: Little-known to the model; shell shimmer and muted palette must be spelled out.
styles.short_de: Vietnamesische Neujahrsholzschnitte (Tết) auf muschelbeschichtetem Dó-Papier mit Perlmuttschimmer, erdigen Naturfarben und rundlich-naiven Formen; Đông Hồ in der Provinz Bắc Ninh, seit etwa 1600.
styles.short_en: Vietnamese Tết woodblock prints on shell-coated dó paper with a pearly sheen, earthy natural colours and rounded naive forms; Đông Hồ, Bắc Ninh province, since about 1600.
styles.era_de: seit dem 16./17. Jh., Đông Hồ (Bắc Ninh, Vietnam)
styles.era_en: 16th–17th c. onward, Đông Hồ (Bắc Ninh), Vietnam
markers_de: gedämpfte Naturfarben: Ziegelrot, Gelb, Blattgrün, Kohleschwarz
ein Druckstock pro Farbe, leichter Passerversatz
markers_en: shell-coated dó paper with pearly shimmer
muted natural brick red, yellow, leaf green, charcoal
one block per colour, slight misregistration
short block-printed caption at the top

styles.era_origin: Vietnam, modern fine-art form developed in Hanoi in the 1930s from traditional lacquer craft.
visual_markers: deep black, cinnabar and amber lacquer layers
gold and silver leaf glowing through
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Vietnamese sơn mài lacquer painting: many layers of deep black, cinnabar red and amber-brown lacquer sanded back and polished to a mirror depth, crushed eggshell inlay forming crackled white mosaic areas, gold and silver leaf glowing through translucent layers, softly blurred edges where layers were rubbed away
styles.avoid: Avoid oil-paint brushwork and plastic gloss; depth comes from sanded translucent layers and inlay.
styles.feasibility_note: Lacquer gloss is approximated; eggshell inlay is missing unless stated.
styles.short_de: Bilder aus vielen Schichten schwarzen, roten und braunen Lacks mit Eierschaleneinlagen und Gold- oder Silberblatt, abgeschliffen und poliert; in den 1930er-Jahren in Hanoi entwickelt.
styles.short_en: Paintings built from many layers of black, red and brown lacquer with eggshell inlay and gold or silver leaf, sanded back and polished; Hanoi, developed in the 1930s.
markers_de: Lackschichten in Tiefschwarz, Zinnoberrot und Bernstein
markers_en: deep black, cinnabar and amber lacquer layers
gold and silver leaf glowing through

styles.era_origin: Iran and Central Asia, 13th-17th c., peaks in Timurid Herat and Safavid Tabriz and Isfahan.
visual_markers: high horizon and tilted ground planes
spongy rocks, gold sky, calligraphy panels
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Persian miniature painting: jewel-bright opaque pigments of lapis blue, vermilion, turquoise and gold, a high horizon with tilted ground planes so everything is seen at once, no shadows, intricately patterned tiles, carpets and garments, coral-like spongy rocks, a gold sky, small graceful figures, framed with ruled borders and calligraphy panels
styles.avoid: Avoid 'Arabian Nights' fantasy illustration and perspective depth; keep flat tilted planes and pattern-on-pattern.
styles.feasibility_note: Palette and pattern are good; calligraphy panels become pseudo-Persian script.
styles.sensitivity_note: Avoid depicting the Prophet Muhammad; fake Persian script may contain unintended words.
styles.short_de: Buchmalerei in Deckfarben und Gold mit hohem Horizont, gekippten Bodenflächen, schattenlosen Figuren und dichten Mustern, entstanden in persischen Hofwerkstätten des 13. bis 17. Jahrhunderts.
styles.short_en: Opaque watercolour and gold manuscript painting with tilted ground planes, high horizons, no shadows and dense patterning, from Persian court workshops of the 13th–17th centuries.
styles.era_de: 13.–17. Jh., Iran und Zentralasien (Herat, Täbris, Isfahan)
styles.era_en: 13th–17th c., Iran and Central Asia (Herat, Tabriz, Isfahan)
markers_en: spongy rocks, gold sky, calligraphy panels
styles.sensitivity_de: Den Propheten Mohammed nicht darstellen; generierte Pseudoschrift in persischen Buchstaben kann ungewollt echte Wörter bilden.
styles.sensitivity_en: Do not depict the Prophet Muhammad; generated pseudo-Persian script may form unintended words.

styles.era_origin: Iran, Qajar dynasty, c. 1789-1925.
visual_markers: flattened bodies with pale moon faces
almond eyes, joined black eyebrows, tiny red lips
dark background under arched niche or curtain
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Qajar-era Persian court oil painting: frontal or three-quarter figures with flattened bodies, pale moon faces, almond eyes, joined black eyebrows and tiny red lips, richly patterned brocade, strings of pearls and jewels in raised highlights, dark olive or black background under an arched niche or painted curtain, craquelure varnish
styles.avoid: Avoid European academic realism and orientalist harem clichés; the hybrid of flat decorative bodies and stylized faces is key.
styles.feasibility_note: Not deeply known to the model; spell out facial conventions and the arched dark background.
styles.sensitivity_note: Avoid orientalist exoticism.
styles.short_de: Iranische Hofmalerei in Öl mit flächigen, prunkvoll gekleideten Figuren, blassen runden Gesichtern, zusammengewachsenen Brauen und dunklem Bogenhintergrund, entstanden unter der Kadscharen-Dynastie (um 1789–1925).
styles.short_en: Iranian court oil painting with flat, richly dressed figures, pale round faces, joined eyebrows and dark arched backgrounds, from the Qajar dynasty (c. 1789–1925).
markers_de: Mandelaugen, zusammengewachsene Brauen, kleiner roter Mund
dunkler Grund unter Bogen oder Vorhang
markers_en: almond eyes, joined brows, small red lips
dark ground under arch or curtain
styles.sensitivity_de: Orientalistische Exotik vermeiden.
styles.sensitivity_en: Avoid orientalist exoticism.

styles.era_origin: Islamic world from the 9th c.; girih refined c. 12th-15th c. in Persia, Central Asia and the Maghreb.
visual_markers: hand-cut glazed tile mosaic with chipped edges
styles.prompt_fragment: built from Islamic geometric ornament: interlacing strapwork forming 8-, 10- and 12-pointed star rosettes and polygons on a compass-and-ruler lattice, over-under weaving of bands, rendered as hand-cut glazed zellige tile mosaic in turquoise, cobalt, white, saffron and green with chipped edges, uneven grout lines and glaze glints
styles.avoid: Avoid kaleidoscope mandalas and random hexagon fills; geometry must be consistent and interlaced.
styles.feasibility_note: Feel is right, but geometric precision fails on inspection; star counts and interlace often wrong.
styles.sensitivity_note: Used in mosques; integrate subjects as abstracted silhouettes rather than figurative imagery in sacred-space contexts.
styles.short_de: Verflochtene Bandornamente aus Sternrosetten und Polygonen, mit Zirkel und Lineal konstruiert, auf Fliesen, Holz und Stuck in der gesamten islamischen Welt seit dem 9. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Interlacing strapwork of star rosettes and polygons built on compass-and-ruler grids, used on tiles, wood and stucco across the Islamic world since the 9th century.
styles.era_de: seit dem 9. Jh.; Girih-Blüte 12.–15. Jh., Persien, Zentralasien, Maghreb
styles.era_en: since the 9th c.; girih peak 12th–15th c., Persia, Central Asia, Maghreb
markers_de: mit Zirkel und Lineal konstruiertes Raster
styles.sensitivity_de: Prägt Moscheen; in sakralen Kontexten Motive nur als abstrahierte Silhouetten statt figürlich einbinden.
styles.sensitivity_en: Common in mosques; in sacred-space contexts integrate subjects as abstract silhouettes, not figurative images.

styles.era_origin: Islamic manuscript illumination refined in Timurid, Safavid and Ottoman courts, 15th-17th c.
visual_markers: endlessly scrolling vines with split palmettes
styles.prompt_fragment: framed and filled with Islamic manuscript illumination: burnished shell-gold grounds, endlessly scrolling arabesque vines with split-leaf palmettes and stylized blossoms in hair-fine outlines, lapis blue, turquoise and carmine accents, symmetrical cartouches and medallions, delicate gold-sprinkled margins on polished cream paper
styles.avoid: Avoid Victorian florals and baroque scrolls; arabesque is flat, symmetrical, infinitely continuing and gilded.
styles.feasibility_note: Gold and scroll feel works; symmetry and continuous-scroll logic are imperfect.
styles.sensitivity_note: Often frames Quranic text; never generate fake Quranic or religious script.
styles.short_de: Vergoldete Buchornamentik aus endlos rankenden Arabesken, Palmetten und Kartuschen als Seitenrahmung, vollendet in timuridischen, safawidischen und osmanischen Hofwerkstätten des 15. bis 17. Jahrhunderts.
styles.short_en: Gilded ornament of endlessly scrolling arabesque vines, palmettes and cartouches framing manuscript pages, perfected in Timurid, Safavid and Ottoman court workshops of the 15th–17th centuries.
styles.era_de: 15.–17. Jh., timuridische, safawidische und osmanische Höfe
styles.era_en: 15th–17th c., Timurid, Safavid and Ottoman courts
markers_de: Akzente in Lapisblau, Türkis und Karmin
styles.sensitivity_de: Rahmt oft Korantext; niemals gefälschte Koran- oder andere religiöse Schrift erzeugen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Often frames Quranic text; never generate fake Quranic or other religious script.

styles.era_origin: Iznik, Anatolia, Ottoman Empire, late 15th-17th c., peak in the mid-16th c.
visual_markers: brilliant white fritware under clear glaze
cobalt, turquoise, emerald and raised tomato-red slip
serrated saz leaves, tulips, carnations, hyacinths
styles.prompt_fragment: painted as Ottoman Iznik ceramic: brilliant white fritware ground under clear glaze, cobalt blue, turquoise, emerald green and a thick raised tomato-red slip, crisp black outlines, serrated saz leaves, tulips, carnations and hyacinth sprays flowing across a grid of square tiles with visible seams, glossy glaze with slight pooling
styles.avoid: Avoid Delft-style monochrome blue and generic Mediterranean tile; raised tomato red and saz leaves are signature.
styles.feasibility_note: Palette and floral vocabulary hold; figurative subjects need adaptation into the floral idiom.
styles.short_de: Osmanische Quarzfritte-Keramik mit Kobaltblau, Türkis, Grün und erhabenem Tomatenrot auf leuchtendem Weiß, bemalt mit Saz-Blättern, Tulpen und Nelken, ab dem späten 15. Jahrhundert in Iznik gefertigt.
styles.short_en: Ottoman fritware with cobalt, turquoise, green and raised tomato red on brilliant white, painted with saz leaves, tulips and carnations, made in Iznik from the late 15th century.
markers_de: leuchtend weiße Fritteware unter klarer Glasur
markers_en: brilliant white fritware under clear glaze
cobalt, turquoise, emerald, raised tomato red

styles.era_origin: Ethiopia, Christian painting from the medieval period; Gondarine styles 17th-18th c.
visual_markers: bold flat crimson, saffron, green, deep blue
styles.prompt_fragment: as traditional Ethiopian Orthodox church painting: figures with oversized almond eyes and frontal faces, thick dark outlines, bold flat fields of crimson, saffron yellow, leaf green and deep blue, plain ochre background, stacked narrative registers like a comic strip, striped and patterned robes, tempera on canvas or parchment with gentle wear
styles.avoid: Avoid Byzantine gold grounds and European shading; the style is flat, bright, outlined and expressive.
styles.feasibility_note: Eyes and outline style render; Ge'ez captions come out as gibberish, so omit text.
styles.sensitivity_note: Sacred iconography of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church; avoid irreverent use of saints and holy figures.
styles.short_de: Flächige, farbkräftige Kirchenmalerei mit großen mandeläugigen Frontalgesichtern, kräftigen Konturen und übereinander gestapelten Bildstreifen aus dem christlichen Äthiopien; der Gondar-Stil blühte im 17. und 18. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Flat, bright church painting with large almond-eyed frontal faces, heavy outlines and stacked narrative registers from Christian Ethiopia; the Gondarine style peaked in the 17th–18th centuries.
styles.era_de: seit dem Mittelalter; Gondar-Stil 17.–18. Jh., Äthiopien
styles.era_en: since the Middle Ages; Gondarine style 17th–18th c., Ethiopia
markers_en: flat crimson, saffron, green, deep blue
styles.sensitivity_de: Sakrale Ikonografie der Äthiopisch-Orthodoxen Tewahedo-Kirche; Heilige und biblische Figuren nicht respektlos verwenden.
styles.sensitivity_en: Sacred iconography of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church; do not use saints and holy figures irreverently.

styles.era_origin: Southern Ndebele women in South Africa; documented from the early 20th c., flourishing from the 1940s.
styles.prompt_fragment: painted in the manner of Ndebele house painting: bold hard-edged geometric shapes outlined with thick black bands, flat fields of cobalt blue, golden yellow, red, green and pink on whitewashed ground, stepped forms, chevrons and abstracted architectural motifs, symmetrical layout, hand-painted brush edges on slightly rough mud plaster
styles.avoid: Avoid Memphis-style pastiche and generic 'African print'; keep black outlines and stepped geometry on white.
styles.feasibility_note: Strong graphic grammar; the model sometimes adds random masks - exclude them.
styles.sensitivity_note: Living identity practice of Ndebele women; do not conflate with pan-African clichés.
styles.short_de: Hartkantige geometrische Wandbemalung mit dicken schwarzen Konturen und leuchtenden Flachfarben auf Kalkweiß, ausgeführt von Frauen der Süd-Ndebele in Südafrika, dokumentiert seit dem frühen 20. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Hard-edged geometric wall murals with thick black outlines and bright flat colours on whitewash, painted by Southern Ndebele women in South Africa, documented since the early 20th century.
styles.era_de: seit dem frühen 20. Jh., leuchtende Farben ab den 1940ern, Südafrika
styles.era_en: early 20th c. onwards, bright colours from the 1940s, South Africa
styles.sensitivity_de: Lebendige Identitätspraxis der Ndebele-Frauen; nicht mit panafrikanischen Klischees vermengen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Living identity practice of Ndebele women; do not merge it into pan-African clichés.

styles.era_origin: Asante and Ewe peoples of Ghana and Togo, documented from the 17th c.
visual_markers: narrow hand-loomed strips sewn edge to edge
alternating warp stripes and weft-faced blocks
gold, emerald, crimson, black, royal blue
styles.prompt_fragment: woven as Ghanaian kente cloth: narrow hand-loomed strips sewn side by side, alternating blocks of warp stripes and weft-faced geometric motifs, zigzags, checks and small ladders in gold, emerald, crimson, black and royal blue, slightly offset strip seams, glossy silk-rayon sheen and tight visible weave
styles.avoid: Avoid printed imitation kente as flat vector fabric; show woven strip structure and texture.
styles.feasibility_note: Woven texture convinces; strip-block logic and named patterns are unreliable.
styles.sensitivity_note: Patterns are named and meaningful, some historically reserved for Asante royalty; strong diaspora identity symbol - avoid costume trivialization.
styles.short_de: Handgewebter Stoff aus schmalen, aneinandergenähten Bahnen mit wechselnden Streifen- und Geometrieblöcken in Gold, Grün, Rot und Schwarz, gewebt von Asante und Ewe seit dem 17. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Narrow handwoven strips sewn into cloth, with alternating stripes and geometric blocks in gold, green, red and black, made by Asante and Ewe weavers since the 17th century.
styles.era_de: seit dem 17. Jh., Ghana und Togo (Asante, Ewe)
styles.era_en: since the 17th c., Ghana and Togo (Asante, Ewe)
markers_de: schmale Webbahnen, Kante an Kante vernäht
markers_en: narrow loom strips sewn edge to edge
warp stripes alternating with weft blocks
gold, emerald, crimson, black, royal blue
styles.sensitivity_de: Muster tragen Namen und Bedeutungen, manche waren dem Asante-Königshof vorbehalten; als Identitätssymbol der Diaspora nicht als Kostümeffekt verharmlosen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Patterns are named and meaningful, some once reserved for Asante royalty; a strong diaspora identity symbol, so avoid costume-like trivialisation.

styles.era_origin: Asante of Ghana, documented since the early 19th c.
visual_markers: black symbols stamped from carved calabash
grid divided by comb-drawn parallel lines
styles.prompt_fragment: as Ghanaian adinkra cloth printing: bold black symbolic motifs stamped from carved calabash stamps in repeated rows, uneven ink density and smudges, grid sections divided by comb-drawn parallel lines, on russet, ochre or off-white cotton, the subject reduced to a stamp-like emblem within the repeating pattern
styles.avoid: Avoid inventing pseudo-adinkra symbols or rendering them as clean vector icons.
styles.feasibility_note: Stamp texture works; real adinkra symbols are not reproduced reliably.
styles.sensitivity_note: Each symbol carries a proverb; traditionally mourning cloth; do not misattribute meanings.
styles.short_de: Baumwolltuch mit schwarzen Sprichwort-Symbolen, gestempelt mit geschnitzten Kalebassen in kammgezogenen Rasterfeldern; Tradition der Asante in Ghana, belegt seit dem frühen 19. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Cotton cloth stamped in black with carved calabash stamps of proverb symbols in comb-ruled grids, an Asante tradition of Ghana documented since the early 19th century.
markers_en: black symbols stamped with carved calabash
styles.sensitivity_de: Jedes Symbol steht für ein Sprichwort, traditionell ist der Stoff Trauerkleidung; Bedeutungen nicht falsch zuordnen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Each symbol stands for a proverb and the cloth is traditionally worn for mourning; do not misattribute meanings.

styles.era_origin: Bamana people of Mali, centuries old; internationally revived since the 1970s.
visual_markers: deep brown-black ground with cream negative motifs
styles.prompt_fragment: as Malian bogolan mud cloth: hand-painted fermented-mud dye producing a deep brown-black ground with cream negative-space motifs, rows of dots, crosses, zigzags and concentric squares arranged in a loose grid, narrow handwoven cotton strips stitched together, uneven absorption and soft mottled edges
styles.avoid: Avoid home-décor 'mudcloth print' vectors and beige minimalism; keep irregular hand painting and strip seams.
styles.feasibility_note: Simple graphic vocabulary renders reliably.
styles.sensitivity_note: Motifs carry Bamana meanings tied to identity and rites; do not invent meanings.
styles.short_de: Handgewebte Baumwollbahnen, mit fermentiertem Schlamm zu dunkelbraunem Grund mit hellen Punkten, Kreuzen und Zickzacklinien bemalt; Tradition der Bamana in Mali, international wiederbelebt seit den 1970ern.
styles.short_en: Handwoven cotton strips painted with fermented mud into a dark brown ground with cream dots, crosses and zigzags, a Bamana tradition of Mali revived internationally since the 1970s.
styles.era_de: traditionell, Mali (Bamana); internationale Wiederbelebung seit den 1970ern
styles.era_en: traditional, Mali (Bamana); international revival since the 1970s
styles.sensitivity_de: Die Motive haben bei den Bamana Bedeutungen für Identität und Riten; keine Bedeutungen erfinden.
styles.sensitivity_en: Motifs carry Bamana meanings tied to identity and rites; do not invent meanings.

styles.era_origin: Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, from 1968.
visual_markers: glossy enamel paint on square board
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Tanzanian Tingatinga painting: glossy enamel paint on a square hardboard panel, flat saturated colours with no shading, stylized forms with decorative dotted and striped fills, crisp black outlines, a plain single-colour background, playful symmetry and repetition, visible brush ridges and high-gloss shine
styles.avoid: Avoid children's-book vector animals; enamel gloss, patterned bodies and plain backgrounds define it.
styles.feasibility_note: Flat bright stylization is easy; enamel sheen must be mentioned.
styles.sensitivity_note: Named after its (deceased) founder; a living school of artists.
styles.short_de: Glänzende Lackfarbenbilder auf quadratischen Platten mit flachen Leuchtfarben, schwarzen Konturen und gepunkteten oder gestreiften Tierkörpern vor einfarbigem Grund, seit 1968 aus Daressalam, Tansania.
styles.short_en: Glossy enamel paintings on square boards with flat bright colours, black outlines and dotted or striped animal bodies on plain backgrounds, from Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, since 1968.
styles.sensitivity_de: Nach dem verstorbenen Begründer benannt und von einer lebendigen Künstlerschule weitergeführt.
styles.sensitivity_en: Named after its late founder and still practised by a living school of artists.

styles.era_origin: Ghana, mid-1980s to late 1990s, for travelling video-club screenings.
visual_markers: oil paint on stitched flour sacks
seams, folds and printed sack lettering showing through
wildly exaggerated imagined action and monsters
bold hand-lettered title with drop shadow
styles.prompt_fragment: as a 1990s Ghanaian hand-painted mobile-cinema poster: oil paint on two stitched-together flour sacks with seams, folds and faded printed lettering showing through, wildly exaggerated dramatic figures and imagined action collaged together, saturated colours, bold hand-lettered title with drop shadows, raw expressive brushwork
styles.avoid: Avoid polished Hollywood key art and recognizable actor likenesses; keep improvised exaggeration and sack texture.
styles.feasibility_note: Texture and drama render well; garbled lettering suits the look.
styles.sensitivity_note: Originals reference real films and actors - never name films or celebrities.
styles.short_de: Ölbilder auf zusammengenähten Mehlsäcken, die Videovorführungen mit übersteigerten, frei erfundenen Actionszenen und kräftigen handgemalten Titeln bewarben; Ghana, Mitte der 1980er bis Ende der 1990er.
styles.short_en: Oil paintings on stitched flour sacks advertising video screenings with exaggerated, invented action scenes and bold hand-lettered titles, made in Ghana from the mid-1980s to the late 1990s.
markers_en: seams and sack print showing through
styles.sensitivity_de: Die Originale warben für echte Filme mit echten Schauspielern; keine Filmtitel oder Prominenten nennen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Originals advertised real films with real actors; never name films or celebrities.

styles.era_origin: Senegal, early 20th c., first Islamic devotional imagery, later everyday life.
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Senegalese reverse-glass painting (suwer): flat bright enamel colours painted behind glass, crisp dark outlines, naive frontal figures, decorative borders, small areas backed with crinkled metallic foil that glints, glossy glass reflections across the surface, simple cloth-tape bound frame
styles.avoid: Avoid deep perspective and painterly blending; reverse painting means flat layered colour under gloss.
styles.feasibility_note: Glass reflections are plausible; reverse-paint layering is subtle.
styles.sensitivity_note: Images of Sufi saints are venerated; do not trivialize them.
styles.short_de: Naive Hinterglasbilder mit flachen Leuchtfarben, dunklen Konturen und Folienakzenten, die Sufi-Heilige und Alltagsszenen zeigen; im Senegal seit dem frühen 20. Jahrhundert gemalt.
styles.short_en: Naive paintings behind glass with flat bright colours, dark outlines and foil accents, depicting Sufi saints and everyday life; made in Senegal since the early 20th century.
styles.sensitivity_de: Bilder von Sufi-Heiligen werden verehrt; nicht verharmlosen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Images of Sufi saints are venerated; do not trivialise them.

styles.era_origin: Industrial wax-resist cloth developed in the Netherlands in the 19th c. from Javanese batik and adopted across West and Central Africa.
visual_markers: dark key layer off-register from fills
styles.prompt_fragment: as an African wax-print (Ankara) cotton textile: large bold motifs in a repeating all-over layout, saturated contrasting colours like indigo, orange, magenta and lime, a dark key outline layer slightly off-register from the fill colours, fine marbled crackle lines from wax resist, crisp glossy cotton finish
styles.avoid: Avoid generic 'tribal' vectors; off-register dye layers and wax crackle are the tells.
styles.feasibility_note: Familiar look; off-register effect needs explicit mention.
styles.sensitivity_note: Do not use manufacturer brand names; pattern names carry social meanings; history entangled with colonial trade.
styles.short_de: Industriell im Wachsreservedruck gefertigte Baumwolle mit großen, kräftigen Rapporten, satten Farben, versetzten Konturen und Bruchlinien; im 19. Jahrhundert in den Niederlanden entwickelt, in West- und Zentralafrika heimisch geworden.
styles.short_en: Industrial wax-resist cotton with large bold repeats, saturated colours, off-register outlines and crackle; developed in the Netherlands in the 19th century and adopted across West and Central Africa.
styles.era_de: seit dem 19. Jh., Niederlande / West- und Zentralafrika
styles.era_en: since the 19th c., Netherlands / West and Central Africa
styles.sensitivity_de: Keine Herstellermarken nennen; Musternamen tragen soziale Bedeutungen, die Geschichte ist mit kolonialem Handel verflochten.
styles.sensitivity_en: Do not use manufacturer brand names; pattern names carry social meanings and the history is entangled with colonial trade.

styles.era_origin: Bark paper from the Otomí of San Pablito, Puebla; painted by Nahua artists from Guerrero since the 1960s.
visual_markers: mottled brown beaten-bark paper with mesh fibres
styles.prompt_fragment: painted on Mexican amate bark paper: a mottled dark-brown handmade sheet with visible beaten fibres and mesh texture, the subject surrounded by densely packed flat stylized birds and flowers in bright fuchsia, orange, turquoise, yellow and white, thin black outlines and decorative dots, naive all-over composition without perspective
styles.avoid: Avoid smooth digital backgrounds; the fibrous bark paper must show through.
styles.feasibility_note: Paper texture and naive palette render reliably.
styles.sensitivity_note: Amate has pre-Hispanic and ongoing Otomí ritual use (cut-paper figures in healing rites).
styles.short_de: Leuchtende, flache Vögel und Blumen mit feinen schwarzen Konturen auf fleckig braunem Rindenpapier, gemalt von Nahua-Künstlern in Guerrero, Mexiko, seit den 1960er-Jahren.
styles.short_en: Bright flat birds and flowers with thin black outlines on mottled brown bark paper, painted by Nahua artists in Guerrero, Mexico, since the 1960s.
styles.era_de: seit den 1960ern, Guerrero, Mexiko (Papier aus San Pablito, Puebla)
styles.era_en: since the 1960s, Guerrero, Mexico (paper from San Pablito, Puebla)
markers_en: mottled brown bark paper with fibre mesh
styles.sensitivity_de: Amate hat vorspanische Wurzeln und dient bei den Otomí bis heute in Heilritualen für ausgeschnittene Papierfiguren.
styles.sensitivity_en: Amate has pre-Hispanic roots and is still used for cut-paper figures in Otomí healing rites.

styles.era_origin: Wixárika (Huichol) people of western Mexico; ritual nierika, commercial yarn paintings since the 1950s-60s.
visual_markers: yarn pressed into beeswax on board
tight concentric contour lines echoing every shape
intense magenta, electric blue, yellow, red, green
styles.prompt_fragment: made as a Wixárika (Huichol) yarn painting: strands of brightly dyed wool yarn pressed into beeswax on a wooden board, following each shape in tight concentric contour lines, intense saturated magenta, electric blue, yellow, red and green, every area filled with echoing outlines and radiating patterns, fuzzy yarn texture
styles.avoid: Avoid psychedelic digital art; yarn-in-wax contour texture is what makes it read correctly.
styles.feasibility_note: Yarn texture convinces; can slide into generic psychedelia.
styles.sensitivity_note: Sacred tradition tied to peyote ritual and Wixárika cosmology; avoid psychedelic-tourism framing and invented sacred symbols.
styles.short_de: Bilder aus leuchtend gefärbter Wolle, in Bienenwachs auf ein Brett gedrückt, jede Form von konzentrischen Konturlinien umfasst; von Wixárika (Huichol) im Westen Mexikos, seit den 1950er/60er-Jahren.
styles.short_en: Pictures made by pressing brightly dyed yarn into beeswax on board, every shape echoed by concentric contour lines, by Wixárika (Huichol) artists of western Mexico since the 1950s–60s.
markers_de: Magenta, leuchtendes Blau, Gelb, Rot, Grün
markers_en: yarn pressed into beeswax on board
magenta, electric blue, yellow, red, green
styles.sensitivity_de: Wurzelt in der Kosmologie und dem Peyote-Ritual der Wixárika; keine Psychedelik-Tourismus-Ästhetik und keine erfundenen heiligen Symbole.
styles.sensitivity_en: Rooted in Wixárika cosmology and peyote ritual; avoid psychedelic-tourism framing and invented sacred symbols.

styles.era_origin: Otomí (Hñähñu) communities of Tenango de Doria, Hidalgo, Mexico, since the 1960s.
visual_markers: dense satin-stitch silhouettes on white muslin
single bold colour or rainbow of separate colours
silky thread sheen and stitch direction
styles.prompt_fragment: embroidered in Otomí tenango style: dense satin-stitch silhouettes on white cotton muslin, stylized flat creatures and plants with no outlines, a single bold thread colour or a rainbow of separate colours, loose symmetrical arrangement, visible stitch direction and silky thread sheen, slight puckering of fabric
styles.avoid: Avoid cross-stitch pixelation and machine-embroidery perfection; satin stitch on white cloth defines it.
styles.feasibility_note: Textile look holds; complex subjects lose stitch logic.
styles.sensitivity_note: Designs have been appropriated by fashion brands; credit Otomí communities rather than 'Mexican' generically.
styles.short_de: Dichte Plattstich-Silhouetten von Tieren und Pflanzen ohne Konturen auf weißer Baumwolle, ein- oder vielfarbig, aus Otomí-Gemeinden in Tenango de Doria, Mexiko, seit den 1960ern.
styles.short_en: Dense satin-stitch silhouettes of animals and plants without outlines on white cotton, in one colour or many, from Otomí communities of Tenango de Doria, Mexico, since the 1960s.
styles.era_de: seit den 1960ern, Tenango de Doria, Hidalgo, Mexiko
styles.era_en: since the 1960s, Tenango de Doria, Hidalgo, Mexico
markers_de: eine kräftige Farbe oder viele Einzelfarben
markers_en: dense satin-stitch silhouettes on white muslin
one bold colour or separate rainbow colours
styles.sensitivity_de: Modemarken haben die Motive kopiert; die Otomí-Gemeinden statt pauschal „Mexiko“ als Urheber nennen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Designs have been copied by fashion brands; credit Otomí communities rather than 'Mexico' in general.

styles.era_origin: Puebla and Tlaxcala, Mexico, from the 16th c., derived from Spanish majolica.
visual_markers: yolk yellow, orange, green, mauve accents
bold radial floral and geometric designs
styles.prompt_fragment: painted as Mexican Talavera majolica: thick milky tin-glaze white ground, raised pooled cobalt blue that stands slightly in relief, accents of yolk yellow, orange, green and mauve, bold radial floral and geometric patterns, hand-brushed irregular edges, fine crazing and glaze drips on square tiles or curved pottery
styles.avoid: Avoid Delft or Iznik look-alikes and flat printed tile; Talavera is thick, raised and slightly naive.
styles.feasibility_note: Common reference; the raised cobalt relief is often lost.
styles.sensitivity_note: 'Talavera' is a protected denomination of origin in Mexico; use descriptively.
styles.short_de: Zinnglasierte Irdenware mit dickem, milchigem Weiß, erhaben stehendem Kobaltblau und Akzenten in Gelb, Grün und Orange, in Puebla und Tlaxcala, Mexiko, seit dem 16. Jahrhundert gefertigt.
styles.short_en: Tin-glazed earthenware with thick milky white, raised cobalt blue and yellow, green and orange accents in floral patterns, made in Puebla and Tlaxcala, Mexico, since the 16th century.
styles.era_de: seit dem 16. Jh., Puebla und Tlaxcala, Mexiko
styles.era_en: since the 16th c., Puebla and Tlaxcala, Mexico
markers_de: Akzente in Dottergelb, Orange, Grün, Mauve
markers_en: yolk yellow, orange, green, mauve accents
bold radial floral and geometric designs
styles.sensitivity_de: „Talavera“ ist in Mexiko eine geschützte Herkunftsbezeichnung; nur beschreibend verwenden.
styles.sensitivity_en: 'Talavera' is a protected designation of origin in Mexico; use the term descriptively.

styles.era_origin: Mexico, tradition centred on San Salvador Huixcolotla, Puebla, since the 19th c.; used for Día de Muertos and fiestas.
visual_markers: vivid tissue-paper rectangles strung on a line
styles.prompt_fragment: cut as Mexican papel picado: rectangular sheets of vivid fuchsia, orange, lime, turquoise and yellow tissue paper with intricate chisel-cut silhouettes and lacy fringe borders, strung in a row on a string, translucent with sunlight glowing through, soft wrinkles and fluttering folds, scalloped grid patterns around the main motif
styles.avoid: Avoid flat vector bunting clip-art; show thin translucent paper and chisel-cut texture.
styles.feasibility_note: Bunting and cut patterns render well; subject silhouettes can be too detailed to be cuttable.
styles.sensitivity_note: Linked to Día de Muertos as a religious and cultural observance; do not conflate with Halloween.
styles.short_de: Bunte Seidenpapierbögen mit ausgemeißelten filigranen Mustern, an Schnüren aufgereiht für Fiestas und Día de Muertos; mexikanisches Handwerk mit Zentrum in Huixcolotla (Puebla), seit dem 19. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Bright tissue-paper banners chisel-cut into lacy silhouettes and strung on lines for fiestas and Día de Muertos; a Mexican craft centred on Huixcolotla, Puebla, since the 19th century.
markers_en: vivid tissue-paper rectangles on a string
styles.sensitivity_de: Gehört zum Día de Muertos als religiösem und kulturellem Fest; nicht mit Halloween gleichsetzen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Tied to Día de Muertos as a religious and cultural observance; do not conflate it with Halloween.

styles.era_origin: Mexico City, late 19th to early 20th c. satirical penny broadsides.
visual_markers: figures as lively satirical skeletons in everyday dress
cheap pink, yellow or green newsprint
styles.prompt_fragment: as a turn-of-the-century Mexican calavera broadside: black relief-printed lines and crosshatching from a metal or lino block, all figures shown as lively satirical skeletons in everyday clothes, heavy ink on cheap pink, yellow or green newsprint, columns of verse in old typefaces below, ink fill-in and press bite
styles.avoid: Avoid sugar-skull tattoo flash and Halloween horror; the tone is witty social satire in rough relief print.
styles.feasibility_note: Relief-print look is reliable; verse becomes pseudo-Spanish.
styles.sensitivity_note: Living religious/cultural tradition; do not name the famous (deceased) printmaker or copy his specific images.
styles.short_de: Schwarze Hochdrucke satirischer Skelette in Alltagskleidung mit Spottversen auf billigem Farbpapier, als Flugblätter zum Día de Muertos in Mexiko-Stadt verkauft, um 1890–1920.
styles.short_en: Black relief prints of satirical skeletons in everyday dress with rhymed verses on cheap coloured paper, sold as broadsides in Mexico City for Día de Muertos, c. 1890–1920.
markers_de: billiges rosa, gelbes oder grünes Papier
markers_en: lively satirical skeletons in everyday dress
cheap pink, yellow or green paper
styles.sensitivity_de: Teil einer lebendigen religiösen und kulturellen Tradition; den berühmten verstorbenen Grafiker nicht nennen und keine seiner Bilder kopieren.
styles.sensitivity_en: Part of a living religious and cultural tradition; do not name the famous late printmaker or copy his specific images.

styles.era_origin: Mexico, bingo-like game since the 18th c.; standard card imagery from the late 19th c.
visual_markers: tall rounded-corner card with thin frame
flat primary colours with heavy black outlines
number in top corner, serif name banner at bottom
styles.prompt_fragment: designed as a vintage Mexican lotería card: tall rounded-corner card with a thin black frame, a single bold central figure in flat primary colours with heavy black outlines and simple shading, a number in the top corner, bold serif name banner at the bottom, chromolithographic print texture, worn edges and foxing on off-white card stock
styles.avoid: Avoid ornate tarot-card styling and glossy digital illustration; keep folk-printed simplicity.
styles.feasibility_note: Card layout renders reliably; give the exact label text.
styles.sensitivity_note: Classic deck artwork is trademarked; create original figures rather than copying named cards.
styles.short_de: Hochformatige Spielkarte mit einer kräftigen Figur in Flachfarben und schwarzen Konturen, Nummer in der Ecke und Namensband unten; aus dem mexikanischen Lotería-Spiel, Ende des 19. Jahrhunderts standardisiert.
styles.short_en: Tall card with a bold figure in flat colours and black outlines, a corner number and name banner, from Mexican lotería, standardised in the late 19th century.
styles.era_de: Spiel seit dem 18. Jh.; Standardbilder ab dem späten 19. Jh., Mexiko
styles.era_en: game since the 18th c.; standard imagery from the late 19th c., Mexico
markers_de: hochformatige Karte mit runden Ecken und dünnem Rahmen
markers_en: tall rounded-corner card with thin frame
flat primary colours, heavy black outlines
styles.sensitivity_de: Die Bilder des klassischen Decks sind markenrechtlich geschützt; eigene Figuren entwerfen statt bekannte Karten zu kopieren.
styles.sensitivity_en: The classic deck artwork is trademarked; create original figures instead of copying named cards.

styles.era_origin: Mexico, 19th to early 20th c. devotional paintings on tin sheets.
visual_markers: naive oil on small tin sheet
protective apparition in clouds in upper corner
hand-lettered narrative text band at bottom
styles.prompt_fragment: painted as a Mexican ex-voto on a small tin sheet: naive oil painting with awkward perspective and stiff figures, the subject staged as a miraculous rescue in the middle, a radiant protective apparition in clouds in the upper corner, a band of hand-lettered narrative text along the bottom, rust spots, dents and nail holes
styles.avoid: Avoid polished religious art; ex-votos are untrained, earnest and quirky with a text panel.
styles.feasibility_note: Format works; hand-lettered Spanish text is garbled.
styles.sensitivity_note: Genuine Catholic devotional practice; parodies are common but can offend believers.
styles.short_de: Naive Ölbilder auf Blech, die einem Heiligen für eine Rettung danken: das Unglück, die Erscheinung in Wolken und ein handgeschriebener Bericht; Mexiko, 19. bis frühes 20. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Naive oil paintings on tin thanking a saint for rescue, showing the mishap, a holy figure in clouds and a written account; Mexico, 19th to early 20th century.
markers_de: Heiligenerscheinung in Wolken in der oberen Ecke
markers_en: naive oil on a small tin sheet
holy apparition in clouds in upper corner
hand-lettered text band at the bottom
styles.sensitivity_de: Gelebte katholische Frömmigkeitspraxis; Parodien sind verbreitet, können Gläubige aber verletzen.
styles.sensitivity_en: A genuine Catholic devotional practice; parodies are common but can offend believers.

styles.era_origin: Ayacucho, Peru, from colonial portable altars; secular scenes from the 1940s.
visual_markers: wooden box with flower-painted hinged doors
styles.prompt_fragment: built as a Peruvian Ayacucho retablo: a small wooden box with hinged doors painted with bright flowers, opened to reveal two or three stacked stage-like levels crowded with tiny hand-modelled painted plaster figures in candy-bright colours, triangular gable top, slightly lumpy handmade finish, photographed straight-on in soft light
styles.avoid: Avoid dollhouse realism and plastic-toy shine; figures are handmade, small and naive.
styles.feasibility_note: Diorama box is achievable; crowded tiny figures turn mushy.
styles.sensitivity_note: Originated as Catholic devotional objects; also used as testimony of the 1980s political violence.
styles.short_de: Holzkasten mit bemalten Flügeltüren, dahinter übereinander gestaffelte Ebenen mit winzigen bemalten Gipsfiguren; aus Ayacucho, Peru, hervorgegangen aus kolonialen Reisealtären, mit weltlichen Szenen seit den 1940ern.
styles.short_en: Wooden box with painted hinged doors opening onto stacked levels of tiny plaster figures, from Ayacucho, Peru, evolved from colonial portable altars, with secular scenes since the 1940s.
styles.era_de: koloniale Wurzeln; weltliche Szenen seit den 1940ern, Ayacucho, Peru
styles.era_en: colonial roots; secular scenes since the 1940s, Ayacucho, Peru
styles.sensitivity_de: Ursprünglich katholische Andachtsobjekte; dienen auch als Zeugnis der politischen Gewalt der 1980er-Jahre.
styles.sensitivity_en: Originally Catholic devotional objects; also used to bear witness to the political violence of the 1980s.

styles.era_origin: Papier-mâché alebrijes in Mexico City from the 1930s; Oaxacan copal-wood carvings from the 1980s.
visual_markers: every surface covered in tiny dots, stripes, zigzags
saturated pink, turquoise, orange, yellow, black
styles.prompt_fragment: made as an Oaxacan alebrije folk sculpture: hand-carved copal wood or papier-mâché with slightly rough carving, every surface covered in tiny painted dots, stripes, zigzags and flame patterns in saturated pink, turquoise, orange, yellow and black, fantastical exaggerated forms, matte acrylic paint, displayed as a handcrafted object
styles.avoid: Avoid smooth 3D renders and glossy vinyl-toy aesthetics; it must look hand-carved and hand-painted.
styles.feasibility_note: Renders well; may become CGI-smooth without 'hand-carved'.
styles.short_de: Fantasiewesen aus geschnitztem Kopalholz oder Pappmaché, übersät mit winzigen bunten Punkten, Streifen und Zickzacklinien; aus Mexiko-Stadt seit den 1930ern und Oaxaca seit den 1980ern.
styles.short_en: Fantastical creatures in carved copal wood or papier-mâché, covered in tiny bright dots, stripes and zigzags, from Mexico City in the 1930s and Oaxaca since the 1980s.
markers_en: tiny dots, stripes and zigzags everywhere

styles.era_origin: Guna (Kuna) women of Panama and Colombia, since the late 19th c.
visual_markers: layered cotton cut away in reverse appliqué
shapes echoed by parallel contour bands
styles.prompt_fragment: stitched as a Guna mola textile panel: several layers of brightly coloured cotton cut away in reverse appliqué so each shape is echoed by parallel contour bands of red, orange, black, yellow and green, narrow slit fillers in empty spaces, tiny visible hand stitches, slightly uneven edges, rectangular panel
styles.avoid: Avoid flat vector illustration and quilting; layered cut-away outlines with stitches are essential.
styles.feasibility_note: Contour echoing works; fabric layering logic is approximated.
styles.sensitivity_note: Molas are a core cultural and political identity marker of Guna women; avoid commercial copying of specific designs.
styles.short_de: Textilfelder aus mehreren Baumwolllagen in umgekehrter Applikation, jede Form von farbigen Konturbändern umfasst; genäht von Guna-Frauen in Panama seit dem späten 19. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Textile panels of layered cotton cut away in reverse appliqué, each shape echoed by coloured contour bands, sewn by Guna women of Panama since the late 19th century.
styles.era_de: seit dem späten 19. Jh., Panama und Kolumbien (Guna)
styles.era_en: since the late 19th c., Panama and Colombia (Guna)
markers_en: shapes echoed by parallel contour bands
styles.sensitivity_de: Molas sind ein zentrales kulturelles und politisches Identitätszeichen der Guna-Frauen; einzelne Entwürfe nicht kommerziell kopieren.
styles.sensitivity_en: Molas are a core cultural and political identity marker of Guna women; do not copy specific designs commercially.

styles.era_origin: Haiti, internationally recognised from 1944 with the Centre d'Art in Port-au-Prince.
visual_markers: crowded scenes stacked up the canvas
hills patterned with individually painted leaves and palms
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Haitian naive painting: brilliant tropical colours in oil or acrylic, crowded scenes stacked up the canvas with no true perspective, rolling hills patterned with individually painted leaves and palms, small busy figures with simple features, lush foliage and fruit repeated as filler, flat bright sky
styles.avoid: Avoid generic Western naïve art and children's-book art; Haitian painting is lush, dense and saturated.
styles.feasibility_note: Naive density works; may overlap with generic naïve art.
styles.sensitivity_note: Some works depict Vodou lwa (spirits); respect sacred iconography.
styles.short_de: Dicht gedrängte Szenen in leuchtenden Tropenfarben, Hügel aus einzeln gemalten Blättern, kleine geschäftige Figuren ohne echte Perspektive; Haiti, international bekannt seit Gründung des Centre d'Art 1944.
styles.short_en: Crowded scenes in brilliant tropical colours, hills of individually painted leaves and small busy figures stacked up the canvas; Haiti, internationally known since the Centre d'Art of 1944.
markers_de: Hügel aus einzeln gemalten Blättern und Palmen
markers_en: crowded scenes stacked up the canvas
hills of individually painted leaves and palms
styles.sensitivity_de: Manche Bilder zeigen Vodou-Geister (Lwa); diese sakrale Ikonografie respektvoll behandeln.
styles.sensitivity_en: Some works depict Vodou lwa (spirits); treat this sacred iconography with respect.

styles.era_origin: Northeast Brazil, chapbook covers from the early 20th c., flourishing mid-century.
visual_markers: bold naive figures with simple faces
parallel gouge strokes for sky and ground
woodgrain and uneven ink on cheap paper
styles.prompt_fragment: as a northeastern Brazilian cordel woodcut: stark black-and-white relief print from a hand-gouged block, bold naive figures with simple faces, cacti, sun rays and sky rendered with parallel gouge strokes, thick black framing border, visible woodgrain and uneven ink density on cheap off-white paper, chapbook cover proportions
styles.avoid: Avoid German Expressionist angst and smooth vector; cordel is folk, humorous and naive.
styles.feasibility_note: Relief-print look is reliable.
styles.short_de: Harte Schwarzweiß-Holzschnitte mit naiven Figuren, Kakteen und Sonnenstrahlen in parallelen Hohleisenspuren, als Titelbilder für Volksheftchen im Nordosten Brasiliens, Blüte Mitte des 20. Jahrhunderts.
styles.short_en: Stark black-and-white woodcuts with naive figures, cacti and sun rays cut in parallel gouge strokes, made as covers for chapbooks in northeastern Brazil, flourishing in the mid-20th century.
styles.era_de: seit dem frühen 20. Jh., Blüte um die Jahrhundertmitte, Nordostbrasilien
styles.era_en: early 20th c. onwards, peak mid-century, northeastern Brazil
markers_de: parallele Hohleisenspuren für Himmel und Boden
markers_en: parallel gouge strokes for sky and ground

styles.era_origin: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast (Haida, Tlingit, Tsimshian and others); the term 'formline' was coined in 1965.
visual_markers: red secondary and blue-green tertiary areas
styles.prompt_fragment: designed in Northwest Coast formline: a continuous swelling-and-tapering black primary formline built of ovoids, U-forms and split U-forms, red secondary formlines, blue-green tertiary areas, the subject split and folded symmetrically to fill the space, rounded rectangular boundaries, carved-and-painted cedar or printed paper texture
styles.avoid: Avoid generic 'tribal tattoo' shapes; formline has a strict grammar of ovoids and controlled line swelling.
styles.feasibility_note: Only a superficial imitation; ovoid placement and line-junction grammar are usually wrong.
styles.sensitivity_note: HIGH: crests and creatures are inherited clan property; serious concern about appropriation and fake 'Native art' markets. Show only with clear labelling as AI study, or omit.
styles.verdict_reason: Confirmed. Crest figures (the animal and logo subjects this prompt targets) are inherited clan property of living Haida, Tlingit and Tsimshian lineages, so this counts as community-owned. Non-Native 'formline' imitation is a long-running dispute and is marketed as fake Native art. The entry's own sensitivity note already says 'or omit'. Keep it as information without a prompt.
styles.short_de: Gestaltungssystem aus durchgehenden, an- und abschwellenden schwarzen Linien, Ovoiden und U-Formen mit roten und blaugrünen Nebenflächen, verwendet von Haida, Tlingit, Tsimshian und anderen Völkern der Nordwestküste.
styles.short_en: Design system of continuous swelling black lines, ovoids and U-forms with red and blue-green secondary areas, used by Haida, Tlingit, Tsimshian and other Northwest Coast nations.
styles.era_de: jahrhundertealt, pazifische Nordwestküste (Kanada, Alaska); Begriff seit 1965
styles.era_en: centuries-old, Pacific Northwest Coast (Canada, Alaska); term coined 1965
styles.sensitivity_de: Wappen und Wesen sind ererbtes Clan-Eigentum, gefälschte „Native Art“ ist ein ernstes Problem; deshalb gibt es keinen Prompt.
styles.sensitivity_en: Crests and creatures are inherited clan property and fake 'Native art' is a serious problem, so no prompt is offered.

styles.era_origin: Plains peoples (Lakota, Cheyenne, Kiowa and others), c. 1860s-1900, drawn on ruled account books.
visual_markers: antique ruled ledger page with faded handwritten entries
flat profile figures and elongated horses
styles.prompt_fragment: drawn as Plains ledger art: coloured pencil, crayon and ink on a page of an antique ruled accounting ledger with faded handwritten entries and columns showing through, figures and horses in flat profile with elongated bodies, flat colours with simple outlines, little or no ground line, action read across the page
styles.avoid: Avoid Western sketchbook drawing and stereotypes like headdresses everywhere.
styles.feasibility_note: Ledger paper background renders well; figure conventions vary.
styles.sensitivity_note: Tied to Native resistance and imprisonment history; a living art form of Plains artists; high risk of stereotyping and appropriation.
styles.short_de: Flache Profilzeichnungen von Reitern, Pferden und Kämpfen in Buntstift und Tinte auf linierten Kontobuchseiten, geschaffen von Künstlern der Plains-Völker von den 1860er- bis in die 1920er-Jahre.
styles.short_en: Flat profile drawings of riders, horses and battles in coloured pencil and ink on ruled account-book pages, made by Plains artists from the 1860s to the 1920s.
styles.era_de: 1860er–1920er, Great Plains, USA; Wiederbelebung seit den 1960er/70ern
styles.era_en: 1860s–1920s, Great Plains, USA; revival since the 1960s–70s
markers_de: Handlung liest sich quer über die Seite
markers_en: ruled ledger page with faded entries
styles.sensitivity_de: Verbunden mit Widerstand und Gefangenschaft indigener Völker und bis heute von Plains-Künstlern gepflegt; hohes Risiko von Klischees und Aneignung.
styles.sensitivity_en: Tied to Native resistance and imprisonment history and still practised by Plains artists; high risk of stereotyping and appropriation.

styles.era_origin: Kinngait (Cape Dorset), Nunavut, Canada, annual print collections since 1959.
visual_markers: bold flat silhouettes with simple curves

styles.prompt_fragment: as an Aboriginal Western Desert-style acrylic dot painting: an aerial, map-like composition of concentric circles connected by meandering tracks, U-shaped marks, every area filled with dense hand-placed dots in ochre red, yellow, white, black and brown on dark canvas, slight variation in dot size and spacing

styles.sensitivity_note: HIGH: designs encode sacred, sometimes restricted knowledge (Tjukurpa/Dreaming) owned by specific families; non-Indigenous imitation is widely seen as appropriation and fake Aboriginal art is a serious issue in Australia. Use only as a clearly labelled non-commercial study, or omit.
styles.verdict_reason: Confirmed. This is the clearest community-owned case: the right to paint a Tjukurpa story belongs to particular kin, some designs are restricted, and fake Aboriginal art is a well-documented problem in Australia. A paste-on prompt produces exactly the outsider imitation that communities object to. Keep it as information only.

styles.avoid: Avoid polished medieval-fantasy illustration, neat colour fills inside the lines and the dense hatching of later Renaissance woodcuts.
styles.feasibility_note: Wash spill and gothic stiffness come through well; blackletter captions often garble, so keep text minimal or omit.
styles.sensitivity_note: Historic broadsides of this kind often carried religious polemic, including antisemitic imagery; do not reproduce such content.
styles.short_de: Spätgotischer Holzschnitt mit dicken Umrisslinien und naiver Perspektive, von Hand flüchtig koloriert; Andachtsbilder, Blockbücher und Frühdrucke aus Süddeutschland und den Niederlanden, um 1420–1520.
styles.short_en: Late-Gothic woodcut with thick outlines and naive perspective, loosely coloured by hand; devotional sheets and blockbooks from southern Germany and the Low Countries, c. 1420–1520.
styles.era_en: c. 1420–1520, southern Germany and Low Countries
markers_de: lockere Lasuren, die über die Linien laufen
naive, flache Perspektive, steife gotische Proportionen
markers_en: naive flat perspective, stiff gothic proportions
styles.sensitivity_de: Einblattdrucke dieser Art transportierten oft religiöse Polemik, auch antijüdische Bildmotive; solche Inhalte nicht reproduzieren.
styles.sensitivity_en: Such broadsides often carried religious polemic, including antisemitic imagery; do not reproduce such content.

styles.era_origin: Germany and Italy c. 1508–1530s, printing several tone blocks to imitate wash drawings heightened with white.
visual_markers: black key block plus two or three tone blocks
single muted hue family (olive, sepia, slate blue)
highlights cut out so bare paper reads as white heightening
flat tone steps, no smooth gradients
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Renaissance chiaroscuro woodcut: a black key block combined with two or three overlapping tone blocks in one muted hue family such as olive green, sepia or slate blue, highlights carved out so bare paper reads as white heightening, imitating a wash drawing on tinted paper, slight registration offsets, soft block-printed ink.
styles.avoid: Avoid full-colour palettes and photographic shading; keep one hue family and flat stepped tones rather than smooth gradients.
styles.feasibility_note: Monochrome tone layering works, but the model often blends the steps into smooth gradients; ask explicitly for flat tone blocks.
styles.short_de: Holzschnitt aus Strichstock und zwei bis drei Tonstöcken in einer gedämpften Farbe, der lavierte, weiß gehöhte Zeichnungen nachahmt; ab 1508 in Deutschland und Italien.
styles.short_en: Woodcut printed from a key block plus two or three tone blocks in one muted hue, imitating wash drawings heightened with white; from 1508 in Germany and Italy.
styles.era_de: ca. 1508 bis um 1600, Deutschland, Italien, Niederlande
markers_de: schwarzer Strichstock plus zwei, drei Tonstöcke
markers_en: black key block plus two or three tone blocks
one muted hue family (olive, sepia, slate blue)
cut-out highlights reading as white heightening

styles.era_origin: Provincetown, Massachusetts, from c. 1915: one block with grooves separating areas, each painted with watercolour and printed by hand.
visual_markers: thin white uninked grooves separating every colour area
soft, blotchy watercolour-like colour inside shapes
muted sage, rust, dusty blue and ochre on cream paper
styles.prompt_fragment: as a white-line woodcut in the Provincetown tradition: every shape separated by a thin uninked white groove, colours brushed onto the block like watercolour and printed area by area so each patch is soft, uneven and slightly blotchy, subtle wood grain, muted sage, rust, dusty blue and ochre on cream paper.
styles.avoid: Avoid black outlines and flat opaque fills; the separating lines must be bare paper, or it turns into cloisonné-style illustration.
styles.feasibility_note: White separation lines usually appear, but the model may add black outlines or make the colour too even.
styles.short_de: Farbholzschnitt von nur einem Stock, dessen Farbfelder durch weiße Rillen getrennt sind und einzeln mit Aquarellfarbe eingefärbt und gedruckt werden; Provincetown, Massachusetts, ab 1915.
styles.short_en: Colour woodcut printed from a single block whose areas are separated by white grooves, each inked with watercolour and printed by hand; Provincetown, Massachusetts, from 1915.
markers_de: dünne weiße Rillen zwischen allen Farbflächen
weiche, fleckige Aquarellfarbe in den Formen
gedämpftes Salbei, Rost, Taubenblau, Ocker auf Creme
markers_en: thin white grooves between all colour areas
muted sage, rust, dusty blue, ochre on cream

styles.era_origin: Linoleum adopted for artistic relief prints c. 1905 and spread widely through art education from the 1920s.
visual_markers: bold simplified shapes cut with U- and V-gouges
flat ink with fine speckle and thin brayer spots
rhythmic gouge-mark texture, no wood grain
one or two colours on heavy paper
styles.prompt_fragment: as a hand-pulled linocut print: bold simplified shapes cut with U- and V-gouges, crisp but slightly wobbly edges, flat ink areas with fine speckle and thin spots from the brayer, rhythmic gouge-mark texture in the background, no wood grain, one or two colours on heavy off-white printmaking paper.
styles.avoid: Avoid perfectly clean vector shapes and uniform 'linocut filter' texture; keep visible chatter marks and ink irregularities.
styles.feasibility_note: Rendered convincingly; main risk is over-clean, vector-like edges.
styles.short_de: Hochdruck von einer Linoleumplatte mit vereinfachten, kräftigen Formen und sichtbaren Hohleisenspuren, seit etwa 1905 künstlerisch genutzt und ab den 1920ern im Kunstunterricht verbreitet.
styles.short_en: Relief print cut into linoleum, with bold simplified shapes and visible gouge marks; used by artists from about 1905 and widespread in art education from the 1920s.
markers_de: kräftige vereinfachte Formen, mit U- und V-Eisen geschnitten
flache Farbe mit feinen Sprenkeln und Walzenlücken
ein bis zwei Farben auf schwerem Papier
markers_en: bold simplified shapes cut with U- and V-gouges
flat ink with fine speckle and brayer gaps
rhythmic gouge marks, no wood grain
one or two colours on heavy paper

styles.era_origin: Printing several colours from one progressively cut block, popularised in the 1950s and now common in contemporary printmaking.
visual_markers: five to seven stacked opaque colour layers, light to dark
glossy ink buildup in darkest layer
limited harmonious palette, pencil edition in margin
styles.prompt_fragment: as a multi-layer reduction linocut: five to seven opaque colours printed light to dark from a single progressively carved block, each layer leaving slightly offset edges and pale halos, gouge-mark texture in every colour, thick glossy ink buildup in the darkest layer, limited harmonious palette, paper margin with pencil edition number.
styles.avoid: Avoid smooth gradients and painterly blending; transitions must be hard-edged stacked layers, not vector illustration with drop shadows.
styles.feasibility_note: Layering reads well; the model may smooth layers into digital shading or lose the gouge texture.
styles.short_de: Mehrfarbiger Linolschnitt von einer einzigen Platte, die nach jedem Farbgang weiter ausgeschnitten wird, gedruckt von hell nach dunkel; seit den 1950er-Jahren verbreitet.
styles.short_en: Multicolour linocut printed from a single block that is cut further after each colour, printed from light to dark; widely practised since the 1950s.
markers_de: fünf bis sieben deckende Farbschichten von hell nach dunkel
harte Kanten mit leicht versetzten Lichthöfen
glänzender Farbauftrag in der dunkelsten Schicht
markers_en: five to seven opaque layers, light to dark
glossy ink buildup in darkest layer

styles.era_origin: Mexico's Taller de Gráfica Popular (founded 1937) and international leftist print collectives of the 1930s–70s, continued in protest printmaking.
visual_markers: dense parallel gouge hatching modelling heavy forms
dramatic low viewpoint and diagonal movement
black on cheap cream paper, occasional red accent
hand-carved block lettering in a banner
styles.prompt_fragment: as a mid-century social-realist linocut: dense parallel gouge hatching modelling heavy, monumental forms, dramatic low viewpoint and diagonal movement, strong black on cheap cream newsprint-weight paper, occasional single flat red accent, hand-carved block lettering integrated in a banner, ink pressure uneven at the edges.
styles.avoid: Avoid slick propaganda-poster gloss and heroic digital rendering; keep the carved, hatched, hand-printed roughness.
styles.feasibility_note: Hatching and composition are reliable; carved lettering may garble on long slogans.
styles.sensitivity_note: Strong political and protest connotations (labour, leftist, anti-fascist); choose slogans with care and avoid imitating identifiable historical posters.
styles.short_de: Schwarzer Linolschnitt mit dichten Schraffuren, wuchtigen Figuren und Schriftband, geprägt von Mexikos Taller de Gráfica Popular (ab 1937) und linken Druckkollektiven bis in die 1970er.
styles.short_en: Black linocut with dense gouge hatching, monumental figures and carved lettering, shaped by Mexico's Taller de Gráfica Popular (founded 1937) and leftist print collectives into the 1970s.
markers_de: dichte parallele Schraffuren modellieren wuchtige Formen
Schwarz auf billigem Cremepapier, gelegentlich Rot
markers_en: dense parallel gouge hatching on heavy forms
black on cheap cream paper, occasional red
hand-carved block lettering in a banner
styles.sensitivity_de: Stark politisch und mit Protest verbunden (Arbeiterbewegung, Linke, Antifaschismus); Parolen mit Bedacht wählen und keine bekannten historischen Plakate nachahmen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Strong political and protest connotations (labour, left, anti-fascist); choose slogans with care and avoid imitating identifiable historical posters.

styles.era_origin: Developed in England by the 1790s; the dominant illustration method for 19th-century books and illustrated newspapers until c. 1890.
visual_markers: image built from fine white lines cut into black
tonal tints of closely spaced parallel lines
crisp miniature detail, no wood grain
black letterpress ink on smooth cream book paper
styles.prompt_fragment: as a 19th-century end-grain wood engraving: image built from extremely fine white lines cut into black, tonal tint areas of closely spaced parallel and curving lines, crisp miniature detail with no visible wood grain, soft vignetted edges fading into the page, printed in black letterpress ink on smooth cream book paper.
styles.avoid: Avoid coarse woodcut chunkiness and cross-hatched pen drawing; tones must come from engraved white lines, not stipple or grey wash.
styles.feasibility_note: General look is reliable; very fine tint lines often turn into noise or ordinary pen hatching.
styles.short_de: Hochdruck vom Hirnholz, bei dem feinste weiße Linien in schwarze Flächen gestochen werden; ab den 1790ern in England, im 19. Jahrhundert Standard für Buch- und Zeitungsillustration.
styles.short_en: Relief print cut into end-grain boxwood, with fine white lines in black; developed in England by the 1790s, standard for 19th-century book and newspaper illustration.
markers_de: Bild aus feinen weißen Linien in Schwarz
markers_en: image of fine white lines cut into black
tonal tints of dense parallel lines
crisp miniature detail, no wood grain
black ink on smooth cream book paper

styles.era_origin: 18th–19th-century mass-produced popular prints from Épinal, Neuruppin and Russia (lubki), with woodcut or litho outlines coloured by stencil.
visual_markers: simple outlined figures in rows or numbered panels
bright stencil colour dabbed off the outlines
captions or rhymed verse under each scene
cheap thin paper with folds and age spots
styles.prompt_fragment: as a 19th-century popular broadsheet print: simple black outlined figures arranged in rows or numbered panels, bright stencilled colour in red, ultramarine, yellow and green dabbed slightly outside the lines, short printed captions or rhymed verse under each scene, naive cheerful drawing, cheap thin rag paper with folds and age spots.
styles.avoid: Avoid modern comic-strip polish, speech bubbles and smooth digital colouring; colour must sit loosely over the outlines.
styles.feasibility_note: Panel layout and stencil colour work; captions may come out as pseudo-text.
styles.sensitivity_note: Historic sheets often contained nationalist, militarist or ethnic caricature; do not reproduce such content.
styles.short_de: Billige Einblattdrucke mit einfach umrissenen Figuren in Bildreihen, schablonenkoloriert und mit Versen darunter, im 18. und 19. Jahrhundert aus Épinal, Neuruppin und Russland.
styles.short_en: Cheap single-sheet prints with simply outlined figures in rows of scenes, stencil-coloured with verses beneath, produced in the 18th and 19th centuries in Épinal, Neuruppin and Russia.
markers_de: einfache Umrissfiguren in Reihen oder nummerierten Feldern
dünnes billiges Papier mit Falten und Stockflecken
markers_en: simple outlined figures in rows or numbered panels
bright stencil colour off the outlines
captions or rhymed verse under scenes
cheap thin paper with folds and foxing
styles.sensitivity_de: Historische Bogen enthielten oft nationalistische, militaristische oder ethnische Karikaturen; solche Inhalte nicht reproduzieren.
styles.sensitivity_en: Historic sheets often carried nationalist, militarist or ethnic caricature; do not reproduce such content.

styles.era_origin: Vulcanised rubber stamps from the 1860s; office and postal use, then 1970s–80s mail art and craft stamping.
visual_markers: partly missing edges and a rocked ghost double
violet, red or black stamp-pad ink
styles.prompt_fragment: as rubber-stamp impressions on paper: simple outlined motifs pressed by hand with uneven pressure, blotchy patchy ink coverage, partly missing edges and a faint doubled ghost where the stamp rocked, slightly fuzzy outlines, stamp-pad ink in violet, red or black, repeated and rotated impressions overlapping freely on uncoated paper.
styles.avoid: Avoid crisp, evenly filled shapes and grunge texture overlays; irregularity must come from pressure and ink.
styles.feasibility_note: Ink irregularity renders, but impressions are often too perfect; complex subjects lose the stamp feel.
styles.sensitivity_note: Avoid imitating official seals, notary or customs stamps.
styles.short_de: Von Hand gesetzte Gummistempelabdrucke mit fleckiger Farbe, ausgebrochenen Rändern und verwackelten Doppelkonturen; Büro- und Poststempel seit den 1860ern, später Mail Art und Bastelstempel.
styles.short_en: Hand-pressed rubber-stamp impressions with patchy ink, missing edges and rocked double outlines; office and postal stamps since the 1860s, later mail art and craft stamping.
markers_de: Stempelfarbe in Violett, Rot oder Schwarz
markers_en: missing edges and rocked ghost double
violet, red or black stamp-pad ink
styles.sensitivity_de: Keine amtlichen Siegel, Notar- oder Zollstempel nachahmen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Do not imitate official seals, notary or customs stamps.

styles.era_origin: Movable type since the 1450s; the deep 'bite' into soft cotton paper is a 2000s revival aesthetic.
visual_markers: type and line art pressed into a visible debossed channel
slight ink gain and speckle in solids
one or two flat spot colours
raking light showing paper fibre and impression depth
styles.prompt_fragment: as letterpress printing on thick soft cotton paper: type and line art pressed deeply so they sit in a visible debossed channel, darker ink squeeze at the edges, slight ink gain and speckle on solids, one or two flat spot colours, raking side light revealing the impression depth and paper fibres.
styles.avoid: Avoid glossy stationery-mockup renders with fake drop shadows; the impression and ink texture must look physical.
styles.feasibility_note: Deboss renders well; easily slides into stock-mockup polish.
styles.short_de: Buchdruck, dessen Lettern und Klischees tief in weiches Baumwollpapier gepresst werden; die Technik gibt es seit den 1450ern, die fühlbar tiefe Prägung ist ein Revival der 2000er.
styles.short_en: Letterpress printing with type and plates pressed deep into soft cotton paper; the technique dates from the 1450s, the tactile deep impression is a 2000s revival look.
styles.era_de: seit den 1450ern; tiefe Prägung seit den 2000ern
markers_de: Schrift und Strich in sichtbar vertiefter Prägung
leichte Tonwertzunahme und Sprenkel in Vollflächen
markers_en: type and line art in a visible debossed channel
slight ink gain and speckle in solids
one or two flat spot colours
raking light showing fibre and impression depth

styles.era_origin: Centuries-old South and Central Asian textile tradition (Sanganer, Bagru, Ajrakh) and European Modeldruck from the late Middle Ages.
visual_markers: repeated stamped motif with misaligned joins
separate outline and fill blocks slightly off register
natural dyes: madder red, indigo, iron black, turmeric
styles.prompt_fragment: as hand block printing on cotton fabric: a carved motif stamped in repeated rows with slight misalignment and gaps at the joins, separate blocks for outline and fill so colours shift a hair off register, natural-dye palette of madder red, indigo, iron black and turmeric, uneven saturation soaking into visible woven fabric texture.
styles.avoid: Avoid seamless digital repeats and crisp vector florals; the repeat must show human misalignment and textile absorption.
styles.feasibility_note: Pattern and textile texture are reliable; misalignment may need emphasis.
styles.sensitivity_note: Several Indian block-print traditions (e.g. Sanganeri, Bagru) are protected Geographical Indications; don't label generated designs as authentic artisan work.
styles.short_de: Stoffdruck mit geschnitzten Holzmodeln, deren Rapport leicht versetzt aneinanderstößt, oft mit Naturfarben; in Indien und Zentralasien seit Jahrhunderten, in Europa seit dem Spätmittelalter.
styles.short_en: Fabric stamped with carved wooden blocks in slightly misaligned repeats and natural dyes; centuries old in South and Central Asia, in Europe since the late Middle Ages.
styles.era_de: seit Jahrhunderten in Süd- und Zentralasien; Europa seit dem Spätmittelalter
styles.era_en: centuries-old in South and Central Asia; Europe since the late Middle Ages
markers_de: Kontur- und Füllmodel leicht außer Passer
markers_en: repeated stamped motif with misaligned joins
outline and fill blocks slightly off register
natural dyes: madder, indigo, iron black, turmeric
styles.sensitivity_de: Mehrere indische Handdrucktraditionen (z. B. Sanganeri, Bagru) sind geschützte geografische Angaben; generierte Entwürfe nicht als echte Handwerksarbeit ausgeben.
styles.sensitivity_en: Several Indian block-print traditions (e.g. Sanganeri, Bagru) are protected Geographical Indications; do not present generated designs as authentic artisan work.

styles.era_origin: Central Europe from the 17th century: resist paste printed with wood and metal-pin blocks, then dyed in indigo (UNESCO intangible heritage since 2018).
visual_markers: white and pale-blue motifs on deep indigo
fine dotted fills from metal pins
small repeats with tiny registration jumps
faint bleed and crackle at shape edges
linen weave and uneven indigo depth
styles.prompt_fragment: as Central European indigo resist printing (Blaudruck): crisp white and pale-blue motifs reserved against deep, slightly uneven indigo cloth, fine dotted fills from metal pins set in the wooden block, small repeat with tiny registration jumps, faint bleed and crackle at shape edges, visible linen weave, folk-ornamental stylisation.
styles.avoid: Avoid blue-and-white porcelain or batik wax-crackle looks; this is crisp block-printed paste resist with pin-dot detail.
styles.feasibility_note: Indigo-and-white pattern is easy; pin-dot fills and resist crackle need emphasis and may drift toward batik.
styles.short_de: Weiße und hellblaue Muster auf tiefblauem Stoff: Mit Holz- und Messingstiftmodeln wird eine farbabweisende Masse (Papp) aufgedruckt, dann in Indigo gefärbt; Mitteleuropa seit dem 17. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: White and pale-blue patterns on deep indigo cloth: a resist paste is printed with wooden and metal-pin blocks before dyeing; Central Europe since the 17th century.
markers_de: weiße und hellblaue Motive auf tiefem Indigo
leichtes Auslaufen und Craquelé an den Kanten
markers_en: white and pale-blue motifs on deep indigo
fine dotted fills from metal pins
small repeat with tiny registration jumps
faint bleed and crackle at edges

styles.era_origin: Europe from c. 1430, at its peak in the 16th–18th centuries for art prints, maps, scientific plates and portraits.
visual_markers: burin lines that swell and taper
systematic parallel and cross-hatching following contours
embossed plate mark on laid paper
