styles.prompt_fragment: as a copperplate line engraving: crisp burin lines that swell and taper, form modelled by disciplined parallel and cross-hatching that follows the contours, dot-and-lozenge fills in mid-tones, no wash or grey tone, rich black ink slightly raised on cream laid paper, embossed rectangular plate mark around the image.
styles.avoid: Avoid sketchy pen hatching and the free wandering line of etching; lines must look cut, regular and systematic.
styles.feasibility_note: Overall look is strong; true swelling burin lines and clean cross-hatch systems often degrade into noisy pen hatching.
styles.short_de: Tiefdruck von einer mit dem Grabstichel gestochenen Kupferplatte, Formen aus an- und abschwellenden Linien und Kreuzschraffur; in Europa seit etwa 1430, Blüte im 16. bis 18. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Intaglio print from a copper plate cut with a burin, forms built from swelling and tapering lines and cross-hatching; Europe from about 1430, peaking in the 16th–18th centuries.
markers_de: systematische Parallel- und Kreuzschraffur entlang der Form
markers_en: burin lines that swell and taper
systematic parallel and cross-hatching along contours
embossed plate mark on laid paper

styles.era_origin: c. 1820–1880, when hardened steel plates allowed long print runs of topographical views, annuals and book illustrations.
visual_markers: extremely fine dense lines giving silvery greys
image vignetting into the page without border
styles.prompt_fragment: as a 19th-century steel engraving: extremely fine, densely ruled lines producing silvery mid-grey tones and atmospheric skies, meticulous miniature detail, image vignetting softly into the page without a border, small engraved title in elegant script beneath, light even printing on smooth bright paper with faint foxing.
styles.avoid: Avoid the bold contrast and heavy blacks of copperplate or woodcut; the impression should be delicate and grey, not dramatic.
styles.feasibility_note: Fine-line density is only approximated; ruled skies may turn into smooth grey.
styles.short_de: Stich in gehärtete Stahlplatten mit extrem feinen, dichten Linien und silbrigen Grautönen, um 1820–1880 für Veduten, Almanache und Buchillustrationen in hohen Auflagen genutzt.
styles.short_en: Engraving on hardened steel plates with extremely fine, dense lines and silvery greys, used c. 1820–1880 for long runs of topographical views, annuals and book illustrations.
markers_de: extrem feine, dichte Linien mit silbrigen Grautönen
randlos in die Seite auslaufende Vignette
markers_en: extremely fine dense lines, silvery greys

styles.era_origin: 17th–19th-century natural-history, botanical, fashion and atlas plates, engraved or etched and coloured by hand.
visual_markers: fine engraved line and stipple base
thin transparent watercolour with slight pooling
subject isolated on a generous cream page
plate number and small engraved caption
styles.prompt_fragment: as a hand-coloured engraved plate from an 18th–19th-century natural history or atlas volume: fine engraved line and stipple base, delicate transparent watercolour applied by hand with slight pooling and occasional spill, subject isolated on a generous cream page, plate number at the top corner, small engraved caption below, embossed plate mark and light foxing.
styles.avoid: Avoid glossy digital botanical illustration and saturated colour; colour must be a thin wash over visible engraved line.
styles.feasibility_note: A well-known vintage look; engraved line can soften into pencil, so stress 'engraved hatching'.
styles.short_de: Gestochene oder radierte Buchtafel, von Hand mit transparentem Aquarell koloriert, typisch für naturkundliche, botanische, Mode- und Atlaswerke des 17. bis 19. Jahrhunderts.
styles.short_en: Engraved or etched book plate coloured by hand with transparent watercolour, typical of 17th- to 19th-century natural history, botanical, fashion and atlas volumes.
markers_de: dünnes transparentes Aquarell mit leichten Pfützen
Motiv frei auf großzügiger cremefarbener Seite
markers_en: fine engraved line and stipple base
thin transparent watercolour with slight pooling
subject isolated on generous cream page
plate number and small engraved caption

styles.era_origin: Europe from the early 16th century, with high points in the 17th century and the 19th-century Etching Revival.
visual_markers: free, lively lines of even width
styles.prompt_fragment: as an intaglio etching: free, lively lines of even width drawn through the ground and bitten by acid, dense scribbled cross-hatching for deep shadow, open sketchy areas left blank, warm-black ink with a thin veil of plate tone, occasional foul-biting specks, embossed plate mark on heavy cream paper.
styles.avoid: Avoid rigid systematic engraving lines and digital pen hatching; lines should feel loose and spontaneous with uneven bite.
styles.feasibility_note: Very reliable; plate tone and plate mark sometimes go missing.
styles.short_de: Tiefdruck, bei dem frei in einen Ätzgrund gezeichnete Linien mit Säure geätzt werden; in Europa seit dem frühen 16. Jahrhundert, Höhepunkte im 17. und 19. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Intaglio print with lines drawn freely through a wax ground and bitten by acid; Europe from the early 16th century, peaking in the 17th and 19th centuries.
markers_en: free, lively lines of even width

styles.era_origin: Late 15th century onward, prized for its velvety burr by 17th-century masters and 19th–20th-century painter-printmakers.
visual_markers: lines with soft fuzzy burr halos
deep inky accents where lines cluster
plate mark on soft white paper
styles.prompt_fragment: as a drypoint print: lines scratched directly into the plate with a needle, each carrying a soft velvety burr that blooms into fuzzy dark halos, scratchy angular energy, deep inky accents where lines cluster, wiped plate tone leaving smoky veils, embossed plate mark on soft white paper.
styles.avoid: Avoid crisp clean ink lines; the defining feature is the blurred, velvety burr, not neat cross-hatching.
styles.feasibility_note: The burr halo tends to be lost; the model draws crisp lines unless 'fuzzy velvety burr' is stressed.
styles.short_de: Mit der Stahlnadel direkt in die Platte geritzte Linien, deren aufgeworfener Grat beim Druck samtig-weiche Ränder erzeugt; seit dem späten 15. Jahrhundert, beliebt bei Malerradierern.
styles.short_en: Lines scratched directly into the plate with a needle, whose raised burr prints soft, velvety edges; used since the late 15th century and favoured by painter-printmakers.
markers_en: lines with soft fuzzy burr halos
deep inky accents where lines cluster
plate mark on soft white paper

styles.era_origin: Developed in France in the 1760s, used for tonal prints, caricature and often hand-coloured topographical views through the 19th century.
visual_markers: flat stepped tone values with hard edges
deep grainy shadows against pale paper
styles.prompt_fragment: as an aquatint: tonal areas built from a fine granular resin-dust texture, flat stepped tone values with hard-edged transitions rather than smooth gradients, combined with sparse etched outline, warm sepia or brown-black ink, dramatic contrast between pale paper and deep grainy shadows, embossed plate mark.
styles.avoid: Avoid smooth airbrush gradients and photographic tone; grain and stepped values are essential.
styles.feasibility_note: Tonal mood works; the granular texture often smooths into wash or watercolour.
styles.short_de: Ätzverfahren für Flächentöne, bei dem aufgeschmolzener Harzstaub eine körnige Tonfläche erzeugt; in den 1760ern in Frankreich entwickelt, im 19. Jahrhundert verbreitet für kolorierte Ansichten.
styles.short_en: Tonal etching in which fused resin dust creates grainy tone areas; developed in France in the 1760s, much used for hand-coloured views in the 19th century.
markers_de: flache, gestufte Tonwerte mit harten Kanten
tiefe körnige Schatten vor hellem Papier
markers_en: flat stepped tones with hard edges
deep grainy shadows against pale paper

styles.era_origin: Known since the 18th century and popularised by 20th-century painter-printmakers for direct brushwork on the plate.
visual_markers: gestural brushstrokes printed as grainy aquatint
ragged dry-brush edges and pooling at stroke ends
calligraphic economy, lots of bare paper
styles.prompt_fragment: as a sugar-lift aquatint: bold gestural brushstrokes transferred to the plate and printed as grainy aquatint tone, ragged dry-brush edges and pooling at stroke ends, calligraphic economy with much bare paper, single ink of black or deep sepia, soft plate tone and embossed plate mark.
styles.avoid: Avoid an ink-wash painting look with smooth gradients; the brush marks must carry granular etched texture.
styles.feasibility_note: Usually rendered as a sumi or ink painting; the granular etched texture inside brushstrokes is hard to get.
styles.short_de: Aquatinta, bei der mit Zuckerlösung gemalte Pinselstriche ausgesprengt und als körniger Ton gedruckt werden; im 18. Jahrhundert bekannt, im 20. Jahrhundert bei Malerradierern beliebt.
styles.short_en: Aquatint in which brushstrokes painted in a sugar solution are lifted from the ground and print as grainy tone; known since the 18th century, popular with 20th-century painter-printmakers.
styles.era_en: known from the 18th c.; widespread in the 20th c.
markers_en: gestural brushstrokes printed as grainy aquatint
ragged dry-brush edges, pooling at stroke ends

styles.era_origin: Late 18th century, first to reproduce pencil and chalk drawings, later used to imprint fabrics, leaves and textures.
visual_markers: imprinted fabric, lace or leaf textures
styles.prompt_fragment: as a soft-ground etching: soft, grainy, crumbly lines that look like pencil or chalk drawn through paper onto the plate, imprinted textures of woven fabric, lace or leaves embedded in the tones, muted warm-grey ink, gentle plate tone, embossed plate mark on heavy paper.
styles.avoid: Avoid crisp etched or pen lines; everything should feel soft, granular and pressed rather than drawn.
styles.feasibility_note: Often reads as a plain pencil drawing; imprinted textures are the best handle.
styles.short_de: Radierung auf weichem, klebrigem Ätzgrund, der Bleistift- und Kreidestriche oder eingedrückte Stoffe und Blätter körnig abbildet; seit dem späten 18. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Etching on a soft, tacky ground that records pencil or chalk lines and pressed-in fabrics or leaves as grainy texture; in use since the late 18th century.
markers_de: eingedrückte Strukturen von Stoff, Spitze, Blättern
markers_en: imprinted fabric, lace or leaf textures

styles.era_origin: Invented in the 1640s in Germany and the Netherlands, dominant for reproducing portraits and paintings in 18th-century England.
visual_markers: forms emerging from velvety deep black
styles.prompt_fragment: as a mezzotint: forms emerging from a deep, velvety black ground, light burnished out in soft continuous tones, fine rocker-grain texture visible in the mid-tones, no outlines or hatching, dramatic candlelit chiaroscuro, rich warm-black ink with slight plate tone, embossed plate mark on soft cream paper.
styles.avoid: Avoid crisp linework and digital black-and-white photo looks; tone must feel granular and burnished, emerging from darkness.
styles.feasibility_note: Dark velvety tonality is reliable; rocker grain may be too faint, so mention it.
styles.short_de: Tiefdruckverfahren, bei dem Formen aus einer samtschwarz aufgerauten Platte herausgeschabt und geglättet werden; um 1642 erfunden, im England des 18. Jahrhunderts führend für Porträtreproduktionen.
styles.short_en: Intaglio process in which forms are scraped and burnished out of a plate roughened to velvety black; invented in the 1640s, dominant for reproducing portraits in 18th-century England.
markers_de: Formen tauchen aus samtigem Tiefschwarz auf

styles.era_origin: Crayon manner developed in France in the 1750s to imitate chalk drawings; stipple engraving flourished in England c. 1770–1820.
visual_markers: tones built from tiny dots and flicks
styles.prompt_fragment: as a late-18th-century stipple engraving: soft tones built entirely from clusters of tiny dots and flicks, powdery like red chalk, minimal outlines, printed in sanguine red-brown or warm sepia with delicate soft-colour touches, oval or vignetted framing, engraved title in fine script below, cream wove paper with plate mark.
styles.avoid: Avoid the coarse stipple of pen drawing and modern dotwork-tattoo style; dots should be tiny and yield soft, sentimental tone.
styles.feasibility_note: The red-chalk look comes through; microscopic dot structure becomes generic softness.
styles.short_de: Stichtechnik, die Töne aus winzigen Punkten und Strichelchen aufbaut und wie Rötel- oder Kreidezeichnung wirkt; Crayonmanier ab den 1750ern in Frankreich, Punktiermanier um 1770–1820 in England.
styles.short_en: Engraving technique building tone from tiny dots and flicks to imitate chalk drawing; crayon manner from the 1750s in France, stipple engraving c. 1770–1820 in England.
markers_de: Töne aus winzigen Punkten und Strichelchen
markers_en: tones built from tiny dots and flicks

styles.era_origin: Developed at Atelier 17 in Paris (1950s): one deeply etched plate inked with colours of different oil content and printed in one pass.
visual_markers: several colours from one deep-etched plate
iridescent teal, magenta, ochre over black lines
styles.prompt_fragment: as a viscosity intaglio print: one deeply etched textured plate printing several colours at once, different relief levels holding different inks so colours interlock and halo, iridescent teal, magenta and ochre over deep black intaglio lines, embossed relief texture, organic eroded surfaces, slightly abstracted forms.
styles.avoid: Avoid psychedelic digital gradients and glossy fluid art; colour must sit in embossed etched texture.
styles.feasibility_note: Niche technique; results drift toward generic colourful abstraction without the etched relief logic.
styles.short_de: Farbtiefdruck von einer einzigen tief geätzten Platte, die mit unterschiedlich zähflüssigen Farben eingewalzt und in einem Durchgang gedruckt wird; in den 1950ern im Pariser Atelier 17 entwickelt.
styles.short_en: Colour intaglio printed in one pass from a single deeply etched plate inked with colours of different viscosity; developed at Atelier 17 in Paris in the 1950s.
markers_de: mehrere Farben von einer tief geätzten Platte
schillerndes Petrol, Magenta, Ocker über schwarzen Linien
markers_en: several colours from one deep-etched plate
iridescent teal, magenta, ochre over black lines

styles.era_origin: Named in the US in the 1950s: plates collaged from card, fabric, sand, glue and found materials, printed intaglio or relief.
visual_markers: embossed textures of fabric, string, sand
irregular cut-shape edges and glued seams
ink caught in rough surfaces, wiped from smooth
styles.prompt_fragment: as a collagraph print: a plate collaged from card, fabric, string, sand and glue, printing as embossed tactile textures with deep blind relief, irregular cut-shape edges and visible glued seams, ink caught in rough surfaces and wiped from smooth ones, earthy muted colours with one deeper accent, heavy dampened printmaking paper.
styles.avoid: Avoid flat digital photo collage; textures must be printed impressions with embossing, not pasted images.
styles.feasibility_note: Tactile texture renders; it can tip into mixed-media collage with real objects.
styles.short_de: Druck von einer aus Karton, Stoff, Schnur, Sand und Leim collagierten Platte, die tastbare Prägestrukturen ergibt; der Begriff entstand in den 1950ern in den USA.
styles.short_en: Print from a plate collaged from card, fabric, string, sand and glue, giving tactile embossed textures; the term was coined in the USA in the 1950s.
markers_de: geprägte Strukturen von Stoff, Schnur, Sand
Farbe in rauen Partien, glatte ausgewischt
markers_en: embossed textures of fabric, string, sand
irregular cut edges and glued seams
ink caught in rough areas, wiped from smooth

styles.era_origin: 19th-century security printing combining hand-engraved vignettes with machine-turned guilloche rosettes, still used on banknotes and certificates.
visual_markers: subject in ultra-fine engraved line and dot
guilloche rosettes and interlaced wave lattices
green, steel-blue or sepia ink over rainbow underprint
styles.prompt_fragment: as security-printing intaglio engraving: subject rendered in ultra-fine engraved line and dot, framed by machine-turned guilloche rosettes, interlaced wave lattices and ornamental scrollwork, microtext border lines, monochrome ink in banknote green, steel blue or sepia over a faint multicolour rainbow underprint, crisp raised-ink sharpness on cotton paper.
styles.avoid: Avoid any real currency layout, denominations, national emblems or serial numbers, and avoid generic money clip-art.
styles.feasibility_note: Guilloche looks convincing at a glance but is rarely geometrically exact; the model may refuse or soften anything that resembles real currency.
styles.sensitivity_note: Counterfeiting law: never imitate real banknotes, securities or currency layouts; keep designs clearly fictional.
styles.short_de: Wertpapier-Tiefdruck mit fein gestochenen Vignetten, maschinell gezogenen Guilloche-Rosetten und Mikroschrift, seit dem 19. Jahrhundert für Banknoten, Aktien und Urkunden.
styles.short_en: Security intaglio combining finely engraved vignettes with machine-turned guilloche rosettes and microtext, used since the 19th century on banknotes, share certificates and documents.
markers_de: Motiv in hauchfeinen Stichlinien und Punkten
Grün, Stahlblau oder Sepia über Irisunterdruck
markers_en: subject in ultra-fine engraved line and dot
guilloche rosettes and interlaced wave lattices
green, steel blue or sepia over rainbow underprint
styles.sensitivity_de: Fälschungsrecht beachten: keine echten Banknoten, Wertpapiere oder Währungslayouts nachahmen, Entwürfe klar fiktiv halten.
styles.sensitivity_en: Counterfeiting law: never imitate real banknotes, securities or currency layouts; keep designs clearly fictional.

styles.era_origin: Since the first adhesive postage stamps of 1840; recess-engraved stamps were valued throughout the 20th century.
visual_markers: miniature vignette in fine engraved line
one or two inks (carmine, ultramarine, bottle green)
styles.prompt_fragment: as a recess-engraved postage stamp: miniature vignette in fine engraved line and dot, single or two-colour ink such as carmine, ultramarine or bottle green, ornamental frame with small value numeral and fictitious lettering, perforated serrated edges on white gummed paper, optional partial wavy postmark cancellation, slight ink squeeze.
styles.avoid: Avoid flat vector stamp illustrations and modern photo stamps; avoid real country names, monarchs or postal emblems.
styles.feasibility_note: Format with perforations is reliable; fine engraving at stamp scale becomes soft.
styles.sensitivity_note: Do not imitate real postal authorities, valid postage or national emblems.
styles.short_de: Briefmarke im Stichtiefdruck mit winziger, fein gestochener Bildvignette, Ornamentrahmen und Zähnung; seit der ersten Marke 1840 und das ganze 20. Jahrhundert hindurch geschätzt.
styles.short_en: Recess-printed postage stamp with a tiny, finely engraved vignette, ornamental frame and perforations; used since the first stamp of 1840 and prized throughout the 20th century.
markers_de: ein bis zwei Farben (Karmin, Ultramarin, Flaschengrün)
markers_en: miniature vignette in fine engraved line
one or two inks (carmine, ultramarine, bottle green)
styles.sensitivity_de: Keine echten Postverwaltungen, gültigen Wertzeichen oder Hoheitszeichen nachahmen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Do not imitate real postal authorities, valid postage or national emblems.

styles.era_origin: Copperplate-printed cottons from the 1750s in Ireland and England, and from 1760 at Jouy-en-Josas, France.
visual_markers: one ink colour (madder red, indigo, sepia) on cream
engraved scenes arranged as scattered islands
fine engraved line and hatching, fabric weave
styles.prompt_fragment: as a toile de Jouy pattern: finely engraved monochrome vignettes in a single ink of madder red, indigo blue or sepia on cream cotton, scenes arranged as scattered islands framed by trees and foliage and repeated in a large half-drop pattern, crisp copperplate line and hatching, faint fabric weave texture.
styles.avoid: Avoid multicolour fills and modern flat-vector toile; strictly one ink with engraved line detail.
styles.feasibility_note: Well-known pattern; repeat seams are not truly tileable.
styles.short_de: Einfarbig mit Kupferplatten bedruckte Baumwollstoffe mit ländlichen Szenen in Laubinseln, ab den 1750ern in Irland und England, ab 1760 in Jouy-en-Josas bei Versailles.
styles.short_en: Single-colour copperplate-printed cottons with pastoral scenes set in islands of foliage, from the 1750s in Ireland and England and from 1760 at Jouy-en-Josas near Versailles.
markers_de: eine Farbe (Krapprot, Indigo, Sepia) auf Creme
Bäume und Laub rahmen jede Vignette
markers_en: one ink (madder red, indigo, sepia) on cream

styles.era_origin: Ancient seal impressions, refined in Japanese karazuri and Western stationery, bookbinding and 20th-century inkless intaglio.
visual_markers: forms read only through raking-light shadow
fibrous cotton paper with wide margins
styles.prompt_fragment: as blind embossing: forms pressed into thick white cotton paper with no ink at all, readable only through soft shadows and highlights of a low raking light, crisp raised and debossed edges, subtle multilevel relief, white-on-white minimalism, fibrous paper surface, generous empty margins.
styles.avoid: Avoid 3D-rendered plastic or clay; it must look like paper fibres stretched over a die, not a CGI bas-relief.
styles.feasibility_note: Raking-light emboss renders well; it can drift toward plaster or CGI relief.
styles.short_de: Farblose Prägung in dickes Papier, deren Formen nur durch Licht und Schatten sichtbar werden; von antiken Siegeln über japanisches Karazuri bis zu Buchbinderei und Druckgrafik.
styles.short_en: Inkless relief pressed into thick paper, its forms visible only through light and shadow; from ancient seals and Japanese karazuri to stationery, bookbinding and printmaking.
styles.era_de: seit der Antike; Japan (Karazuri), westliche Buchkunst und Druckgrafik
styles.era_en: since antiquity; Japan (karazuri), Western bookbinding and printmaking
markers_de: Weiß auf Weiß, ganz ohne Farbe
markers_en: forms readable only in raking-light shadow
fibrous cotton paper with wide margins

styles.era_origin: Industrial hot-foil stamping on book covers from the late 19th century, now ubiquitous on premium packaging and stationery.
visual_markers: gold, copper or silver foil with mirror reflections
tiny breaks and flaking in thin lines
styles.prompt_fragment: as hot-foil stamping on dark uncoated board: line art and lettering in gold, copper or silver metallic foil pressed into a slight deboss, mirror-like reflections that shift across the surface, tiny breaks and flaking where thin lines failed to transfer, fibrous matte paper contrasting with metallic shine, photographed under angled light.
styles.avoid: Avoid the shiny CGI 'luxury gold' look with lens flares; foil should show physical imperfections and sit flush in the paper.
styles.feasibility_note: Easy to get; hard to keep it from looking like a glossy stock mockup.
styles.short_de: Metallfolie in Gold, Kupfer oder Silber, die mit einem beheizten Prägestempel leicht vertieft auf Karton übertragen wird; seit dem späten 19. Jahrhundert, heute verbreitet auf hochwertigen Verpackungen.
styles.short_en: Gold, copper or silver foil transferred onto board with a heated die, leaving a slight deboss; in use since the late 19th century, now common on upscale packaging.
markers_de: Gold-, Kupfer- oder Silberfolie mit Spiegelreflexen
markers_en: gold, copper or silver foil with mirror reflections
tiny breaks and flaking in thin lines

styles.era_origin: Invented by Alois Senefelder in Munich c. 1796–98; used for 19th-century prints, caricature and sheet music, and still practised by artists.
visual_markers: grainy litho-crayon tone catching stone grain
highlights scratched out with a blade
rich warm black on smooth paper
styles.prompt_fragment: as a crayon lithograph pulled from stone: soft grainy tones from greasy litho crayon catching the grain of the stone, areas of liquid tusche wash with blotchy reticulation, highlights scratched out with a blade, rich warm black on smooth off-white paper, drawing-like spontaneity with no plate mark.
styles.avoid: Avoid charcoal smudging and digital pencil brushes; grain should be fine, even and printed.
styles.feasibility_note: Reads well; can collapse into a generic charcoal drawing.
styles.short_de: Flachdruck vom Kalkstein, auf den mit fetter Kreide oder Tusche gezeichnet wird, mit körnigen, zeichnerisch weichen Tönen; um 1796–98 von Alois Senefelder in München erfunden.
styles.short_en: Planographic print drawn on limestone with greasy crayon or tusche, giving grainy, drawing-like tones; invented by Alois Senefelder in Munich around 1796–98.
markers_de: sattes warmes Schwarz auf glattem Papier
markers_en: grainy litho-crayon tone in stone grain
highlights scratched out with a blade
rich warm black on smooth paper

styles.era_origin: Patented in 1837 in France; dominant colour printing c. 1860–1910 for labels, trade cards, advertising and die-cut scraps.
visual_markers: rich saturated colours from many overprinted stones
hand-stippled grain instead of halftone dots
styles.prompt_fragment: as a late-Victorian chromolithograph: rich saturated colours built from a dozen or more overprinted stones, each area showing fine hand-stippled grain instead of halftone dots, metallic gold bronzing in ornamental borders, slight registration shifts at edges, sentimental decorative composition, glossy-varnished card stock with embossed edges.
styles.avoid: Avoid modern CMYK rosettes and clean digital vintage pastiche; texture must be stipple grain and layered stone colour.
styles.feasibility_note: Victorian chromo is well represented; stipple grain may be lost.
styles.sensitivity_note: Victorian trade cards frequently carried racist caricature; avoid such imagery.
styles.short_de: Farblithografie aus oft über zehn übereinandergedruckten Steinen mit satten Farben und handgetupftem Korn, 1837 in Frankreich patentiert, um 1860–1910 vorherrschend für Etiketten, Sammelbilder und Glanzbilder.
styles.short_en: Colour lithography from ten or more overprinted stones, with saturated colours and hand-stippled grain; patented in France in 1837, dominant c. 1860–1910 for labels, trade cards and scraps.
styles.era_de: 1837 patentiert; Blüte ca. 1860–1910, Europa und USA
styles.era_en: patented 1837; peak c. 1860–1910, Europe and USA
markers_de: satte Farben aus vielen übereinandergedruckten Steinen
markers_en: saturated colours from many overprinted stones
hand-stippled grain instead of halftone dots
styles.sensitivity_de: Viktorianische Reklame- und Sammelbilder enthielten häufig rassistische Karikaturen; solche Bilder vermeiden.
styles.sensitivity_en: Victorian trade cards frequently carried racist caricature; avoid such imagery.

styles.era_origin: Mid-19th to early 20th century: chromolithographs varnished and embossed with canvas texture to imitate oil paintings for middle-class homes.
visual_markers: mechanical canvas weave embossed uniformly over the image
fake brush relief not matching painted forms
sweet, slightly flat colours over litho grain
styles.prompt_fragment: as a 19th-century oleograph: a chromolithograph imitating an oil painting, with a mechanical canvas-weave texture embossed uniformly across the whole image, fake brushstroke relief that doesn't match the painted forms, glossy amber-yellowed varnish, sweet slightly flat colours with fine litho grain beneath, sentimental parlour-picture mood.
styles.avoid: Avoid a genuine oil painting with real impasto; the charm is the mechanical, slightly cheap imitation.
styles.feasibility_note: The model tends to produce a convincing oil painting; the mechanical imitation quality is subtle.
styles.sensitivity_note: Commonly used for devotional and religious pictures; handle religious iconography respectfully.
styles.short_de: Lackierte Chromolithografie mit eingeprägter Leinwandstruktur, die ein Ölgemälde vortäuscht; von der Mitte des 19. bis ins frühe 20. Jahrhundert als Wandbild bürgerlicher Wohnungen verbreitet.
styles.short_en: Varnished chromolithograph embossed with canvas texture to pass as an oil painting, hung in middle-class homes from the mid-19th to the early 20th century.
styles.era_de: Mitte 19. bis frühes 20. Jh., Europa und USA
styles.era_en: mid-19th to early 20th c., Europe and USA
markers_de: Pinselrelief, das nicht zu den Formen passt
süßliche, etwas flache Farben über Litho-Korn
markers_en: fake brush relief not matching forms
sweet, flat colours over litho grain
styles.sensitivity_de: Häufig für Andachts- und Heiligenbilder genutzt; religiöse Bildmotive respektvoll behandeln.
styles.sensitivity_en: Often used for devotional pictures; treat religious iconography with respect.

styles.era_origin: Commercial mesh-stencil printing from the early 1900s, fine-art serigraphy from the 1930s, poster culture since the 1960s.
visual_markers: mesh texture and squeegee drag in solids
ink sitting on heavy matte stock
styles.prompt_fragment: as a hand-pulled screen print: thick, opaque flat spot-colour layers, four to six inks with visible overprint where translucent colours overlap, slight misregistration leaving thin gaps and overlaps, faint mesh texture and squeegee drag streaks in large solids, crisp yet slightly sawtoothed edges, ink sitting on heavy matte poster stock.
styles.avoid: Avoid clean flat-vector illustration with perfect alignment; show physical ink layers, overprint and registration errors.
styles.feasibility_note: Reliable; tends toward vector cleanliness unless physical artefacts are requested.
styles.short_de: Schablonendruck durch ein Siebgewebe: dicke, deckende Farbflächen mit Überdrucken und leichtem Passerversatz; gewerblich ab etwa 1900, künstlerisch ab den 1930ern, Plakatkultur seit den 1960ern.
styles.short_en: Stencil printing through mesh, giving thick opaque colour layers with overprints and slight misregistration; commercial from c. 1900, fine art from the 1930s, poster culture since the 1960s.
styles.era_de: gewerblich ab ca. 1900; Kunst ab den 1930ern; Plakate ab den 1960ern
styles.era_en: commercial c. 1900; fine art 1930s; posters 1960s onward
markers_de: Überdruck, wo lasierende Farben sich überlagern
leichter Passerversatz mit Blitzern und Überlappungen
Farbe liegt auf schwerem mattem Karton
markers_en: mesh texture and squeegee drag in solids
ink sitting on heavy matte stock

styles.era_origin: Paris c. 1900–1930s: luxury fashion and decorative portfolios coloured by hand through many stencils.
visual_markers: dabbed brush texture and pooling inside shapes
vivid jewel tones with gold or silver touches
styles.prompt_fragment: as an Art Deco pochoir plate: vivid flat colour applied by brush through dozens of hand-cut stencils, crisp shape edges with slight pooling and dabbed brush texture inside each area, jewel tones with touches of gold or silver, a fine printed key line, elegant flattened composition on bright heavy paper.
styles.avoid: Avoid soft gradients and digital flat-vector perfection; colour must show dabbed gouache texture.
styles.feasibility_note: Deco elegance comes through; the dabbed stencil texture needs emphasis.
styles.short_de: Drucke, von Hand mit Gouache durch zahlreiche Schablonen koloriert, mit scharfkantigen Farbflächen und getupfter Textur; typisch für Pariser Mode- und Dekorationsmappen um 1910–1930.
styles.short_en: Prints coloured by hand with gouache through dozens of cut stencils, giving crisp flat shapes with dabbed texture; used for Paris fashion and design portfolios around 1910–1930.
markers_en: jewel tones with gold or silver

styles.era_origin: Digital stencil duplicator introduced in Japan in 1986, adopted by zine makers, small presses and illustrators from the 2000s.
visual_markers: two or three spot inks (fluoro pink, blue, yellow)
styles.prompt_fragment: as a risograph print: two or three spot inks such as fluorescent pink, medium blue and yellow overprinting to create new colours, grainy uneven ink coverage with speckled solids, coarse halftone or dither in tonal areas, visible misregistration between layers, faint roller marks, soy ink sitting matte on uncoated off-white paper.
styles.avoid: Avoid neat flat vector colours and fake grain overlays; texture and registration error should look mechanical and uneven.
styles.feasibility_note: Well known; grain can look like a uniform noise filter.
styles.sensitivity_note: RISO is a manufacturer trademark; the term is used generically for the look.
styles.short_de: Druck vom japanischen Digital-Schablonendrucker in zwei bis drei Schmuckfarben, mit körniger Deckung, Mischfarben im Überdruck und Passerversatz; seit den 2000ern in der Zine- und Kleinverlagsszene verbreitet.
styles.short_en: Prints from a Japanese digital stencil duplicator in two or three spot inks, with grainy coverage, overprinted colours and misregistration; used by zine makers since the 2000s.
styles.era_en: since 1986, Japan; zine revival from the 2000s
markers_de: zwei bis drei Schmuckfarben (Neonpink, Blau, Gelb)
markers_en: two or three spot inks (fluoro pink, blue, yellow)
styles.sensitivity_de: RISO ist eine Herstellermarke; der Begriff steht hier allgemein für den Look.
styles.sensitivity_en: RISO is a manufacturer's trademark; the term is used generically for the look.

styles.era_origin: Patented in the 1880s; the standard office, school, church and underground-press duplicator until the 1980s.
visual_markers: typed text and stylus lines cut into wax stencil
oily black ink bleeding into pulp paper
styles.prompt_fragment: as a mimeographed sheet: typewritten text and stylus-drawn line art cut into a wax stencil, printed in slightly oily black ink that bleeds into absorbent pulp paper, filled-in letter counters, dense patches where the stencil stretched, faint set-off from the previous sheet, uneven coverage, slightly crooked, ragged hand-drawn borders.
styles.avoid: Avoid crisp laser-printed text and clean digital line art; it must look like a cheap duplicated newsletter or zine page.
styles.feasibility_note: Cheap duplicated feel works; specific stencil artefacts are subtle.
styles.sensitivity_note: 'Mimeograph' was originally a trademark and is now generic.
styles.short_de: Abzüge von einer mit Schreibmaschine oder Griffel beschriebenen Wachsmatrize, in öliger schwarzer Farbe auf saugfähigem Papier; bis in die 1980er Standard in Büro, Schule und Untergrundpresse.
styles.short_en: Duplicated sheets printed through a typed or stylus-cut wax stencil in oily black ink on absorbent paper; standard for office, school and underground press until the 1980s.
markers_de: Schreibmaschinentext und Griffellinien aus der Wachsmatrize
ölige schwarze Farbe, ins Papier verlaufen
markers_en: typed text and stylus lines from a wax stencil
oily black ink bleeding into pulp paper
styles.sensitivity_de: „Mimeograph“ war ursprünglich ein Markenname und ist heute Gattungsbegriff.
styles.sensitivity_en: 'Mimeograph' was originally a trademark and is now generic.

styles.era_origin: Invented in Germany in 1923; school worksheets and office forms printed from aniline-dye masters until the 1980s.
styles.prompt_fragment: as a spirit-duplicator copy: everything printed in soft violet-purple aniline dye, lines slightly fuzzy and fading unevenly from one side of the sheet to the other, typed or hand-drawn worksheet character, faint purple smudges and ghost lines, cheap thin paper with a slight curl.
styles.avoid: Avoid any colour but violet and crisp printed black; it must look like a faded school handout, not a purple filter.
styles.feasibility_note: The purple colour is easy; the uneven fade and fuzzy dye lines need emphasis.
styles.sensitivity_note: 'Ditto' was a trademark; the term is used generically.
styles.short_de: Abzüge von einer Anilinfarben-Matrize, alles in unscharfem Violett, das über den Bogen verblasst; Arbeitsblätter und Büroformulare von den 1920ern bis in die 1980er.
styles.short_en: Copies from an aniline-dye master, all in fuzzy violet fading across the sheet; school worksheets and office forms from the 1920s to the 1980s.
styles.sensitivity_de: „Ditto“ war ein Markenname; der Begriff wird allgemein verwendet.
styles.sensitivity_en: 'Ditto' was a trademark; the term is used generically.

styles.era_origin: First made in Italy in the 1640s, revived by Impressionists in the 1870s–80s and widespread in contemporary printmaking.
visual_markers: painterly ink flattened into reticulated texture
highlights wiped with rags and fingers
styles.prompt_fragment: as a monotype: ink painted and wiped on a smooth plate then pressed onto damp paper, painterly passages flattened into soft reticulated textures, highlights wiped out with rags, fingers and brush handles, smoky veils of tone, faint ghost-print paleness in places, plate edge visible, one or two oil-based colours.
styles.avoid: Avoid looking like a direct oil or ink painting; paint should look squashed and transferred, with press textures.
styles.feasibility_note: Mood works; it often reads as a regular painting without the press-flattened texture.
styles.short_de: Unikatdruck von einer glatten Platte, auf der die Farbe gemalt und ausgewischt wird, mit gequetschten, rauchigen Tönen; um 1640 in Italien erfunden, von Degas wiederbelebt.
styles.short_en: A one-off print from ink painted and wiped on a smooth plate, then pressed onto paper, with flattened smoky tones; invented in 1640s Italy, revived by Degas.
markers_de: mit Lappen und Fingern ausgewischte Lichter
markers_en: painterly ink flattened into reticulated texture
highlights wiped out with rags and fingers

styles.era_origin: Explored by Post-Impressionists around 1900 and by early 20th-century modernists: drawing on paper laid over an inked surface.
visual_markers: accidental smudges where the hand rested
single dark brown or black ink
styles.prompt_fragment: as an oil transfer drawing: lines drawn with pressure on the back of paper laid over an inked surface, so they print soft, grainy and slightly blurred, accidental smudges and cloudy tone where the hand rested, irregular naive line weight, one dark brown or black ink on thin paper, ghostly understated mood.
styles.avoid: Avoid crisp pen lines or charcoal; the line should look indirect, slightly blind and smudged.
styles.feasibility_note: Easily becomes charcoal or pencil; the transfer smudges are the key handle.
styles.short_de: Auf die Rückseite eines über eingefärbtem Grund liegenden Blatts gezeichnet, druckt die Linie weich, körnig und verwischt; bei Gauguin um 1900 und Klee in den 1920ern.
styles.short_en: Drawing on the back of paper laid over an inked surface, so the line prints soft, grainy and smudged; used by Gauguin around 1900 and Klee in the 1920s.
markers_en: single dark brown or black ink

styles.era_origin: Gelatine-plate printing has long been used; it became a widespread craft and art-journal technique with reusable gel plates in the 2010s.
visual_markers: crisp negative silhouettes from leaves or masks
styles.prompt_fragment: as a gel-plate print: several translucent acrylic layers pulled from a soft gel plate, brayer streaks and lifted textures, crisp negative silhouettes left by leaves, paper masks or stencils, ghostly second-pull impressions, small air-bubble specks, bright mixed colours over earthy neutrals, monoprint layering on cartridge paper.
styles.avoid: Avoid digital collage and vector shapes; layers must show the soft, slightly blotchy acrylic transfer of a gel plate.
styles.feasibility_note: Layered craft look renders; can slide into generic mixed-media collage.
styles.sensitivity_note: 'Gelli' is a brand name; use 'gel plate' generically.
styles.short_de: Monotypien von einer weichen Gelplatte in durchscheinenden Acrylschichten, mit Walzenspuren und scharfen Aussparungen von Blättern oder Masken; seit den 2010ern verbreitete Bastel- und Art-Journal-Technik.
styles.short_en: Monoprints pulled from a gel plate in translucent acrylic layers, with brayer streaks and crisp silhouettes from leaves or masks; a craft and art-journal technique since the 2010s.
markers_de: scharfe Aussparungen von Blättern oder Masken
markers_en: crisp negative silhouettes from leaves or masks
styles.sensitivity_de: „Gelli“ ist ein Markenname; allgemein spricht man von Gelplatte.
styles.sensitivity_en: 'Gelli' is a brand name; use 'gel plate' generically.

styles.era_origin: Japanese suminagashi from the 12th century, Persian and Ottoman ebru from the 15th–16th centuries, European marbled endpapers from the 17th century.
visual_markers: swirling veined patterns pulled from floating colour
fine dark veins where colours meet
styles.prompt_fragment: as hand-marbled paper: colours floated on a thickened size and transferred in one pull, swirling veined patterns, combed nonpareil feathering and round stone-drops, fine dark veins where colours meet, earthy ochre, indigo, oxblood and cream or soft concentric ink rings, slight blotch where the paper lifted, decorative endpaper character.
styles.avoid: Avoid psychedelic digital fluid-art pours and glossy resin; it must be matte paper with combed traditional patterns.
styles.feasibility_note: Pattern renders beautifully; figurative subjects only work as motifs formed within the marbling.
styles.sensitivity_note: Ebru is UNESCO intangible heritage of Türkiye and suminagashi is a Japanese tradition; credit the traditions accurately.
styles.short_de: Auf dem Marmoriergrund schwimmende Farben, zu Schlieren gekämmt und in einem Zug abgenommen; aus Japan, Persien und dem Osmanischen Reich, in Europa als Vorsatzpapier seit dem 17. Jh.
styles.short_en: Colours floated on a thickened bath, combed into swirls and lifted onto paper in one pull; Japanese, Persian and Ottoman traditions, European endpapers since the 17th century.
styles.era_de: seit dem 12. Jh., Japan, Persien, Osmanisches Reich; Europa ab dem 17. Jh.
styles.era_en: since the 12th c., Japan, Persia, Ottoman Empire; Europe from the 17th c.
markers_en: fine dark veins where colours meet
matte paper with slight lift blotches
styles.sensitivity_de: Ebru ist immaterielles UNESCO-Kulturerbe der Türkei, Suminagashi eine japanische Tradition; beide korrekt benennen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Ebru is UNESCO-listed intangible heritage of Türkiye and suminagashi a Japanese tradition; name the traditions accurately.

styles.era_origin: Japanese gyotaku records of caught fish from the mid-19th century; European nature printing developed in Vienna in the 1850s.
visual_markers: true surface texture (scales, veins, ridges) in mottled ink
soft fuzzy edges where paper wrapped the form
styles.prompt_fragment: as a direct nature print: the real object inked and pressed onto thin washi so its true surface texture—scales, veins, ridges—appears in mottled sumi ink, soft fuzzy edges where the paper wrapped around the form, uneven ink density, small details added by brush afterwards, generous empty paper, brief brush inscription.
styles.avoid: Avoid drawn or painted illustration; the image must read as an impression taken from a physical object.
styles.feasibility_note: Works well for flat textured objects; people and complex scenes do not suit the logic.
styles.sensitivity_note: Japanese tradition; avoid fake red seals and pseudo-Japanese text.
styles.short_de: Abdrucke direkt von eingefärbten Fischen, Blättern oder anderen Objekten, die deren Oberflächenstruktur in fleckiger Tusche zeigen; japanisches Gyotaku und Wiener Naturselbstdruck seit dem 19. Jh.
styles.short_en: Prints taken directly from inked fish, leaves or real objects, showing their true surface texture in mottled ink; Japanese gyotaku and Viennese nature printing from the 19th century.
styles.era_de: seit Mitte des 19. Jh., Japan und Wien
styles.era_en: since the mid-19th century, Japan and Vienna
markers_de: echte Oberflächenstruktur (Schuppen, Adern) in fleckiger Tusche
markers_en: true surface texture (scales, veins) in mottled ink
soft, fuzzy edges where paper wrapped the form
styles.sensitivity_de: Japanische Tradition; keine falschen roten Siegel und keine Pseudo-Schriftzeichen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Japanese tradition; avoid fake red seals and pseudo-Japanese inscriptions.

styles.era_origin: Chinese ink rubbings of carved steles since at least the Tang dynasty, European brass rubbings, and frottage as a Surrealist technique from 1925.
visual_markers: raised areas dark and mottled, incised lines white
pad-dabbed ink blotches or directional crayon strokes
paper wrinkles moulded to the surface
textures of wood grain, stone or relief
styles.prompt_fragment: as a rubbing taken from a carved or textured surface: paper laid over relief and dabbed or rubbed with ink or wax crayon, raised areas printing dark and mottled, recessed incised lines staying white, directional crayon strokes and pad blotches, wrinkles and creases where the paper moulded to the surface, matte black or deep brown.
styles.avoid: Avoid a clean white-on-black vector inversion; the mottled, uneven rubbing texture and paper creases are the point.
styles.feasibility_note: Texture renders; the model may invert values or make it too clean.
styles.sensitivity_note: Rubbings of real gravestones, steles or sacred inscriptions can be culturally sensitive; avoid fake Chinese or Latin inscriptions implying authenticity.
styles.short_de: Abnahme von Inschriften, Reliefs oder Grabplatten durch aufgelegtes, mit Tusche betupftes oder mit Wachs geriebenes Papier: Erhabenes wird dunkel, Eingeschnittenes bleibt weiß; in China seit der Tang-Zeit.
styles.short_en: Copies of carved inscriptions or brasses made by dabbing or rubbing paper laid over them: raised areas turn dark, incised lines stay white; in China since Tang times.
styles.era_de: seit der Tang-Zeit (7. Jh.), China; später auch Europa
styles.era_en: since the Tang dynasty (7th c.), China; later also Europe
markers_de: Erhabenes dunkel und fleckig, Eingeschnittenes weiß
markers_en: raised areas dark and mottled, incised lines white
pad-dabbed blotches or directional crayon strokes
paper wrinkles moulded to the surface
styles.sensitivity_de: Abreibungen echter Grabsteine, Stelen oder sakraler Inschriften können heikel sein; keine erfundenen chinesischen oder lateinischen Inschriften mit Echtheitsanspruch.
styles.sensitivity_en: Rubbings of real gravestones, steles or sacred inscriptions can be sensitive; avoid fake Chinese or Latin inscriptions posing as authentic.

styles.era_origin: Halftone photographs in newspapers from the 1880s–90s, printed with coarse screens on newsprint through the late 20th century.
visual_markers: show-through text, column rule and caption
styles.prompt_fragment: as a black-and-white newspaper halftone: photograph reproduced with a coarse 45-degree dot screen visible on close view, ink gain clogging the shadows into muddy blacks, flat grey highlights, cheap off-white newsprint with fibre flecks, faint show-through of text from the reverse side, column rule and small caption beneath.
styles.avoid: Avoid crisp modern greyscale photography and decorative oversized dots; the dot structure should be fine and degraded by cheap printing.
styles.feasibility_note: Reliable newspaper look; exact dot screens are approximate.
styles.sensitivity_note: Avoid fabricated news clippings showing real people or events (misinformation risk).
styles.short_de: Zeitungsfotos im groben Punktraster auf billigem Zeitungspapier, mit zugelaufenen Schatten und flauen grauen Lichtern; von den 1890ern bis ins späte 20. Jahrhundert üblich.
styles.short_en: Photographs reproduced in newspapers with a coarse dot screen on cheap newsprint, with clogged shadows and grey highlights; common from the 1890s through the late 20th century.
styles.sensitivity_de: Keine gefälschten Zeitungsausschnitte mit realen Personen oder Ereignissen (Desinformationsgefahr).
styles.sensitivity_en: Avoid fabricated news clippings showing real people or events (misinformation risk).

styles.era_origin: Four-colour process offset lithography, dominant from the 1950s in magazines, packaging and flyers.
styles.prompt_fragment: as a cheap four-colour offset print: visible CMYK rosette patterns in tones and skin, cyan, magenta and yellow plates shifted a fraction of a millimetre so edges show coloured fringes and ghost doubles, slight dot gain darkening mid-tones, faint paper texture, small imperfections like hickeys and ink streaks.
styles.avoid: Avoid a deliberate chromatic-aberration or glitch filter; it should look like an imperfectly registered real print.
styles.feasibility_note: Colour fringes come through; rosette fidelity is unreliable.
styles.short_de: Billiger Vierfarb-Offsetdruck, bei dem Cyan-, Magenta-, Gelb- und Schwarzplatte leicht verschoben sind, mit Farbsäumen und sichtbaren Rasterrosetten; seit den 1950ern verbreitet.
styles.short_en: Cheap four-colour offset printing in which the cyan, magenta, yellow and black plates sit slightly out of register, leaving coloured fringes and visible rosettes; common from the 1950s.

styles.era_origin: Two-plate halftone printing in photo books from the early 20th century, iconic in 1950s–60s record and book design and in editorial design today.
visual_markers: black or navy plate carrying shadows
one bold spot colour in mid-tones
styles.prompt_fragment: as a two-colour duotone print: a photographic image separated into two halftone plates, black or deep navy carrying the shadows and a single bold spot colour such as orange, teal or ochre carrying mid-tones, paper white for highlights, fine visible screen, matte uncoated stock, mid-century editorial feel.
styles.avoid: Avoid neon gradient-map duotones of social-media design; it must look like two inks printed on paper.
styles.feasibility_note: Easy to get; the printed screen and paper need mention to avoid a digital gradient map.
styles.short_de: Fotodruck mit zwei Rasterplatten, meist Schwarz plus eine Schmuckfarbe; verbreitet in Fotobüchern sowie in der Platten- und Buchgestaltung der 1950er und 60er.
styles.short_en: A photograph printed from two halftone plates, usually black plus one spot colour; common in photo books and in 1950s–60s record and book design.
markers_de: Schwarz- oder Marineblau-Platte trägt die Schatten
eine kräftige Schmuckfarbe in den Mitteltönen
markers_en: black or navy plate carrying the shadows
one bold spot colour in the mid-tones

styles.era_origin: Rotary photogravure from c. 1910 for Sunday supplements, illustrated weeklies and catalogues until the 1960s.
visual_markers: single rich ink: sepia, olive green or blue-black
fine cell screen, serrated type edges
styles.prompt_fragment: as a 1930s rotogravure magazine supplement: photographs printed in a single rich ink of sepia brown, olive green or blue-black, deep velvety near-continuous tones with a fine cell screen and slightly serrated edges on type, soft focus, captions in condensed sans serif, thin semi-gloss paper with faint show-through.
styles.avoid: Avoid crisp halftone dots and modern sepia filters; tone should be deep and inky with soft cell structure.
styles.feasibility_note: Monochrome magazine feel works; the cell screen is rarely visible.
styles.short_de: Rotationstiefdruck in einer satten Farbe wie Sepia oder Olivgrün, mit tiefen, samtigen Tönen; typisch für Sonntagsbeilagen und Illustrierte von etwa 1910 bis in die 1960er.
styles.short_en: Rotary gravure printing in one rich ink such as sepia or olive, with deep velvety tones; Sunday supplements and illustrated magazines from about 1910 to the 1960s.
markers_de: eine satte Farbe: Sepia, Oliv oder Blauschwarz
markers_en: single rich ink: sepia, olive or blue-black
fine cell screen, serrated type edges

styles.era_origin: Common in 1940s–60s children's books, magazines and packaging, where illustrators hand-drew each colour plate to save costs.
visual_markers: black key plus one or two spot inks
overprint creating a deeper third colour
litho-crayon, spatter and dry-brush textures per plate
generous paper white on cream stock
styles.prompt_fragment: as a mid-century pre-separated two- or three-colour print: each ink plate hand-drawn, black key plus warm red and mustard or teal, overlapping inks creating a deeper third colour, flat areas textured with litho crayon, spatter and dry brush, slight misregistration, generous paper white on cream uncoated stock.
styles.avoid: Avoid full-colour palettes and clean vector mid-century pastiche; texture and overprint must show the physical separations.
styles.feasibility_note: Limited-palette mid-century look is reliable; true overprint logic is inconsistent.
styles.short_de: Illustrationen, deren Farbauszüge die Zeichner von Hand anlegten, meist Schwarz plus ein bis zwei sich überdruckende Schmuckfarben; verbreitet in Kinderbüchern und Zeitschriften der 1940er–60er.
styles.short_en: Illustrations in which the artist drew each ink plate by hand, usually black plus one or two spot colours that overprint; common in 1940s–60s children's books and magazines.
markers_de: Schwarz plus ein bis zwei Schmuckfarben
markers_en: black key plus one or two spot inks
overprint forming a deeper third colour
generous paper white on cream stock

styles.era_origin: Standard in letterpress and offset production; make-ready waste sheets run repeatedly through the press collect overlapping images.
visual_markers: image on a larger sheet with crop marks
registration targets and CMYK colour-control strip
separations or progressive proofs side by side
pencil correction notes and ink thumbprints
styles.prompt_fragment: as a printer's press sheet: the image placed on a larger uncoated sheet with crop marks, registration targets and a CMYK colour-control strip along the edge, individual colour separations or progressive proofs shown side by side, overlapping ghost impressions from make-ready passes, handwritten pencil correction notes and inky thumbprints.
styles.avoid: Avoid neat digital print mockups; the sheet must show physical press artefacts and layering.
styles.feasibility_note: Crop marks and colour bars come through; coherent separations are unreliable.
styles.short_de: Druckbogen mit Schnittmarken, Farbkontrollstreifen, einzelnen Farbauszügen und übereinanderliegenden Einrichtdrucken; die Andruck- und Makulaturbogen aus Buch- und Offsetdruck.
styles.short_en: A printer's sheet with crop marks, colour bars, separate colour proofs and overlapping make-ready impressions; the proof and waste sheets of letterpress and offset printing.
styles.era_en: 20th century to today, print shops worldwide
markers_de: Motiv auf größerem Bogen mit Schnittmarken
markers_en: image on a larger sheet with crop marks
separations or progressive proofs side by side

styles.era_origin: Xerographic copiers from 1959; copy art of the 1960s–70s and punk/DIY zines from the late 1970s.
visual_markers: black toner speckle and drum streaks
shadow lines from cut-and-paste edges and tape
dark borders from an open copier lid
skew and stretch from moving originals
styles.prompt_fragment: as a multi-generation photocopy: crushed high contrast with lost mid-tones, black toner speckle and drum streaks, grey shadow lines from cut-and-pasted edges and tape, dark vignette borders from an open copier lid, slight skew and stretch from moving the original, fused glossy black toner on cheap white copy paper.
styles.avoid: Avoid neat digital threshold filters and grunge brushes; artefacts must look like real copier generation loss.
styles.feasibility_note: Copier artefacts render convincingly.
styles.sensitivity_note: Xerox is a trademark; prefer 'photocopy' in prompts.
styles.short_de: Durch wiederholtes Kopieren verfremdete Bilder mit hartem Kontrast, Tonerkrümeln und sichtbaren Klebekanten; Copy Art ab den 1960ern, Punk-Fanzines ab den späten 1970ern.
styles.short_en: Images degraded by repeated photocopying into crushed contrast, toner speckle and visible paste-up edges; copy art from the 1960s and punk zines from the late 1970s.
styles.era_de: seit den 1960ern; Punk-Zines ab Ende der 1970er
styles.era_en: since the 1960s; punk zines from the late 1970s
markers_de: Schräglage und Verzerrung durch verrutschte Vorlage
markers_en: shadow lines from paste-up edges and tape
dark borders from an open copier lid
skew and stretch from a moved original
styles.sensitivity_de: Xerox ist ein Markenname; im Prompt besser „photocopy“ verwenden.
styles.sensitivity_en: Xerox is a trademark; prefer 'photocopy' in prompts.

styles.era_origin: Carbon paper with typewriters, receipt books and forms from the late 19th century until the 1980s.
visual_markers: soft blue-violet or grey-black carbon impression
styles.prompt_fragment: as a typewriter carbon copy: typed text and pressure-drawn lines transferred in soft blue-violet or grey-black carbon, fuzzy uneven characters where keys struck lighter or heavier, smears and fingerprint smudges of carbon, faint impression marks, thin translucent onion-skin paper with crease lines.
styles.avoid: Avoid crisp printed text and typewriter fonts on clean white; the carbon smudge and thin paper are essential.
styles.feasibility_note: Typewriter feel works; carbon fuzz and onion-skin translucency are subtle.
styles.sensitivity_note: Avoid fabricating official documents, forms or signatures that could pass as genuine records.
styles.short_de: Über Kohlepapier auf dünnes Durchschlagpapier übertragene Schreibmaschinenschrift, unscharf und verschmiert in Blau oder Schwarz; Büro-Durchschläge vom späten 19. Jh. bis in die 1980er.
styles.short_en: Typed text copied through carbon paper onto thin onion-skin sheets, fuzzy and smudged in blue or black; office copies from the late 19th century to the 1980s.
markers_en: soft blue-violet or grey-black carbon impression
styles.sensitivity_de: Keine amtlichen Dokumente, Formulare oder Unterschriften fälschen, die als echt durchgehen könnten.
styles.sensitivity_en: Avoid fabricating official documents, forms or signatures that could pass as genuine records.

styles.era_origin: Group-3 fax machines printing on thermal paper, common from the 1980s to the early 2000s.
visual_markers: low-resolution one-bit dither instead of grey
horizontal streaks and dropped scan lines
styles.prompt_fragment: as a 1990s thermal fax printout: low-resolution one-bit black rendering with coarse dither patterns instead of grey, jagged stair-step edges, horizontal streaks and dropped scan lines, slight vertical stretch, a tiny transmission header line across the top, greyish glossy thermal paper with curl and faded edges.
styles.avoid: Avoid clean digital bitmap or pixel-art aesthetics; the degradation must look transmitted and printed on thermal paper.
styles.feasibility_note: Dither and streaks render; header text may garble.
styles.sensitivity_note: Avoid fabricating official-looking documents or real phone numbers in headers.
styles.short_de: Grob aufgelöste Schwarzweiß-Übertragungen auf welligem Thermopapier, mit grobem Dithering, Treppenkanten und ausgefallenen Zeilen; Bürokommunikation von den 1980ern bis Anfang der 2000er.
styles.short_en: Low-resolution black-and-white transmissions printed on curling thermal paper, with coarse dither, jagged edges and dropped scan lines; office communication from the 1980s to the early 2000s.
styles.sensitivity_de: Keine amtlich wirkenden Fälschungen und keine echten Telefonnummern in der Kopfzeile.
styles.sensitivity_en: Avoid fabricated official-looking documents or real phone numbers in headers.

styles.era_origin: Direct thermal printers in point-of-sale systems since the 1980s, now also used for receipt-printer art and zines.
visual_markers: narrow curling strip of thermal paper
styles.prompt_fragment: as a direct thermal receipt-printer output: a narrow curling strip of glossy thermal paper, monochrome dithered image in faded grey-black, monospaced type with dashed separator lines, slightly uneven print-head density and faint vertical streaks, serrated tear-off edge, light fading and scuffing as if kept in a pocket.
styles.avoid: Avoid crisp laser-printed graphics and fake store branding; it must look like actual thermal print.
styles.feasibility_note: Format renders well; text is handled better in gpt-image-2 but still needs exact copy.
styles.sensitivity_note: Never create realistic receipts from real merchants or with amounts that could serve as fake proof of purchase.
styles.short_de: Blasse, grauschwarz gerasterte Bilder und Monospace-Schrift auf einem schmalen, gerollten Thermopapierstreifen; Kassenbons seit den 1980ern, heute auch für Bondrucker-Kunst und Zines.
styles.short_en: Faded grey-black dithered images and monospaced type on a narrow curling strip of thermal paper; point-of-sale receipts since the 1980s, now also used for printer art and zines.
markers_en: narrow curling strip of thermal paper
styles.sensitivity_de: Keine realistischen Belege echter Händler oder mit Beträgen, die als Kaufnachweis taugen könnten.
styles.sensitivity_en: Never create realistic receipts from real merchants or with amounts that could pass as proof of purchase.

styles.era_origin: 9- and 24-pin impact printers, common from the mid-1970s through the early 1990s.
visual_markers: text and graphics built from visible pin dots
fan-fold paper with sprocket holes and perforations
styles.prompt_fragment: as a dot-matrix printout: text and graphics built from visible round pin dots, horizontal banding between print-head passes, faded fabric-ribbon ink, coarse block or ASCII-shaded imagery, on continuous fan-fold paper with tractor-feed sprocket holes, perforated tear lines and pale green-bar stripes.
styles.avoid: Avoid pixel-art game aesthetics and a smooth LCD bitmap look; impact dots and ribbon fade must be visible.
styles.feasibility_note: Paper format is easy; consistent dot construction of glyphs is not.
styles.short_de: Text und Grafik aus sichtbaren Nadelpunkten in blassem Farbbandabdruck auf Endlospapier mit Lochrand; Computerausdrucke von Mitte der 1970er bis Anfang der 1990er.
styles.short_en: Text and graphics built from visible pin dots in faded ribbon ink on fan-fold paper with sprocket holes; computer printouts from the mid-1970s to the early 1990s.
markers_de: Text und Grafik aus sichtbaren Nadelpunkten
markers_en: text and graphics from visible pin dots

styles.era_origin: Cyanotype copying of technical drawings from the 1870s until diazo replaced it in the mid-20th century.
visual_markers: crisp white lines on deep Prussian blue
dimension lines, section hatching, title block
slight bleed of lines into blue
blotchy uneven blue with washed patches
fold creases, edge wear, pin holes
styles.prompt_fragment: as an original blueprint copy: crisp white lines on deep Prussian-blue paper, technical drawing conventions with dimension lines, section hatching and a ruled title block, slight bleed of white lines into the blue, uneven blotchy blue with lighter washed patches, fold creases, edge wear and pin holes.
styles.avoid: Avoid neon-glow sci-fi blueprint interfaces and cyan grid wallpaper; it should be a physical paper copy with chemical irregularity.
styles.feasibility_note: Very reliable, though often too clean and digital without physical cues.
styles.short_de: Cyanotypie-Kopien technischer Zeichnungen, weiße Linien auf tiefem Preußischblau mit fleckiger Färbung und Knickspuren; Standard in Technik und Architektur von den 1870ern bis in die 1950er.
styles.short_en: Cyanotype copies of technical drawings, white lines on deep Prussian blue with blotchy colour and fold wear; standard in engineering and architecture from the 1870s to the 1950s.
markers_de: klare weiße Linien auf tiefem Preußischblau
markers_en: crisp white lines on deep Prussian blue
slight bleed of lines into the blue
fold creases, edge wear, pin holes

styles.era_origin: Diazo copying from the 1920s, replacing blueprints for architectural and engineering drawings until large-format digital printing in the 1990s.
visual_markers: blue-violet or sepia lines on off-white
fold lines, dog-ears, reproduced handwritten notes
styles.prompt_fragment: as a diazo whiteprint: technical drawing reproduced as blue-violet or sepia lines on off-white paper with a faint pale-lavender background haze, slightly uneven line density, sun-faded beige edges, fold lines and dog-eared corners, handwritten annotations reproduced along with the drawing.
styles.avoid: Avoid the white-on-blue blueprint look; here the lines are dark on light.
styles.feasibility_note: Lesser-known process; the model may default to a blueprint or plain line drawing.
styles.sensitivity_note: Ozalid is a trade name.
styles.short_de: Blauviolette oder sepiafarbene Linien auf gebrochenem Weiß mit zartem Lavendelschleier; das Kopierverfahren für technische Zeichnungen von den 1920ern bis in die 1990er.
styles.short_en: Dark blue-violet or sepia lines on off-white paper with a faint lavender haze; the copy process for technical drawings from the 1920s to the 1990s.
markers_de: blauviolette oder sepiafarbene Linien auf gebrochenem Weiß
markers_en: blue-violet or sepia lines on off-white
fold lines and copied handwritten notes
styles.sensitivity_de: Ozalid ist ein Markenname.
styles.sensitivity_en: Ozalid is a trade name.

styles.era_origin: Rooted in 19th-century tunnel books and peep shows; popular as hand- and laser-cut layered shadow boxes since the 2010s.
visual_markers: 8-12 stacked cardstock layers with visible gaps
crisp cut edges with slight paper fibre
tonal depth from light foreground to dark background or vice versa
one flat colour per layer, no printed detail
styles.prompt_fragment: rendered as a hand-cut layered paper shadow box: eight to twelve stacked sheets of matte coloured cardstock, each layer a flat silhouette with crisp knife-cut edges, physical gaps between layers casting soft graduated shadows, gentle side lighting, visible paper grain, tonal depth from pale foreground to deep background, photographed straight-on inside a shallow box frame
styles.avoid: Avoid glossy digital gradients and fake drop shadows; every tone must come from a separate flat paper layer, not airbrushed shading.
styles.feasibility_note: Layering and shadow depth render reliably; very fine filigree cut-outs merge or blur at small scale.
styles.short_de: Gestapelte Ebenen aus einfarbigem, als Silhouette geschnittenem Karton, deren Zwischenräume weiche Schatten und Tiefe erzeugen; Vorbild sind Guckkasten- und Tunnelbücher, als Schattenbox beliebt seit den 2010ern.
styles.short_en: Stacked layers of flat-coloured card cut as silhouettes, with soft shadows in the gaps creating depth; descended from tunnel books, popular as shadow boxes since the 2010s.
styles.era_de: Guckkästen des 18./19. Jh.; Schattenboxen seit den 2010ern
styles.era_en: 18th–19th-century peep shows; shadow boxes since the 2010s
markers_en: 8–12 stacked card layers with visible gaps
crisp cut edges with paper fibre
tonal depth from front to back

styles.era_origin: Kirigami is Japanese cut-and-fold paper craft; origamic architecture was formalised by architect Masahiro Chatani in the early 1980s.
visual_markers: single sheet of white card cut and folded at 90 degrees
forms rise from a folded card spine
monochrome white, shadows do the drawing
styles.prompt_fragment: constructed as a kirigami pop-up card from a single sheet of bright white cardstock, cut and folded at a ninety-degree spine so the form rises in stepped parallel planes, precise scalpel cuts, crisp mountain and valley folds, no colour, raking side light so cast shadows define every shape, plain neutral backdrop
styles.avoid: Avoid coloured printing and organic curved surfaces; the look depends on one white sheet, straight folds and shadows, otherwise it drifts into layered paper or paper sculpture.
styles.feasibility_note: The pop-up read is reliable, but the model often breaks single-sheet logic with floating pieces and impossible folds.
styles.short_de: Aus einem einzigen weißen Kartonblatt geschnittene und gefaltete Formen, die sich aus einem 90-Grad-Falz aufrichten und durch Schatten wirken; in den 1980ern von Masahiro Chatani in Japan entwickelt.
styles.short_en: Shadow-defined forms cut and folded from one sheet of white card, rising from a 90-degree fold; developed as origamic architecture by Masahiro Chatani in 1980s Japan.
markers_de: ein einziges weißes Kartonblatt, geschnitten und gefaltet
reines Weiß, Schatten zeichnen die Form
markers_en: single sheet of white card cut and folded

styles.era_origin: Movable books go back to medieval volvelles; illustrated pop-ups became mainstream in the 19th century, with a golden age in the 1980s-90s.
visual_markers: open book spread with elements standing up from the gutter
printed illustrated card pieces on glued tabs
white card edges and slight warping
styles.prompt_fragment: presented as a pop-up book spread: printed, illustrated cardstock pieces rising from the open centre fold on glued v-fold tabs, layered flaps and a pull-tab at the page edge, visible white card edges and slight warping, matte offset-printed colours, photographed at a three-quarter angle on a table in soft window light
styles.avoid: Avoid a flat illustration printed on a page; pieces must physically stand up with visible tabs and fold mechanics.
styles.feasibility_note: The open-book pop-up setup renders well; tabs and v-folds are often implied rather than mechanically plausible.
styles.short_de: Aufgeschlagene Buchseiten, aus deren Falz sich bedruckte Kartonteile auf Laschen aufrichten, mit Klappen und Zuglaschen; verbreitet seit dem 19. Jh., Boom in den 1980ern und 90ern.
styles.short_en: Open book spreads with printed card pieces standing up from the gutter on folded tabs, flaps and pull-tabs; mainstream since the 19th century, booming in the 1980s–90s.
markers_de: aufgeschlagene Doppelseite, Elemente stehen aus dem Falz
markers_en: open spread with elements rising from the gutter
printed card pieces on glued tabs

styles.era_origin: Paper filigree made by Renaissance religious communities; revived as a Regency-era pastime and again in 2010s papercraft illustration.
visual_markers: narrow paper strips glued on edge
tight and loose coils, teardrops, scrolls
styles.prompt_fragment: made entirely of quilling: narrow strips of coloured paper set on edge and glued to a flat card base, shapes outlined by standing strips and filled with tight coils, teardrops and scrolls, visible strip thickness and spiral interiors, soft directional light raking across the relief, photographed slightly from above
styles.avoid: Avoid flat paper cut-outs and smooth gradients; every form must be built from edge-on strips and coils or it collapses into layered paper art.
styles.feasibility_note: Coil-and-strip texture reads convincingly; faces and fine detail get lost and coil logic becomes inconsistent in dense areas.
styles.short_de: Schmale, hochkant gestellte Papierstreifen, zu Spiralen, Tropfen und Schnecken gerollt und auf Karton geklebt; Papierfiligran der Renaissance, wiederbelebt um 1800 und in den 2010ern.
styles.short_en: Narrow paper strips set on edge and rolled into coils, teardrops and scrolls on a card base; Renaissance paper filigree, revived around 1800 and in the 2010s.
styles.era_de: seit dem 15./16. Jh., Europa; Revivals um 1800 und in den 2010ern
styles.era_en: since the 15th–16th century, Europe; revivals c. 1800 and 2010s
markers_de: enge und lockere Spiralen, Tropfen, Schnecken
markers_en: tight and loose coils, teardrops, scrolls

styles.era_origin: Japanese paper folding documented since the Edo period; modern figurative and tessellation origami developed from the mid-20th century.
visual_markers: forms built from crisp folded planes, no cuts or glue
sharp crease lines and faceted geometry
solid or lightly patterned washi paper
paper thickness and soft crease ridges
figures as physical objects on a surface
styles.prompt_fragment: folded as origami from square sheets of solid-colour and lightly patterned paper: every form built from crisp creases and flat faceted planes, no cuts or glue, thin white edges where the paper turns, slight softness at crease ridges, small physical figures arranged on a plain tabletop, diffused daylight, moderate depth of field
styles.avoid: Avoid smooth low-poly 3D renders and printed textures on facets; real origami shows paper thickness, crease memory and one colour per side.
styles.feasibility_note: Folded paper figures are well learned; complex humans tend to become low-poly sculptures rather than foldable designs.
styles.short_de: Aus quadratischen Blättern gefaltete Figuren mit scharfen Kniffen und facettierten Flächen, ohne Schnitt und Kleber; in Japan seit der Edo-Zeit belegt, modernes Origami seit den 1950ern.
styles.short_en: Figures folded from square sheets with crisp creases and faceted planes, without cuts or glue; Japanese paper folding documented since the Edo period, modern origami from the 1950s.
styles.era_de: seit der Edo-Zeit (17. Jh.), Japan; modernes Origami ab den 1950ern
styles.era_en: since the Edo period (17th c.), Japan; modern origami from the 1950s
markers_de: klare gefaltete Flächen, ohne Schnitt und Kleber
markers_en: crisp folded planes, no cuts or glue
small physical figures on a surface

styles.era_origin: Printed cut-out card models (Modellbogen) date to the 19th century; the faceted low-poly papercraft look spread with 3D-unfolding software in the 2000s-2010s.
visual_markers: small gaps and lifted edges at joins
styles.prompt_fragment: assembled as a low-poly papercraft model from printed cardstock: triangular and polygonal facets folded along scored lines, flat colour printed on each facet, slight gaps and lifted edges at glued seams, white card edges showing on ridges, a few tabs visible, photographed on a cutting mat under even studio light
styles.avoid: Avoid clean digital low-poly rendering with perfect shading; facets must look like paper with seams, gaps and fold memory.
styles.feasibility_note: Faceted geometry is reliable; seams and tabs are dropped unless explicitly requested.
styles.sensitivity_note: 'Pepakura' is a software product name; use 'papercraft' in prompts.
styles.short_de: Facettierte Modelle aus bedrucktem Karton, entlang gerillter Linien gefaltet, mit Klebelaschen und kleinen Fugen; Wurzeln im Modellbogen des 19. Jh., als Low-Poly-Look verbreitet seit den 2000ern.
styles.short_en: Faceted models of printed card folded along scored lines, with glue tabs and gaps at the seams; rooted in 19th-century cut-out sheets, popular since the 2000s.
styles.era_de: Modellbogen seit dem 19. Jh.; Low-Poly-Look seit den 2000ern
styles.era_en: 19th-century cut-out sheets; low-poly look since the 2000s
markers_en: small gaps and lifted edges at joins
styles.sensitivity_de: „Pepakura“ ist ein Softwarename; im Prompt „papercraft“ verwenden.
styles.sensitivity_en: 'Pepakura' is a software product name; use 'papercraft' in prompts.

styles.era_origin: Mid-20th-century advertising and window-display craft; revived in 2010s editorial set design.
visual_markers: curved, scored and rolled sheets forming a bas-relief
mostly white or tightly limited palette
soft gradients only from paper curvature
slotted and glued joints, fringed edges
styles.prompt_fragment: sculpted from scored, curved and rolled sheets of heavy white paper as a shallow bas-relief: crisp curved score lines, cones and cylinders, fanned and fringed edges, joints slotted and glued, soft gradients only where the curved paper turns from the light, single warm key light from the upper side, plain white background
styles.avoid: Avoid stacked flat layers and printed colour; volume should come from bending and scoring paper, not layered cut-outs.
styles.feasibility_note: The white relief look is reliable; complex scoring drifts toward smooth plaster or a 3D-render look.
styles.short_de: Flache weiße Reliefs aus starkem Papier, geritzt, gebogen und gerollt, schattiert nur durch die Wölbung; Werbe- und Schaufensterhandwerk der Jahrhundertmitte, in den 2010ern im Editorial-Set-Design wiederbelebt.
styles.short_en: Shallow white reliefs of scored, curved and rolled heavy paper, shaded only by the bends; mid-20th-century advertising and display craft, revived in 2010s editorial set design.
styles.era_de: 1930er–1960er, Werbung und Schaufenster; Revival in den 2010ern
styles.era_en: 1930s–1960s, advertising and window display; revived in the 2010s
markers_en: curved and scored sheets forming a bas-relief

styles.era_origin: Long-standing architecture-school and children's craft material; a popular handmade 'cardboard world' set-design look since the 2010s.
visual_markers: brown corrugated board with exposed flutes on cut edges
leftover shipping print and pencil marks
styles.prompt_fragment: built from brown corrugated cardboard: exposed wavy flutes on every cut edge, slightly crooked box-cutter cuts, hot-glue beads, strips of masking tape, faint pencil guidelines and leftover shipping print on some panels, warm brown monochrome with occasional marker accents, photographed as a physical model under soft warm light
styles.avoid: Avoid clean smooth beige 3D surfaces; corrugation, tape and glue are what make it read as real cardboard.
styles.feasibility_note: Corrugated cardboard texture is well learned.
styles.short_de: Modelle aus brauner Wellpappe mit offenen Wellen an den Schnittkanten, schiefen Cutterschnitten, Heißkleber und Kreppband; Bastel- und Modellbaumaterial, seit den 2010ern auch als Set-Design-Look.
styles.short_en: Models of brown corrugated cardboard with exposed flutes, crooked cutter cuts, hot glue and tape; a classroom and model-making material, used as a set-design look since the 2010s.
styles.era_de: 20. Jh. bis heute; als Set-Design-Look seit den 2010ern
styles.era_en: 20th century to today; set-design look since the 2010s
markers_de: Wellpappe mit offenen Wellen an den Kanten
markers_en: corrugated board with exposed flutes on cut edges
leftover shipping print and pencil marks

styles.era_origin: Paper-pulp moulding from ancient China, later European decorative wares; a staple carnival and school craft.
visual_markers: newspaper strips visible under thin paint
matte poster paint with brush marks
styles.prompt_fragment: sculpted in papier-mâché: lumpy, softly rounded forms built from layered newspaper strips over a wire or balloon armature, faint printed newsprint showing through thin matte poster paint, visible brush strokes, uneven seams, small chips and drips, handmade imperfect proportions, photographed as a physical object in natural light
styles.avoid: Avoid smooth vinyl or 3D-render surfaces; the lumpy strip texture and matte hand-painted finish must show.
styles.feasibility_note: The handmade lumpy look works; the newspaper texture often disappears under smooth paint.
styles.short_de: Klumpig gerundete Formen aus geleimten Zeitungsstreifen oder Papiermasse über einem Gerüst, matt mit Plakatfarbe bemalt; aus dem alten China, heute für Karnevalsmasken und Schulbasteleien.
styles.short_en: Lumpy, rounded forms built from glued newspaper strips or pulp over an armature, painted in matte poster colours; from ancient China, used for carnival masks and school crafts.
styles.era_de: seit dem alten China; in Europa ab dem 17./18. Jh.
