styles.short_de: Mosaiktafel aus weißen, fein gravierten Muschelfiguren, in Bitumen gesetzt zwischen Lapislazuli und rotem Kalkstein, in Registern angeordnet wie auf der sogenannten Standarte von Ur.
styles.short_en: Mosaic panel of cut white shell figures with incised details set in bitumen with lapis lazuli and red limestone, arranged in registers as on the Standard of Ur.
markers_en: white shell silhouettes with incised lines

styles.era_origin: Late Antique and early Islamic Egypt, c. 3rd-9th century CE.
visual_markers: aubergine purple monochrome or bright polychrome
stepped blocky contours from the weave
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Late Antique Coptic tapestry fragment: tightly woven wool weft in aubergine purple, madder red, ochre and green on undyed beige linen, figures and vines enclosed in roundels and vertical bands, stepped blocky contours from the weave, large staring frontal eyes, frayed edges, holes and faded areas, mounted flat under museum light
styles.avoid: Avoid shaded medieval tapestry and millefleurs density; keep the small woven scale, linen ground and fragmentary archaeological state.
styles.feasibility_note: Weave texture renders, but can drift toward knitting or embroidery; stepped contours need emphasis.
styles.sensitivity_note: Some pieces carry Christian iconography; most are excavated grave goods.
styles.short_de: Kleine, in Wolle eingewirkte Motive auf ungefärbtem Leinen, oft purpurne Medaillons und Zierstreifen mit Figuren, Tieren und Ranken, aus dem spätantiken und frühislamischen Ägypten.
styles.short_en: Small tapestry-woven wool motifs on undyed linen, often purple roundels and bands with figures, animals and vines, from Late Antique and early Islamic Egypt.
markers_en: wool tapestry weave on undyed linen
styles.sensitivity_de: Viele Stücke tragen christliche Bildmotive, die meisten stammen aus Grabfunden.
styles.sensitivity_en: Many pieces carry Christian iconography and most come from excavated graves.

styles.era_origin: Gandhara (today Pakistan and Afghanistan), c. 1st-5th century CE, fusing Hellenistic and Indian traditions.
visual_markers: wavy hair and calm half-lidded faces
crowded narrative relief panels framed by Corinthian pilasters
styles.prompt_fragment: carved in the Gandharan Greco-Buddhist manner: grey-green schist with crisp yet eroded surfaces, Hellenistic deeply rippling drapery folds, wavy hair, calm half-lidded faces, crowded narrative relief panel framed by small Corinthian pilasters and acanthus, chipped edges and missing fragments, soft directional museum light
styles.avoid: Avoid white classical marble and glossy golden Buddha statues; keep the grey schist, the hybrid drapery and the archaeological damage.
styles.feasibility_note: Stone relief and drapery render well; keep the schist colour explicit.
styles.sensitivity_note: Buddhist sacred imagery: avoid decorative, humorous or commercial use of Buddha figures; looting and heritage destruction context in the region.
styles.short_de: Reliefs und Statuen aus grauem Schiefer und Stuck, die buddhistische Themen mit hellenistischem Faltenwurf, gewelltem Haar und ruhigen Gesichtern verbinden; Gandhara, 1. bis 5. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Grey schist and stucco reliefs and statues that combine Buddhist subjects with Hellenistic drapery, wavy hair and calm faces, made in Gandhara between the 1st and 5th centuries.
styles.era_de: 1.–5. Jh. n. Chr., Gandhara (heute Pakistan und Afghanistan)
styles.era_en: 1st–5th century CE, Gandhara (today Pakistan and Afghanistan)
styles.sensitivity_de: Buddhistische Sakralbilder: Buddhafiguren nicht dekorativ, humoristisch oder werblich einsetzen; Raubgrabungen und Kulturgutzerstörung in der Region mitbedenken.
styles.sensitivity_en: Buddhist sacred imagery: avoid decorative, humorous or commercial use of Buddha figures, and keep the looting and heritage destruction in the region in mind.

styles.era_origin: China, Shang and Western Zhou dynasties, c. 1600-771 BCE.
visual_markers: bilaterally symmetrical zoomorphic masks with bulging eyes
ground of dense square leiwen thunder spirals
notched casting flanges along the axis
mottled malachite green, azurite and cuprite red patina
styles.prompt_fragment: as an archaic Chinese ritual bronze: cast surface encrusted with mottled malachite green, turquoise and rust-red patina, motifs translated into bilaterally symmetrical zoomorphic masks with bulging eyes, background filled with dense square thunder-spiral patterns, raised notched flanges along the central axis, heavy monumental mass, low museum spotlight
styles.avoid: Avoid shiny new bronze and generic fantasy-dragon ornament; keep strict split symmetry, the spiral ground and archaeological patina.
styles.feasibility_note: Patina and casting texture are convincing; the split-face taotie logic is often muddled.
styles.short_de: Gegossene Ritualgefäße aus Bronze mit symmetrischen Taotie-Tiermasken auf einem Grund aus eckigen Donnermustern und grün-roter Patina, aus der Shang- und Westlichen Zhou-Zeit Chinas.
styles.short_en: Cast bronze ritual vessels covered with symmetrical taotie animal masks on a ground of square thunder spirals, with green and red patina, from Shang and Western Zhou China.
markers_en: symmetrical animal masks with bulging eyes

styles.era_origin: Rome and central Italy, 12th-13th century, building on Late Antique opus sectile.
visual_markers: cut slabs of red porphyry, green serpentine and white marble
large roundels linked by interlaced guilloche bands
fields of tiny triangles, hexagons and stars
styles.prompt_fragment: rendered as Cosmatesque opus sectile inlay: precisely cut slabs and tiny triangles of red porphyry, green serpentine, gold glass and white marble, large roundels linked by interlaced guilloche bands, geometric fields of hexagons and stars, worn polished floor surface with hairline cracks and missing tesserae, viewed flat from above
styles.avoid: Avoid figurative Roman pebble mosaic and pictorial Florentine pietra dura; keep pure geometry in thick cut stone.
styles.feasibility_note: Geometry and stone colours work; perfectly continuous interlace may break.
styles.short_de: Geometrische Einlegearbeit aus zugeschnittenem Porphyr, Serpentin und Marmor, mit Kreisscheiben und verschlungenen Bändern, in Kirchenböden und -ausstattung im mittelalterlichen Rom und Mittelitalien.
styles.short_en: Geometric inlay of cut porphyry, serpentine and marble with roundels linked by interlaced bands, laid in church floors and furnishings in medieval Rome and central Italy.
markers_de: roter Porphyr, grüner Serpentin, weißer Marmor
Felder aus kleinen Dreiecken und Sternen
markers_en: red porphyry, green serpentine, white marble
fields of small triangles and stars

styles.era_origin: Antwerp and the Northern Renaissance, c. 1510-1560.
visual_markers: very high horizon and bird's-eye panorama
rivers and estuaries winding to a distant sea
oil on oak panel with craquelure
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Northern Renaissance world landscape panel painting: elevated bird's-eye viewpoint with a very high horizon, fantastical sheer rock pinnacles, rivers and estuaries winding to a distant sea, strict colour recession from warm brown foreground through green middle ground to pale blue distance, minute figures, crisp oil glazes on oak panel, fine craquelure
styles.avoid: Avoid Romantic sublime drama and fantasy concept art; keep tiny figures, systematic three-zone recession and panel-painting precision.
styles.feasibility_note: Panoramic composition and colour zoning are well understood by the model.
styles.short_de: Panoramalandschaft aus erhöhter Sicht mit schroffen Felsen, Flüssen bis zum Meer, winzigen Figuren und braun-grün-blauer Farbstaffelung, gemalt in Antwerpen um 1510–1560.
styles.short_en: Panoramic landscape seen from a high viewpoint, with jagged rocks, rivers winding to the sea, tiny figures and brown-green-blue colour zones, painted in Antwerp c. 1510–1560.
markers_de: sehr hoher Horizont, Panorama aus Vogelschau
Flüsse, die sich zum fernen Meer winden
markers_en: rivers winding to a distant sea

styles.era_origin: Habsburg courts in Vienna and Prague, 1560s-1590s; revived by the Surrealists.
visual_markers: figure assembled entirely from realistic objects (fruit, flowers, books, animals)
each element readable up close, figure readable from afar
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Mannerist composite head painting: the subject's form assembled entirely from tightly packed, precisely painted natural objects such as fruits, vegetables, flowers, shells, books or tools, each element readable up close while the whole reads as a figure from afar, strict profile or bust pose, dark olive background, smooth sixteenth-century oil technique
styles.avoid: Avoid photographic food styling and cute cartoon fruit faces; keep it a painted Mannerist panel where the objects stay realistic.
styles.feasibility_note: Composite faces work well; the model sometimes adds literal eyes or skin instead of objects.
styles.short_de: Gemalter Kopf oder Brustbild aus naturgetreuen Früchten, Blumen, Tieren oder Gegenständen, erst aus der Distanz als Gesicht lesbar; entstanden am Habsburgerhof in Wien und Prag.
styles.short_en: Painted head or bust composed entirely of realistic fruit, flowers, animals or objects, readable as a face from afar, devised at the Habsburg courts in Vienna and Prague.
markers_en: objects readable up close, face from afar

visual_markers: few austere objects on a stone ledge or window niche
sharp tenebrist side light with hyperreal clarity
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Spanish Golden Age bodegón: few austere objects placed along a grey stone ledge or carved window niche, some suspended on strings, absolute black void behind, single sharp side light carving each form with hyperreal clarity, meditative rhythmic spacing, sober earth palette, smooth oil on canvas with fine craquelure
styles.avoid: Avoid lush Dutch abundance and moody food-blog photography; keep the sparse ascetic arrangement and the painted surface.
styles.feasibility_note: Lighting and sparse composition render reliably; the model may add too many objects unless restrained.
styles.short_de: Karges spanisches Stillleben aus wenigen Früchten, Gemüsen oder Gefäßen auf einer Steinbrüstung oder in einer Fensternische, scharf beleuchtet vor schwarzem Grund, um 1600–1670.
styles.short_en: Sparse Spanish still life of a few fruits, vegetables or vessels on a stone ledge or in a window niche, sharply lit against a black ground, c. 1600–1670.
markers_de: wenige Dinge auf Steinbrüstung oder in Nische
markers_en: few objects on a stone ledge or niche

styles.era_origin: Netherlands, c. 1490-1570, the painter of 's-Hertogenbosch and his many followers.
visual_markers: hybrid creatures part animal, part object
oversized fruits and shells used as buildings
glowing fiery skies behind dark silhouettes
thin translucent oil on oak panel
styles.prompt_fragment: as an early sixteenth-century Netherlandish fantastical panorama: hundreds of small busy vignettes populated by hybrid creatures part animal, part object, oversized fruits and shells used as buildings, glowing fiery skies behind dark silhouettes, high horizon, thin translucent oil glazes on oak panel, pale flesh tones, meticulous yet whimsical drawing
styles.avoid: Avoid modern dark fantasy and horror concept art; keep the moralising whimsy, small scale and panel technique.
styles.feasibility_note: Overall look works; coherence of many tiny vignettes degrades into mush.
styles.sensitivity_note: Religious hell imagery and frequent nudity.
styles.short_de: Niederländische Tafelbilder voller winziger Szenen mit Mischwesen, riesigen Früchten und brennenden Himmeln, von Hieronymus Bosch und seinen Nachfolgern, um 1490–1570.
styles.short_en: Netherlandish panel paintings crowded with tiny scenes of hybrid creatures, giant fruits and burning skies, by Hieronymus Bosch and his followers, c. 1490–1570.
markers_en: hybrid creatures of animal and object
giant fruits and shells as buildings
styles.sensitivity_de: Enthält religiöse Höllenbilder und häufig Nacktheit.
styles.sensitivity_en: Contains religious hell imagery and frequent nudity.

visual_markers: looping speech balloons with tiny script
engraved title and publisher imprint below the image
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Georgian-era satirical print: fluid etched outlines and cross-hatching on laid paper, loosely hand-applied watercolour washes in pale blue, rose and yellow, grotesquely exaggerated bodies and faces, looping speech balloons filled with tiny copperplate script, engraved title line and publisher imprint below, crowded theatrical staging, visible plate mark
styles.avoid: Avoid modern editorial cartoon line and digital flat colour; keep etched hatching, loose wash colouring and period lettering.
styles.feasibility_note: Style and colouring hold; small script inside balloons is garbled.
styles.sensitivity_note: Historic prints often contain ethnic, national and gender stereotypes; caricaturing real living persons carries defamation risk.
styles.short_de: Handkolorierte Radierung, die Politik und Gesellschaft mit grotesken Figuren, Sprechblasen und locker aufgetragenem Aquarell verspottet; verkauft von Londoner Druckläden um 1770–1830.
styles.short_en: Hand-coloured etching that mocks politics and society with grotesque figures, speech balloons and loose watercolour, sold by London print shops c. 1770–1830.
styles.sensitivity_de: Historische Blätter enthalten oft ethnische, nationale und geschlechtsbezogene Stereotype; Karikaturen lebender Personen können Persönlichkeitsrechte verletzen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Historic prints often contain ethnic, national and gender stereotypes; caricaturing living people carries a defamation risk.

visual_markers: forms dissolved into intersecting straight rays
cool blues and greens pierced by hot accents
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Russian Rayonist painting: forms dissolved into sheaves of intersecting straight rays of reflected light, strong crossing diagonals, thick linear brushstrokes, semi-abstract space vibrating with energy, cool blues, greens and greys pierced by orange and red, visible canvas texture
styles.avoid: Avoid Futurist motion repetition, Cubist faceting and digital light-ray effects; everything should become painted ray strokes.
styles.feasibility_note: Tends to slide into generic Futurism or lens-flare streaks.
styles.short_de: Malerei der russischen Avantgarde, in der sich Formen in sich kreuzende, gerade Lichtstrahlen auflösen, gemalt in linearen Strichen; 1912 in Moskau von Larionow und Gontscharowa begründet.
styles.short_en: Russian avant-garde painting in which forms dissolve into crossing straight rays of reflected light in linear strokes; founded by Larionov and Goncharova in Moscow in 1912.
markers_de: kühles Blau und Grün mit heißen Akzenten
markers_en: cool blues and greens with hot accents

styles.era_origin: Developed within Surrealism in 1927 as the painted counterpart of frottage.
visual_markers: wet oil scraped over hidden textured objects
raised imprints of wood grain, mesh, string
styles.prompt_fragment: made with the Surrealist grattage technique: layered wet oil paint scraped with a blade over hidden textured objects such as planks, wire mesh, string and leaves, producing raised rhythmic imprints, ghostly woodgrain and lattice patterns, petrified-forest forms against a dark mysterious ground, muted browns, ochres and night blues, scratched highlights
styles.avoid: Avoid photographic texture overlays and generic grunge; keep scraped oil relief and dreamlike imprinted forms.
styles.feasibility_note: Specific scraped-imprint logic is hard; often becomes generic distressed texture.
styles.short_de: Maltechnik, bei der nasse Ölfarbe von einer Leinwand über strukturierten Gegenständen abgeschabt wird, sodass deren Abdruck stehen bleibt; 1927 von Max Ernst in Paris entwickelt.
styles.short_en: Painting technique in which wet oil paint is scraped off a canvas laid over textured objects, leaving their imprints; developed by Max Ernst in Paris in 1927.
markers_de: Abdrücke von Holzmaserung, Gitter und Schnur
markers_en: scraped oil paint over hidden textures
imprints of wood grain, mesh and string

styles.era_origin: Paris Surrealists, from c. 1925.
visual_markers: vertical figure built from 3-4 horizontal segments
each segment in a different hand and medium
abrupt style and scale shifts at the joins
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Surrealist exquisite corpse drawing: a single vertical figure assembled from three or four horizontal segments, each in a different hand and medium such as pencil, ink, crayon or cut collage, abrupt style and scale shifts where lines barely meet at the joins, visible horizontal fold creases in the sheet, playful absurd anatomy, aged paper
styles.avoid: Avoid seamless hybrid creature design; the joins, fold lines and medium shifts must stay visible.
styles.feasibility_note: Model tends to unify styles across segments; spell out each segment's medium.
styles.short_de: Gemeinschaftszeichnung: Mehrere Personen zeichnen nacheinander je einen Abschnitt einer Figur auf gefaltetem Papier, ohne die übrigen Teile zu sehen; Pariser Surrealisten, ab etwa 1925.
styles.short_en: Collaborative drawing in which several people each draw one section of a figure on folded paper without seeing the others, played by the Paris Surrealists from about 1925.
markers_de: pro Abschnitt andere Hand und Technik
markers_en: a different hand and medium in each segment

styles.era_origin: 1930s Surrealism, with 16th-17th-century anthropomorphic landscape precedents.
visual_markers: one scene readable as two images
figures, rocks or shadows forming a larger hidden form
infinite pale plain and long shadows
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Surrealist double image: one scene painted so its elements, figures, rocks, architecture and shadows, simultaneously form a second, larger hidden image, smooth veristic oil technique with academic precision, infinite pale plain under a clear sky, long late-afternoon shadows, eerie stillness, both readings equally convincing
styles.avoid: Avoid optical-illusion clipart and the melting-clock surreal cliché; keep both readings subtle but resolvable.
styles.feasibility_note: True dual readings are hard for current models; one reading usually dominates.
styles.short_de: Präzise gemalte Szene, deren Figuren, Felsen und Schatten zugleich ein zweites, größeres Bild ergeben; von Salvador Dalí in den 1930er-Jahren als paranoisch-kritische Methode entwickelt.
styles.short_en: Precisely painted scene whose figures, rocks and shadows also form a second, larger image, developed by Salvador Dalí in the 1930s as his paranoiac-critical method.
markers_de: Einzelteile bilden eine größere verborgene Figur
weite, helle Ebene mit langen Schatten
markers_en: one scene readable as two images
elements forming a larger hidden figure
vast pale plain with long shadows

styles.era_origin: São Paulo, 1920s, after the 1922 Modern Art Week and the 1928 Anthropophagic Manifesto.
visual_markers: stylised cacti, palms and banana leaves
candy pink, sky blue, leaf green and ochre
styles.prompt_fragment: as 1920s Brazilian Anthropophagic modernism: simplified, swollen, smoothly modelled rounded forms, enlarged limbs and small heads, stylised cacti, palms and banana leaves, flattened geometric hillside towns, clean outlines, tropical palette of candy pink, sky blue, leaf green, ochre and rust, matte oil on canvas, calm sunlit stillness
styles.avoid: Avoid generic Art Deco and naive art; keep the tropical modernist palette and soft volumetric distortion.
styles.feasibility_note: Rounded forms and palette are easy to steer.
styles.sensitivity_note: The movement metaphorically used Indigenous 'cannibalism'; avoid exoticising Indigenous people.
styles.short_de: Brasilianische Malerei der Moderne mit prallen, weich gerundeten Figuren, stilisierten Kakteen und Palmen und tropischer Palette aus Rosa, Blau und Grün; Zentrum São Paulo, 1920er-Jahre.
styles.short_en: Brazilian modernist painting with swollen, smoothly rounded figures, stylised cacti and palms and a tropical palette of pink, blue and green, centred in São Paulo in the 1920s.
markers_en: stylised cacti, palms and banana leaves
candy pink, sky blue and leaf green
styles.sensitivity_de: Die Bewegung nutzte indigenen „Kannibalismus“ als Metapher; indigene Menschen nicht exotisierend darstellen.
styles.sensitivity_en: The movement used Indigenous 'cannibalism' as a metaphor; avoid exoticising Indigenous people.

styles.era_origin: Spain, Italy and France, late 1940s-1960s.
visual_markers: heavy wall-like crusts of sand, plaster, marble dust
patched burlap sacking, scorched holes, tar
earth greys, ochre, black with a single red accent
styles.prompt_fragment: as a postwar European matter painting: heavy wall-like surface built from sand, plaster, marble dust and glue, cracked crusts, patched burlap sacking, scorched holes and tar drips, incised scratches and cryptic signs, mostly earth greys, ochres and black with a single blood-red accent, raking light emphasising relief
styles.avoid: Avoid gestural action-painting splashes and decorative textured wall art; keep it sober, raw and material.
styles.feasibility_note: Material crusts and burlap render convincingly; motif legibility requires care.
styles.short_de: Abstrakte Malerei aus Sand, Gips, Sackleinen, Teer und anderen Materialien, aufgebaut zu krustigen, versehrten Oberflächen in Erdtönen; eine Richtung des europäischen Informel der Nachkriegszeit.
styles.short_en: Abstract painting built up from sand, plaster, burlap, tar and other matter into crusty, scarred surfaces in earthy tones, a strand of postwar European Informel.
markers_de: dicke Krusten aus Sand und Gips
erdiges Grau und Ocker mit rotem Akzent
markers_en: thick crusts of sand and plaster
patched burlap, burn holes and tar
earth greys and ochres with a red accent

visual_markers: clean vertical slashes or punched hole constellations
motif implied only by cut arrangement
styles.prompt_fragment: as Italian Spatialist art: a taut monochrome canvas in a single saturated colour, its surface pierced by clean vertical slashes or constellations of punched holes, black depth visible through the openings, canvas edges curling inward, soft shadows from gallery light, the motif suggested only by the arrangement of cuts and holes
styles.avoid: Avoid torn paper or damaged poster looks; cuts must be few, deliberate and elegant.
styles.feasibility_note: Slashed canvas is well known; motif-by-holes needs a simple subject.
styles.short_de: Einfarbige Leinwände mit glatten Schnitten oder Lochgruppen, die das Bild in den realen Raum öffnen; von Lucio Fontana ab 1946 in Buenos Aires und Mailand begründet.
styles.short_en: Monochrome canvases slit with clean cuts or pierced with clusters of holes that open the picture into real space; Lucio Fontana's movement in Milan after 1946.
markers_en: clean vertical slashes or punched-hole clusters

styles.era_origin: Düsseldorf, founded 1957/58, international network until 1966.
visual_markers: perforated metal raster screens and embossed grids
light and shadow as the actual material
styles.prompt_fragment: as a ZERO group work: white-on-white relief where the motif emerges only through light and shadow, built from rhythmic fields of nails, perforated metal raster screens, embossed grids, polished aluminium and soot traces, raking light creating vibration and moiré, serene, immaterial, gallery wall presentation
styles.avoid: Avoid colourful Op Art and sterile 3D renders; keep handmade irregularity and light-as-material.
styles.feasibility_note: Nail fields and white relief work; making a motif legible through shadow alone is hard.
styles.short_de: Weiße Reliefs, Nagelfelder, Rasterbleche und polierte Metalle, bei denen Licht und Schatten zum eigentlichen Material werden; Düsseldorfer Gruppe und internationales Netzwerk, 1957–1966.
styles.short_en: White-on-white reliefs, nail fields, perforated grids and polished metal in which light and shadow become the material; Düsseldorf group and international network, 1957–1966.
markers_en: perforated metal grids and embossed rasters
raking light and shadow as material

styles.era_origin: Ashiya/Osaka, Japan, 1954-1972.
visual_markers: glossy industrial enamel smeared by feet
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Gutai-style work: traces of the body wrestling with materials, glossy industrial enamel smeared by bare feet, splattered from thrown bottles, dragged by ropes, puddles and drips, paper screens burst through, mud and gravel on raw unprimed canvas, bright red, yellow and black, the motif barely legible within violent physical traces
styles.avoid: Avoid tidy drip painting and decorative alcohol ink; keep brutal physical evidence and enamel gloss.
styles.feasibility_note: Enamel gloss and splatter render; footprints and burst paper need explicit wording.
styles.short_de: Rohe, körperliche Abstraktion aus Fußspuren, zerschellten Farbflaschen und durchbrochenen Papierwänden, mit glänzendem Lack, Schlamm und Rinnspuren; japanische Avantgardegruppe aus Ashiya, 1954–1972.
styles.short_en: Raw, physical abstraction made with feet, thrown paint bottles and bodies bursting through paper, in glossy enamel, mud and drips; Japanese avant-garde group from Ashiya, 1954–1972.
markers_de: Schlamm und Kies auf roher Leinwand
markers_en: glossy industrial enamel smeared by feet
mud and gravel on raw canvas

styles.era_origin: New York, mid-1960s.
visual_markers: industrial materials: plywood, aluminium, steel plates, firebricks, fluorescent tubes
strict grids or rows on floor or wall
styles.prompt_fragment: as a 1960s Minimal Art installation: the motif reduced to serial identical units of industrially fabricated plywood, anodised aluminium, steel plates, firebricks or fluorescent tubes, arranged in strict grids or rows directly on a white gallery floor or wall, no handmade trace, even daylight, documentary installation photograph
styles.avoid: Avoid lifestyle minimalism and glossy 3D renders; keep literal industrial materials, seriality and documentary photo.
styles.feasibility_note: Gallery installations render well; avoid CGI sterility.
styles.short_de: Gleichförmige, industriell gefertigte Elemente wie Sperrholzkästen, Stahlplatten, Schamottsteine oder Leuchtstoffröhren in strengen Reihen und Rastern; New Yorker Skulptur der Mitte der 1960er-Jahre.
styles.short_en: Identical industrially made units such as plywood boxes, steel plates, firebricks or fluorescent tubes set out in strict rows or grids; New York sculpture of the mid-1960s.
markers_de: Industriematerial: Sperrholz, Aluminium, Stahl, Schamottstein, Leuchtstoffröhre
strenge Reihen oder Raster auf Boden oder Wand
markers_en: industrial materials: plywood, aluminium, steel, firebrick, fluorescent tube
strict rows or grids on floor or wall

styles.era_origin: International, late 1960s-1970s.
visual_markers: small black-and-white snapshots mounted in a grid
sober sans-serif or typewriter text on white
styles.prompt_fragment: presented as 1960s-70s Conceptual Art: the subject replaced or accompanied by deadpan documentation, typewritten instructions, a dictionary-style definition, index cards, stamped forms and small black-and-white snapshots mounted in a neat grid on white board, sober sans-serif or typewriter text, no aesthetic flourish, archival gallery presentation
styles.avoid: Avoid stylish modern typographic posters and meme layouts; keep it bureaucratic, typewritten and unglamorous.
styles.feasibility_note: Layout works; longer typewritten text loses legibility.
styles.short_de: Kunst als Idee, vermittelt durch Schreibmaschinentexte, Lexikondefinitionen, Formulare, Karteikarten und kleine Schwarzweißfotos im nüchternen Raster; internationale Bewegung der späten 1960er und der 1970er.
styles.short_en: Art as idea, shown through typewritten instructions, definitions, forms, index cards and small black-and-white photos in plain grids; international movement of the late 1960s and 1970s.
markers_de: nüchterne Grotesk- oder Schreibmaschinenschrift auf Weiß
markers_en: small black-and-white photos in a grid
plain sans-serif or typewriter text on white

styles.era_origin: Turin, Rome and Genoa, 1967-early 1970s.
visual_markers: humble raw materials: rags, coal, earth, burlap, lead, twigs, fresh vegetables
confrontation with classical plaster fragments or mirrors
floor installations in worn whitewashed rooms
styles.prompt_fragment: as an Arte Povera installation: humble raw materials, piles of rags, coal, earth, burlap, lead sheets, broken glass, twigs and fresh vegetables, a thin neon line, confronted with a plaster classical fragment or a mirror, arranged on the floor of a worn whitewashed space, documentary photograph, soft natural light
styles.avoid: Avoid tidy found-object assemblage and trash art; keep the poetic clash of organic, industrial and classical.
styles.feasibility_note: Materials render well; the poetic sparseness can become cluttered.
styles.short_de: Installationen aus einfachen Materialien wie Lumpen, Kohle, Erde, Blei, Zweigen und Gemüse, kombiniert mit Neon, Spiegeln oder antiken Gipsabgüssen; 1967 benannte italienische Bewegung.
styles.short_en: Installations of humble materials such as rags, coal, earth, lead, twigs and vegetables, set against neon, mirrors or classical casts; Italian movement named in 1967.
markers_de: Lumpen, Kohle, Erde, Jute, Blei, Zweige, Gemüse
antiker Gipsabguss oder Spiegel als Gegenpol
markers_en: rags, coal, earth, burlap, lead, twigs, vegetables
classical plaster cast or mirror as counterpoint
floor installation in a worn whitewashed room

styles.era_origin: International, from the 1962 Wiesbaden festival onward.
visual_markers: cheap black offset on newsprint or card
dense grids of mixed typefaces and tiny photos
plastic boxes of numbered oddments with printed labels
styles.prompt_fragment: as Fluxus ephemera: cheap black offset printing on newsprint or card, dense grid of mixed typefaces and tiny photos, a plastic box of numbered oddments with printed labels, short absurd event-score instructions, rubber stamps, deadpan humour, DIY mail-order multiples, slightly misaligned paste-up
styles.avoid: Avoid punk zine chaos and polished Swiss layouts; keep the deadpan, game-like boxed-multiple character.
styles.feasibility_note: Grid layout works; text is pseudo-legible.
styles.short_de: Billig gedruckte Schwarzweiß-Ephemera, Schachteln mit beschrifteten Kleinobjekten und knappe, absurde Handlungsanweisungen; internationales Netzwerk ab den Wiesbadener Festspielen 1962.

styles.era_origin: China, Tang dynasty, peak c. 680-755.
visual_markers: runny lead glazes in amber, copper green and cream
unglazed buff clay at the base
styles.prompt_fragment: as Tang dynasty sancai glazed earthenware: lively modelled figure forms covered in runny lead glazes of amber brown, copper green and creamy white that streak and pool, splashed and dappled patterns, unglazed buff clay at the base, crackled glossy surface, museum lighting
styles.avoid: Avoid modern glossy ceramics and porcelain; keep drippy three-colour glaze and archaic modelling.
styles.feasibility_note: Glaze drips and ceramic sculpture render convincingly.
styles.sensitivity_note: Funerary objects (mingqi); market full of looting and forgeries.
styles.short_de: Irdenware-Figuren und -Gefäße unter laufenden Bleiglasuren in Bernstein, Grün und Creme, die Schlieren und Pfützen bilden; chinesische Grabkeramik der Tang-Dynastie, Blüte um 680–755.
styles.short_en: Earthenware figures and vessels under runny lead glazes of amber, green and cream that streak and pool; Chinese tomb ceramics of the Tang dynasty, peaking around 680–755.
markers_de: laufende Bleiglasuren in Bernstein, Kupfergrün und Creme
markers_en: runny lead glazes in amber, copper green and cream
unglazed buff clay at the base
styles.sensitivity_de: Es handelt sich um Grabbeigaben (Mingqi); der Markt ist voller Raubgrabungsfunde und Fälschungen.
styles.sensitivity_en: These are funerary objects (mingqi), and the market is full of looted pieces and forgeries.

styles.era_origin: China from the Han dynasty; Japan and Korea from the 7th century; living practice.
visual_markers: bold black ink on absorbent white paper
pressure variation from wet blots to dry flying-white streaks
energetic cursive rhythm in vertical columns
styles.prompt_fragment: as East Asian brush calligraphy: the motif written or suggested by bold black ink strokes on absorbent white xuan or washi paper, varying pressure from fat wet blots to dry flying-white streaks, energetic cursive rhythm, vertical columns, generous white space, one or two small vermilion seal stamps, ink bleeding into fibres
styles.avoid: Avoid pseudo-Chinese fake characters and decorative 'Asian' fonts; if characters appear, they must be real.
styles.feasibility_note: Brush dynamics are good; real characters are frequently malformed.
styles.sensitivity_note: Malformed or nonsensical characters are a common offensive cliché; have native readers check text.
styles.short_de: Schwarze Tuschezeichen, mit weichem Pinsel auf saugfähiges Papier geschrieben, von nassen Klecksen bis zum trockenen 'fliegenden Weiß', mit roten Siegeln; China seit der Han-Zeit, ebenso Korea und Japan.
styles.short_en: Black ink characters brushed on absorbent paper, from wet blots to dry 'flying white', with vermilion seals; Chinese art since the Han dynasty, also in Korea and Japan.
styles.era_de: China seit der Han-Dynastie, später Korea und Japan; bis heute
styles.era_en: China since the Han dynasty, later Korea and Japan; living practice
markers_de: kräftige schwarze Tusche auf saugfähigem Papier
Druckwechsel von nassen Klecksen bis zum trockenen 'fliegenden Weiß'
markers_en: bold black ink on absorbent white paper
pressure shifts from wet blots to dry flying white
energetic cursive rhythm in vertical columns
styles.sensitivity_de: Verunstaltete oder sinnlose Schriftzeichen sind ein verbreitetes, kränkendes Klischee; Texte von Muttersprachlern prüfen lassen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Malformed or nonsensical characters are a common, offensive cliché; have native readers check any text.

styles.era_origin: Proportioned scripts codified from the 10th century; Ottoman refinement 15th-19th century.
visual_markers: sweeping verticals and deep curved bowls
burnished cream paper with gold rules
styles.prompt_fragment: as classical Arabic calligraphy: stacked, interlaced letterforms in black ink with sweeping verticals and deep curved bowls, vowel marks used as delicate ornament, balanced symmetrical or mirrored composition on burnished cream paper framed by gold rules and a marbled border, reed-pen sharpness, quiet manuscript elegance
styles.avoid: Avoid random pseudo-Arabic squiggles and generic swirly fonts; keep authentic reed-pen letter construction.
styles.feasibility_note: Arabic letter joining and words are usually garbled.
styles.sensitivity_note: Often carries Qur'anic verses and divine names; never place on inappropriate objects; incorrect text offends.
styles.short_de: Gestapelte, verschlungene arabische Buchstaben mit schwungvollen Senkrechten, tiefen Bögen und ornamentalen Vokalzeichen auf geglättetem Papier mit Goldlinien; Proportionsschriften seit dem 10. Jh., osmanisch verfeinert.
styles.short_en: Stacked, interlaced Arabic letters with sweeping verticals, deep bowls and ornamental vowel marks on burnished paper with gold rules; proportioned scripts since the 10th century, refined by Ottomans.
styles.era_de: seit dem 10. Jh.; osmanische Blüte 15.–19. Jh.
styles.era_en: since the 10th century; Ottoman refinement 15th–19th century
markers_en: sweeping verticals and deep curved bowls
burnished cream paper with gold rules
styles.sensitivity_de: Trägt oft Koranverse und Gottesnamen; nie auf unpassende Gegenstände setzen, fehlerhafter Text kann verletzen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Often carries Qur'anic verses and divine names; never place it on inappropriate objects, and incorrect text can offend.

styles.era_origin: Iran and Central Asia, from c. 13th century; prominent in Timurid architecture.
visual_markers: letters built on a strict square grid
glazed bricks or tiles in turquoise, cobalt and buff
styles.prompt_fragment: as square Kufic: letterforms constructed on a strict square grid of right angles, forming maze-like blocks with rotational symmetry, rendered in glazed tiles or brick in turquoise, cobalt blue and unglazed buff terracotta, pixel-like geometry, slight variations in tile colour and grout lines, architectural wall surface
styles.avoid: Avoid generic pixel art and Greek key meanders; keep it a script system in glazed brick.
styles.feasibility_note: Grid geometry works; actual readable words are unlikely.
styles.sensitivity_note: Frequently encodes sacred names; invented text should not mimic sacred formulas.
styles.short_de: Arabische Schrift, auf strengem Quadratraster zu labyrinthartigen Blöcken gebaut, in glasierten Ziegeln oder Fliesen in Türkis, Kobalt und Ocker; Iran und Zentralasien seit dem 12. Jh.
styles.short_en: Arabic script built on a square grid into maze-like blocks, in glazed brick or tile of turquoise, cobalt and buff; Iran and Central Asia since the 12th century.
styles.era_de: seit dem 12. Jh., Iran und Zentralasien; Blüte unter Ilchaniden und Timuriden
styles.era_en: from the 12th century, Iran and Central Asia; peak under Ilkhanids and Timurids
markers_de: glasierte Ziegel oder Fliesen in Türkis, Kobalt und Ocker
markers_en: letters built on a strict square grid
glazed brick or tile in turquoise, cobalt and buff
styles.sensitivity_de: Bildet oft heilige Namen ab; erfundener Text sollte keine religiösen Formeln nachahmen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Often spells sacred names; invented text should not imitate sacred formulas.

styles.era_origin: China, matured in the Song and Yuan dynasties (10th-14th century).
visual_markers: oblique parallel projection without vanishing point
meticulous roof tiles, bracket sets and balustrades
light mineral colours on aged silk
styles.prompt_fragment: as Chinese jiehua ruled-line painting: architecture and objects drawn with ruler-straight fine ink lines in oblique parallel projection, meticulous roof tiles, bracket sets and balustrades, no vanishing point, light mineral colours on aged silk, small figures in pavilions, misty landscape fringe, handscroll format
styles.avoid: Avoid Western perspective drawing and freehand shan shui; keep ruler precision and parallel projection.
styles.feasibility_note: Parallel projection tends to slip into perspective.
styles.short_de: Architekturdarstellung mit linealgeraden, feinen Tuschelinien in schräger Parallelprojektion, mit detailreichen Dächern, Konsolen und Balustraden auf Seide; in der Song- und Yuan-Zeit ausgereifte chinesische Gattung.
styles.short_en: Architecture drawn with ruler-straight fine ink lines in oblique parallel projection, with detailed roofs, brackets and balustrades on silk; Chinese genre perfected in the Song and Yuan dynasties.
markers_en: oblique parallel projection, no vanishing point
meticulous roof tiles, brackets and balustrades
light mineral colours on aged silk

styles.era_origin: Huxian, Shaanxi from 1958; Jinshan, Shanghai from the 1970s.
visual_markers: high tilted viewpoint with many simultaneous activities
embroidery- and papercut-derived pattern on every surface
styles.prompt_fragment: as Chinese peasant painting: bright flat gouache in saturated reds, greens, yellows and blues, a high tilted viewpoint showing many simultaneous activities, every surface filled with decorative pattern borrowed from embroidery and papercut, naive stacked perspective, cheerful bold outlines, harvest-festival energy
styles.avoid: Avoid generic naive art and Cultural Revolution propaganda gloss; keep folk-pattern density and flat bright colour.
styles.feasibility_note: Flat folk colour and patterns render reliably.
styles.sensitivity_note: Early Huxian works served state propaganda; avoid uncritical political use.
styles.short_de: Leuchtende, flächige Gouacheszenen aus hoher, gekippter Sicht, voller Betriebsamkeit und mit Stickerei- und Scherenschnittmustern überzogen; Bauernmalerei aus Huxian (ab 1958) und Jinshan (ab den 1970ern).
styles.short_en: Bright flat gouache scenes from a high tilted viewpoint, crowded with activity and covered in embroidery and papercut patterns; rural painting from Huxian (from 1958) and Jinshan (1970s).
styles.era_de: ab 1958 Huxian (Shaanxi), ab den 1970ern Jinshan (Shanghai), China
styles.era_en: from 1958 Huxian (Shaanxi), from the 1970s Jinshan (Shanghai), China

Stickerei- und Scherenschnittmuster auf jeder Fläche

embroidery and papercut patterns on every surface
styles.sensitivity_de: Frühe Huxian-Bilder dienten der Staatspropaganda; nicht unkritisch politisch einsetzen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Early Huxian works served state propaganda; avoid uncritical political use.

styles.era_origin: Korea, late Joseon dynasty, 18th-19th century.
visual_markers: pale washes of light blue, red and ochre
album leaf on toned mulberry paper with seal
styles.prompt_fragment: as late Joseon Korean genre painting: lively everyday figures drawn with economical, confident ink brush lines and pale washes of light blue, red and ochre, almost no background beyond a few strokes of ground or a tree, humorous candid observation, open circular composition, album leaf on toned mulberry paper with a small seal
styles.avoid: Avoid Chinese gongbi detail and generic 'oriental ink' looks; keep sparse sketchiness, humour and blank ground.
styles.feasibility_note: Sparse brush figures render well; costume details may drift to Chinese or Japanese.
styles.short_de: Ungeschönte, humorvolle Alltagsszenen in sparsamen Pinsellinien und blassen Lavierungen in Blau, Rot und Ocker auf fast leerem Grund; koreanische Malerei der späten Joseon-Zeit, 18.–19. Jh.
styles.short_en: Candid, humorous everyday scenes in economical brush lines and pale washes of blue, red and ochre on almost empty ground; Korean painting of the late Joseon, 18th–19th century.
markers_de: blasse Lavierungen in Hellblau, Rot und Ocker
Albumblatt auf getöntem Maulbeerpapier mit Siegel
markers_en: pale washes of light blue, red and ochre
album leaf on toned mulberry paper with seal

styles.era_origin: Gujarat and Rajasthan, c. 12th-16th century.
visual_markers: angular figures with the far eye projecting beyond the face
styles.prompt_fragment: as Western Indian Jain manuscript painting: flat angular figures in three-quarter profile with the far eye projecting beyond the face, pointed noses, puffed chests, brilliant vermilion red ground, lapis blue and gold highlights, wiry black outlines, horizontal folio with blocks of script on cream paper, small decorative roundels
styles.avoid: Avoid lush Mughal naturalism and lyrical Rajput style; keep angular stylisation and the projecting eye.
styles.feasibility_note: The projecting far eye is often lost; script is pseudo-text.
styles.sensitivity_note: Sacred Jain texts and Tirthankara images; avoid trivial or commercial use of holy figures.
styles.short_de: Kantige Figuren mit über das Profil ragendem fernem Auge, drahtigen Konturen, zinnoberrotem Grund, Lapisblau und Gold neben Textblöcken; Jaina-Handschriften aus Gujarat und Rajasthan, 12.–16. Jh.
styles.short_en: Angular figures with the far eye jutting past the profile, wiry outlines, vermilion grounds, lapis and gold beside text blocks; Jain manuscripts from Gujarat and Rajasthan, 12th–16th century.
markers_de: kantige Figuren mit herausragendem fernem Auge
markers_en: angular figures with the far eye projecting beyond the face
styles.sensitivity_de: Illustriert heilige Jaina-Texte und Tirthankara-Bilder; heilige Figuren nicht trivial oder kommerziell verwenden.
styles.sensitivity_en: Illustrates sacred Jain texts and Tirthankara images; avoid trivial or commercial use of holy figures.

visual_markers: minimal geometry: circles, ovals, triangles, radiating bands
flat saturated gouache in saffron, black, red, turquoise
styles.prompt_fragment: as Rajasthani tantric painting: meditative minimal geometry of concentric circles, ovals, triangles and radiating bands in flat saturated gouache of saffron, black, red and turquoise, painted on found old paper with faint handwriting, stains and creases, strict central symmetry, quiet hand-painted edges
styles.avoid: Avoid psychedelic mandala clipart and glowing digital sacred geometry; keep matte hand painting on aged paper.
styles.feasibility_note: Simple geometry and paper texture render well.
styles.sensitivity_note: Ritual diagrams with sacred function; avoid decorative branding and disrespectful contexts.

round faces with large almond eyes

styles.era_origin: Bhil communities of Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Rajasthan; on paper and canvas since the 1980s.
visual_markers: flat silhouettes filled entirely with multicoloured dots
styles.prompt_fragment: as Bhil painting: simple flat silhouettes of figures, animals and trees filled entirely with rows of small multicoloured dots, bright yellow, red, blue, white and green on a solid saturated background, no shading or perspective, playful decorative rhythm, acrylic on paper or canvas with slight dot irregularities
styles.avoid: Avoid Aboriginal dot-painting composition and Gond line-and-dash fills; keep dotted silhouettes on colour fields.

styles.sensitivity_note: Adivasi community art; do not conflate with Aboriginal dot painting or pass off as authentic.

rows of small figures, animals, sun and moon

dramatic dancing poses in dense narrative

styles.era_origin: Southern Africa, painted over many thousands of years into the 19th century.
visual_markers: delicate fine-line figures in red ochre, black, white
sandstone grain, lichen and mineral streaks
styles.prompt_fragment: as Southern African San rock painting: delicate fine-line figures in red ochre, black and white painted on a sandstone overhang, elongated running and dancing figures, finely shaded antelopes, flowing lines of movement, faded fragments overlapping older layers, rock grain, lichen and mineral streaks showing through

styles.feasibility_note: Rock texture and fine ochre lines render well.
styles.sensitivity_note: Sacred heritage of San peoples; avoid the outdated term 'Bushman' and spiritual misappropriation.

styles.era_origin: Igbo women's body and wall painting, southeastern Nigeria; modernised by the Nsukka School from the 1970s.

indigo-black dye on skin, wall or paper
styles.prompt_fragment: as Igbo uli drawing: delicate, fluid black lines and small solid motifs such as spirals, crescents, ladders, stars and serpentine curves placed asymmetrically with generous empty space, translucent indigo-black dye or ink on pale paper or an earth-washed wall, economical elegant linework, modernist restraint
styles.avoid: Avoid dense mehndi ornament and generic tribal tattoo; keep sparse, asymmetric lyrical lines.
styles.feasibility_note: Model tends to fill space; stress emptiness.
styles.sensitivity_note: Body painting tradition of Igbo women; respectful context.
styles.short_de: Sparsame, fließende schwarze Linien mit kleinen Spiralen, Mondsicheln und Sternen auf viel Leerraum; Körper- und Wandmalerei der Igbo-Frauen aus Südostnigeria, seit den 1970ern modern weitergeführt.
styles.short_en: Sparse, fluid black lines with small spirals, crescents and stars in open space; Igbo women's body and wall painting from southeastern Nigeria, modernised since the 1970s.
styles.era_de: traditionell, Südostnigeria; ab den 1970ern von der Nsukka-Schule aufgegriffen
styles.era_en: Traditional, southeastern Nigeria; taken up by the Nsukka School from the 1970s
markers_de: indigoschwarzer Farbstoff auf Haut, Wand oder Papier
markers_en: small solid motifs: spirals, crescents, stars
indigo-black dye on skin, wall or paper
styles.sensitivity_de: Wurzelt in der Körpermalerei von Igbo-Frauen; respektvoll einsetzen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Rooted in Igbo women's body painting; use it in a respectful context.

styles.era_origin: Senufo people, Korhogo, Côte d'Ivoire; widely produced since the 1960s.
styles.prompt_fragment: as Senufo Korhogo cloth: stylised silhouette figures, masked dancers, birds, fish and reptiles painted in dark brown-black fermented mud dye on off-white handspun cotton, narrow handwoven strips stitched together with visible seams, slightly bleeding edges, flat graphic symmetry, sparse spacing, rough natural fibres
styles.avoid: Avoid Bogolan's dark ground with white geometric motifs; keep dark figurative silhouettes on light strip cloth.
styles.feasibility_note: Silhouettes on cloth render reliably.
styles.sensitivity_note: Some imagery relates to Senufo Poro society and masks; avoid misrepresenting sacred content.
styles.short_de: Handgesponnener Baumwollstoff, seit Ende der 1960er von Senufo-Künstlern um Korhogo (Elfenbeinküste) mit dunklen Schlammfarben-Silhouetten von Maskenfiguren, Vögeln und Fischen bemalt.
styles.short_en: Handspun cotton cloth painted by Senufo artists around Korhogo, Côte d'Ivoire, since the late 1960s, with dark mud-dye silhouettes of masked figures, birds and fish.
styles.era_de: seit Ende der 1960er, Norden der Elfenbeinküste
styles.era_en: Since the late 1960s, northern Côte d'Ivoire
styles.sensitivity_de: Manche Motive beziehen sich auf den Poro-Bund der Senufo und seine Masken; sakrale Inhalte nicht verfälschen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Some motifs relate to the Senufo Poro society and its masks; do not misrepresent sacred content.

styles.era_origin: Mbuti people, Ituri Forest, DR Congo; painted by women.
visual_markers: freehand black and dark-red plant-dye lines
patterns that interrupt and switch abruptly ('break patterning')
styles.prompt_fragment: as Mbuti barkcloth painting: freehand black and dark-red plant-dye lines applied with twigs and fingertips on soft pounded beige bark cloth, grids, stars, nets, dotted lines and zigzags that wander, interrupt themselves and switch pattern abruptly, large empty voids, asymmetric musical rhythm, fibrous bark texture with holes and patches
styles.avoid: Avoid regular stencilled tapa grids and generic doodle patterns; keep improvised break patterning.
styles.feasibility_note: Model tends to regularise the patterns.
styles.sensitivity_note: Often marketed under the derogatory 'Pygmy' label; credit Mbuti women artists.
styles.short_de: Geklopfter Rindenbaststoff, von Mbuti-Frauen im Ituri-Wald (DR Kongo) freihändig bemalt, mit schwarzen und roten Linien, Rastern und Sternen, die abrupt abbrechen.
styles.short_en: Pounded bark cloth painted freehand by Mbuti women of the Ituri Forest (DR Congo), with black and red lines, grids and stars that break off abruptly.
markers_de: freihändige Linien in Schwarz und Dunkelrot aus Pflanzenfarbe
markers_en: freehand black and dark-red plant-dye lines
patterns that break off and switch abruptly
styles.sensitivity_de: Wird oft unter dem abwertenden Etikett ‚Pygmäen‘ vermarktet; die Mbuti-Frauen als Künstlerinnen nennen.
styles.sensitivity_en: Often marketed under the derogatory label 'Pygmy'; credit Mbuti women as the artists.

styles.era_origin: Ethiopia and Eritrea, 18th-20th century, made by debtera scribes.
visual_markers: columns of Ge'ez script in black and red
frontal faces with huge staring eyes
styles.prompt_fragment: as an Ethiopian protective healing scroll: long narrow strip of cream parchment with columns of Ge'ez-style script in black and red, interrupted by square talismanic panels of frontal faces with huge staring eyes, eight-pointed stars, interlaced nets, crosses and winged figures in red, yellow, green and black, rough hand-cut edges
styles.avoid: Avoid the softer Ethiopian Orthodox church painting look; keep talismanic geometry, staring eyes and narrow scroll format.
styles.feasibility_note: Format and eyes work; Ge'ez script garbled.
styles.sensitivity_note: Protective religious objects; avoid occult exoticisation and misuse of prayer texts.
styles.short_de: Langer, schmaler Pergamentstreifen mit Ge'ez-Gebeten und Talisman-Feldern voller starrender Augen, Sterne und Kreuze, von äthiopischen Debtera-Schreibern gefertigt, vor allem im 18.–20. Jahrhundert.
styles.short_en: Long narrow parchment strip with Ge'ez prayers and talismanic panels of staring eyes, stars and crosses, made by Ethiopian debtera scribes, mainly 18th–20th century.
markers_de: frontale Gesichter mit großen starrenden Augen
markers_en: columns of Ge'ez script in black and red

styles.sensitivity_de: Religiöse Schutzobjekte; okkulte Exotisierung und Missbrauch der Gebetstexte vermeiden.
styles.sensitivity_en: Protective religious objects; avoid occult exoticism and misuse of prayer texts.

styles.era_origin: Swahili coast of East Africa, from the late 19th century.
visual_markers: rectangular cloth with wide patterned border
two or three intense flat colours
styles.prompt_fragment: as an East African kanga print: rectangular cotton cloth with a wide patterned border framing a bold central medallion, a line of capital-letter Swahili proverb text along one side, two or three intense flat colours such as black, red and yellow, repeated graphic motifs, screen-printed fabric with slight colour misregistration
styles.avoid: Avoid the allover West African wax-print look; keep the border-centre-inscription structure.
styles.feasibility_note: Layout works; Swahili text is unreliable.
styles.sensitivity_note: Proverbs carry social messages; garbled or invented Swahili may offend.

styles.era_origin: Makonde carvers of Tanzania and Mozambique; modern styles from the 1950s.
visual_markers: surreal distortions against rough chisel marks
styles.prompt_fragment: carved in the modern Makonde style from African blackwood: dense polished dark heartwood with pale sapwood streaks, figures and creatures elongated, twisted and intertwined into an open-work column, exaggerated surreal distortions, smooth glossy surfaces against rough chisel marks, dramatic side light
styles.avoid: Avoid generic tribal souvenir carvings; keep the intertwined surreal composition and contrasting woods.
styles.feasibility_note: Wood carving renders convincingly.
styles.sensitivity_note: Shetani depict spirits; blackwood is a near-threatened species; avoid 'tribal' stereotypes.

styles.era_de: traditionell, Mittlerer und Hoher Atlas, Marokko

styles.era_origin: Mesoamerica (Mexica and colonial feather mosaics of the 16th century); also Hawaii.

colour patches shimmering with angle of light

styles.sensitivity_note: Sacred and royal Indigenous art; avoid 'Aztec headdress' stereotypes; Hawaiian featherwork is chiefly regalia.

styles.era_origin: Sarhua, Ayacucho, Peru, since at least the 19th century; urban workshops in Lima since the 1970s.
visual_markers: bright pinks, blues, greens, ochres outlined in black
styles.prompt_fragment: as a Tablas de Sarhua painting: long narrow wooden board primed with chalky white lime, flat naive figures in Andean dress, animals and houses in neat stacked registers, bright pinks, blues, greens and ochres outlined in black, a handwritten Spanish caption along the bottom, sun and saint motifs, sparse plain ground

styles.sensitivity_note: Some boards narrate the violence of Peru's 1980s-90s conflict; Quechua community heritage.

styles.era_origin: Santa Fe Indian School Studio from 1932, with roots in the Kiowa Six of the 1920s; dominant into the 1960s.
visual_markers: fine-line detail in clothing and feathers
muted earth tones with turquoise and red
styles.prompt_fragment: as Native American Studio-style painting of the 1930s-50s: flat opaque watercolour figures and animals floating on blank paper without horizon or background, crisp outlines, delicate fine-line detail in clothing and feathers, decorative symmetry, muted earth tones accented with turquoise and red, calm stylised poses
styles.avoid: Avoid Plains ledger drawing on lined paper and Wild West illustration; keep the blank-background flat style.
styles.feasibility_note: Flat figures on blank ground render reliably.
styles.sensitivity_note: Ceremonial dress and dances are culturally sensitive; avoid fake 'Native' branding (US Indian Arts and Crafts Act); treat as a historic style.

styles.short_en: Flat opaque watercolours of figures and animals on blank paper, with crisp outlines and fine detail, taught at the Santa Fe Indian School Studio from 1932.
markers_de: feine Linien in Kleidung und Federn
gedämpfte Erdtöne mit Türkis und Rot
markers_en: fine-line detail in dress and feathers
muted earth tones with turquoise and red
styles.sensitivity_de: Zeremonielle Kleidung und Tänze sind sensibel; Ergebnisse nie als indigene Arbeit ausgeben (US Indian Arts and Crafts Act); als historischen Stil behandeln.
styles.sensitivity_en: Ceremonial dress and dances are sensitive; never present output as Native-made (US Indian Arts and Crafts Act); treat it as a historical style.

styles.era_origin: Sepik region, Papua New Guinea; traditional and ongoing.
visual_markers: red ochre, white lime, black charcoal, yellow
curvilinear stylised faces with large concentric eyes
styles.prompt_fragment: as Sepik River ceremonial painting: flat panels of dried sago palm bark painted in red ochre, white lime, black charcoal and yellow, bold curvilinear stylised faces with large concentric eyes, spirals, hook and leaf forms filling the surface, fibrous texture and cracking pigment, arranged in rows like a ceremonial house ceiling
styles.avoid: Avoid Aboriginal dot painting and generic tribal-mask clipart; keep the sago panels and curvilinear face motifs.
styles.feasibility_note: Pigment texture works; specific motif vocabulary is approximate.
styles.sensitivity_note: Spirit-house imagery is sacred and clan-owned; avoid commercial reuse of clan designs.
styles.verdict_reason: Confirmed. The Kwoma and Abelam paintings belong to the ceremonial house (korob, haus tambaran), which only initiated men may enter, and the motifs are clan property. That is the same pattern as Aboriginal painting. The material correction is right: the panels are sago-palm spathe (leaf sheath), not bark, and the entry's own alias already says 'sago spathe painting'. My web check of museum records failed (rate limit and missing pages), so the material point rests on standard ethnographic knowledge.
styles.short_de: Geschwungene Gesichter mit großen konzentrischen Augen, Spiralen und Haken in Ocker, Weiß, Schwarz und Gelb auf Tafeln aus Sagopalmen-Blattscheiden aus Zeremonialhäusern am Sepik, Papua-Neuguinea.
styles.short_en: Curvilinear faces with large concentric eyes, spirals and hooks in ochre, white, black and yellow on sago-palm spathe panels from ceremonial houses in Papua New Guinea.
styles.era_en: Traditional and ongoing, Sepik region, Papua New Guinea
markers_de: Pigmente in Rotocker, Kalkweiß, Schwarz und Gelb
geschwungene Gesichter mit großen konzentrischen Augen
markers_en: red ochre, white lime, black and yellow pigments
curvilinear faces with large concentric eyes
styles.sensitivity_de: Die Malereien der Zeremonialhäuser zeigen clangebundene Geister- und Ahnenmotive aus zugangsbeschränkten Männerhäusern; daher kein Prompt.
styles.sensitivity_en: Ceremonial-house paintings show clan-owned spirit and ancestor designs from restricted men's houses, so no prompt is offered.

styles.era_origin: Polynesia, centuries-old practice, revived since the 1980s.
visual_markers: rows of triangles, spearheads, waves, shark teeth
composition following the curvature of the form
styles.prompt_fragment: in Polynesian tatau ornament: dense black geometric bands assembled from rows of small triangles, spearheads, waves, shell and shark-tooth motifs, fine parallel line fills, carefully balanced solid and open areas, composition following the curvature of the form, crisp hand-tapped edges, solely black on skin tone or bark-cloth ground
styles.avoid: Avoid flame-like 1990s neo-tribal clichés; keep the Polynesian geometric motif vocabulary.
styles.feasibility_note: Geometric bands render; authentic motif grammar is approximate.
styles.sensitivity_note: High: tatau encodes genealogy and rank; Māori tā moko must not be copied; use only as broad reference, never replicate personal designs.
styles.verdict_reason: Confirmed, but on better grounds than the comparison with tā moko. The Samoan pe'a and malu are described as a sacred covenant between the wearer, the tattooist and the ancestral spirits (atua). The master tattooist's role is held through hereditary titles in two families, Sa Su'a and Sa Tulou'ena, and non-Samoans rarely receive it (Wikipedia: Pe'a). Pacific communities have also pushed back on commercial copies, for example Nike's 2013 'Pro Tattoo Tech' leggings, which were withdrawn (from memory, not checked again here). The entry's portrait and people subjects would put tatau on bodies and faces. That makes it sacred, community-held material.
styles.short_de: Dichte schwarze geometrische Bänder aus Dreiecken, Wellen und Haizahnmotiven, die den Körperformen folgen, aus den Tätowiertraditionen Samoas, der Marquesas und anderer polynesischer Inseln.
styles.short_en: Dense black geometric bands of triangles, waves and shark-tooth motifs following the body's curves, from the tattoo traditions of Samoa, the Marquesas and other Polynesian islands.
styles.era_en: Centuries old, Polynesia; revived since the 1980s
markers_de: Reihen aus Dreiecken, Speerspitzen, Wellen, Haizähnen
markers_en: rows of triangles, spearheads, waves, shark teeth
styles.sensitivity_de: Tatau verschlüsselt Abstammung, Rang und Identität und ist lebendige sakrale Praxis; wie das Tā Moko der Māori sollte es nicht per Prompt nachgebildet werden.
styles.sensitivity_en: Tatau encodes genealogy, rank and identity and is a living sacred practice; like Māori tā moko, it should not be reproduced from a prompt.

white-trunked ghost gums with crisp contours

bold two-tone wave and border patterns

styles.era_origin: Studio and cinema lighting technique, popularised in 1980s-90s commercial, sports and car advertising with twin strip-light kickers.
visual_markers: near-black frame with the subject defined only by thin bright contour lines
two opposing kicker lights from behind left and right
front of the subject falls into shadow
crisp specular edges on hair, shoulders or product edges
styles.prompt_fragment: photographed in a black studio with only two strip softboxes behind the subject at left and right, thin bright rim highlights tracing every contour while the front falls into near-total shadow, pure black background, crisp specular edges, no front fill, high contrast, medium-format clarity
styles.avoid: Avoid adding a frontal key light or teal-orange glow, which turns it back into a generic dramatic portrait or a Rembrandt low-key.
styles.feasibility_note: Rim light renders reliably; the model sometimes adds unwanted fill on faces, so state 'no front light'.
styles.short_de: Studiolicht, bei dem zwei Kantenlichter von hinten nur dünne helle Konturen vor reinem Schwarz zeichnen und die Vorderseite dunkel bleibt; Standard in Sport-, Fitness- und Produktwerbung.
styles.short_en: Studio lighting where two kicker lights behind the subject trace thin bright contours against pure black, leaving the front dark; a staple of sports, fitness and product advertising.

styles.era_en: Studio and film lighting since the 1930s; twin-strip variant in advertising from the 1990s

markers_en: near-black frame, subject drawn by thin bright contours
two opposing kicker lights from behind
front of the subject in shadow

styles.era_origin: American fashion and portrait studios of the 1950s-60s, later the template for documentary portraits against white paper.
visual_markers: subject isolated on seamless white paper with no horizon or floor line
full tonal range and crisp detail on the subject despite the white ground
flat frontal soft light with minimal shadow
often black-and-white with a filed black negative border
deadpan direct gaze or angular dynamic pose
styles.prompt_fragment: shot against seamless white studio paper with no visible floor line, flat frontal soft daylight, subject rendered with full tonal range and crisp detail, stark isolation, fine-grain black-and-white large-format negative printed with a rough filed black border, deadpan direct gaze or angular pose
styles.avoid: Avoid dreamy overexposed pastel glow (that is high-key) and e-commerce cutout perfection; keep the negative border and tonal depth.
styles.feasibility_note: Clean white background is easy; the filed negative border appears when explicitly requested.
styles.sensitivity_note: Strongly associated with a few famous mid-century photographers; describe the look, never name them.
styles.short_de: Porträts vor nahtlosem weißem Papier mit flachem, weichem Licht und voller Tonwertzeichnung, oft schwarzweiß mit schwarzem Negativrand; amerikanische Studios ab den 1950ern.
styles.short_en: Portraits isolated on seamless white paper with flat soft light and full tonal detail, often black-and-white with a black negative border; American studios from the 1950s.
